5.244.s:
.. paijavana uvāca .. ..
śāligrāmaśilāyāṃ ca jagadādiḥ sanātanaḥ ..
kathaṃ pāṣāṇatāṃ prāpto gaṇḍakyāṃ tacca me vada ..
tvatprasādena viprarṣe harau bhaktirdṛḍhā bhavet ..
bhavaṃtastīrtharūpā hi darśanātpāpahāriṇaḥ .. 2 ..
5.244.d:
.. पैजवन उवाच .. ..
शालिग्रामशिलायां च जगदादिः सनातनः ..
कथं पाषाणतां प्राप्तो गण्डक्यां तच्च मे वद ..
त्वत्प्रसादेन विप्रर्षे हरौ भक्तिर्दृढा भवेत् ..
भवंतस्तीर्थरूपा हि दर्शनात्पापहारिणः .. 2 ..
5.244.m: Paijavana said: / In the śāligrāma stone, how did the eternal origin of the world / attain the state of stone in the Gaṇḍakī river? Tell me that. / By your favor, O brahmin-seer, let devotion to Hari become firm. / For your honors are the embodiment of sacred fords, removing sins merely by darśana.

5.244.s:
tīrthāmṛtāvagāhena yathā pavitratā nṛṇām ..
bhavadvākyāmṛtājjātā tathā mama na saṃśayaḥ .. 3 ..
5.244.d:
तीर्थामृतावगाहेन यथा पवित्रता नृणाम् ..
भवद्वाक्यामृताज्जाता तथा मम न संशयः .. 3 ..
5.244.m: Just as purity arises for men by immersing in the nectar of sacred fords, / so it has arisen for me from the nectar of your speech; of this there is no doubt.

5.244.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
itihāsastvayaṃ puṇyaḥ purāṇeṣu ca paṭhyate ..
yathā sa eva bhagavāñchāligrāmatvamāgataḥ .. 4 ..
5.244.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
इतिहासस्त्वयं पुण्यः पुराणेषु च पठ्यते ..
यथा स एव भगवाञ्छालिग्रामत्वमागतः .. 4 ..
5.244.m: Gālava said: / This sacred legend is recited in the Purāṇas, / telling how that very Lord came to the state of a śāligrāma,

5.244.s:
maheśvaraśca liṃgatvaṃ kathaye'haṃ tavā'nagha ..
pūrvaṃ prajāpatirdakṣo brahmaṇoṃ'guṣṭha saṃbhavaḥ .. 5 ..'
5.244.d:
महेश्वरश्च लिंगत्वं कथयेऽहं तवाऽनघ ..
पूर्वं प्रजापतिर्दक्षो ब्रह्मणोंऽगुष्ठ संभवः .. 5 ..'
5.244.m: and how Maheśvara became a liṅga, I shall tell you, O sinless one. / Formerly, the progenitor Dakṣa, who arose from the thumb of Brahmā—

5.244.s:
tasyāsīdduhitā sādhvī satīnāmnī sulakṣaṇā ..
hareṇoḍhā vidhijñena vedoktavidhinā tataḥ .. 6 ..
5.244.d:
तस्यासीद्दुहिता साध्वी सतीनाम्नी सुलक्षणा ..
हरेणोढा विधिज्ञेन वेदोक्तविधिना ततः .. 6 ..
5.244.m: had a virtuous daughter named Satī, endowed with auspicious marks. / She was then wed by Hara, the knower of ordinances, according to the rite prescribed by the Vedas.

5.244.s:
sa cakāra mahāyajñe haradveṣaṃ vimūḍhadhīḥ ..
tena dveṣeṇa mahatā satī prakupitā bhṛśam .. 7 ..
5.244.d:
स चकार महायज्ञे हरद्वेषं विमूढधीः ..
तेन द्वेषेण महता सती प्रकुपिता भृशम् .. 7 ..
5.244.m: At a great sacrifice, he, foolish in mind, harbored hatred toward Hara. / Because of that great hatred, Satī became exceedingly enraged.

5.244.s:
yajñavedyāṃ samāgamya vahnidhāraṇayā tadā ..
prāṇāyāmaparā bhūtvā dehotsargaṃ cakāra sā .. 8 ..
5.244.d:
यज्ञवेद्यां समागम्य वह्निधारणया तदा ..
प्राणायामपरा भूत्वा देहोत्सर्गं चकार सा .. 8 ..
5.244.m: Having approached the sacrificial altar, then, by meditating upon the fire / and devoting herself to breath control, she cast off her body.

5.244.s:
pitṛbhāgaṃ parityajya svabhāgena yutā satī ..
manasā dhyānamagamacchītalaṃ ca himālayam .. 9 ..
5.244.d:
पितृभागं परित्यज्य स्वभागेन युता सती ..
मनसा ध्यानमगमच्छीतलं च हिमालयम् .. 9 ..
5.244.m: Abandoning the share inherited from her father, endowed with her own divine portion, Satī / entered into mental meditation upon the cool Himālaya.

5.244.s:
yatrayatra mano yāti svakarmavaśagaṃ mṛtau ..
avatārastatratatra jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 6.245.10 ..
5.244.d:
यत्रयत्र मनो याति स्वकर्मवशगं मृतौ ..
अवतारस्तत्रतत्र जायते नात्र संशयः .. 6.245.10 ..
5.244.m: Wherever the mind goes at death, governed by one's own actions, / there indeed one's rebirth takes place; of this there is no doubt.

5.244.s:
dahyamānā hi sā devī himālayasutā'bhavat ..
tatra sā pārvatī bhūtvā tapa ugraṃ samāśritā .. 11 ..
5.244.d:
दह्यमाना हि सा देवी हिमालयसुताऽभवत् ..
तत्र सा पार्वती भूत्वा तप उग्रं समाश्रिता .. 11 ..
5.244.m: Indeed, having consumed herself, that goddess became the daughter of Himālaya. / There, having become Pārvatī, she undertook severe austerity,

5.244.s:
śivabhaktiratā nityaṃ haravrataparāyaṇā ..
śṛṃge himavataḥ putrī mano nyasya maheśvare .. .. 12 ..
5.244.d:
शिवभक्तिरता नित्यं हरव्रतपरायणा ..
शृंगे हिमवतः पुत्री मनो न्यस्य महेश्वरे .. .. 12 ..
5.244.m: constantly delighting in devotion to Śiva, dedicated to the observances of Hara, / that daughter [of Himavat], fixing her mind on Maheśvara on a peak of Himavat.

5.244.s:
tato varṣasahasrāṃte bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ ..
athājagāma taṃ deśaṃ viprarūpo maheśvaraḥ .. 13 ..
5.244.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रांते भगवान्भूतभावनः ..
अथाजगाम तं देशं विप्ररूपो महेश्वरः .. 13 ..
5.244.m: Then, at the end of a thousand years, the Lord, the author of all beings, / Maheśvara, came to that place in the form of a brahmin.

5.244.s:
tāṃ jñātvā tapasā śuddhāṃ karmabhāvaiḥ parīkṣitaiḥ ..
tato divyavapurbhūtvā kare jagrāha pārvatīm .. 14 ..
5.244.d:
तां ज्ञात्वा तपसा शुद्धां कर्मभावैः परीक्षितैः ..
ततो दिव्यवपुर्भूत्वा करे जग्राह पार्वतीम् .. 14 ..
5.244.m: Knowing her to be purified by austerity through tested deeds and dispositions, / he then assumed a divine form and took Pārvatī by the hand.

5.244.s:
tapasā nirjitaścāsmi karavāṇi ca kiṃ priyam ..
tataḥ prāha maheśānaṃ pramāṇaṃ me pitā guruḥ . .. 15 ..
5.244.d:
तपसा निर्जितश्चास्मि करवाणि च किं प्रियम् ..
ततः प्राह महेशानं प्रमाणं मे पिता गुरुः . .. 15 ..
5.244.m: [He said:] 'I have been conquered by your austerity; what pleasant deed may I do for you?' / Then she said to Maheśāna: 'My father, my guru, is the authority.'

5.244.s:
saptarṣīnsa tathoktastu preṣayāmāsa śaṃkaraḥ ..
te tatra gatvā samayaṃ vaktuṃ himavatā saha .. 16 ..
5.244.d:
सप्तर्षीन्स तथोक्तस्तु प्रेषयामास शंकरः ..
ते तत्र गत्वा समयं वक्तुं हिमवता सह .. 16 ..
5.244.m: Having been told thus, Śaṃkara sent the seven seers. / They, having gone there, spoke of the alliance with Himavat.

5.244.s:
nivedya ca maheśānaṃ preṣitā munayo yayuḥ .
tato lagnadine devā mahendrādaya īśvaram .. 17 ..
5.244.d:
निवेद्य च महेशानं प्रेषिता मुनयो ययुः .
ततो लग्नदिने देवा महेन्द्रादय ईश्वरम् .. 17 ..
5.244.m: Having announced it to Maheśāna, the seers who had been sent departed. / Then, on the auspicious day, the gods, Mahendra and the others, approached Īśvara;

5.244.s:
brahmaviṣṇupurogāśca purodhāyāgnimāyayuḥ ..
yogasiddhā samāyāṃtaṃ varaveṣaṃ vṛṣadhvajam . 18 .
5.244.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुपुरोगाश्च पुरोधायाग्निमाययुः ..
योगसिद्धा समायांतं वरवेषं वृषध्वजम् . 18 .
5.244.m: and led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, placing the sacred fire in front, they arrived. / The seers perfected in yoga [saw] the bull-bannered [god] arriving in the attire of a bridegroom.

5.244.s:
himavānpūjayāmāsa madhuparkādikaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
upacārairmudā yukto mānayankṛtakṛtyatām .. 19 ..
5.244.d:
हिमवान्पूजयामास मधुपर्कादिकैः शुभैः ..
उपचारैर्मुदा युक्तो मानयन्कृतकृत्यताम् .. 19 ..
5.244.m: Himavat worshiped him with auspicious offerings of madhuparka and the like; / filled with joy through proper attentions, he considered his purpose accomplished.

5.244.s:
vedoktena vidhānena tāṃ kanyāṃ samayojayat ..
pāṇigraheṇa vidhinā dvijātigaṇasaṃvṛtaḥ .. 6.245.20 ..
5.244.d:
वेदोक्तेन विधानेन तां कन्यां समयोजयत् ..
पाणिग्रहेण विधिना द्विजातिगणसंवृतः .. 6.245.20 ..
5.244.m: Surrounded by a host of the twice-born, in accordance with the rite prescribed in the Vedas, / he united that maiden [with him] through the ceremony of grasping the hand.

5.244.s:
vahniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya girīśastadanantaram ..
dānakāle ca gotrādi pṛṣṭo lajjāparo hara ..21..
5.244.d:
वह्निं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य गिरीशस्तदनन्तरम् ..
दानकाले च गोत्रादि पृष्टो लज्जापरो हर ..21..
5.244.m: Having circumambulated the fire, thereafter the Lord of the Mountain [questioned him]; / and when asked about his lineage and family at the time of the maiden-giving, Hara was overcome with modesty.

5.244.s:
brahmaṇo vacanāttena vidhiśeṣo'vaśeṣitaḥ..
caruprāśanakāle tu paṃcavaktraprakāśakṛt..22..
5.244.d:
ब्रह्मणो वचनात्तेन विधिशेषोऽवशेषितः..
चरुप्राशनकाले तु पंचवक्त्रप्रकाशकृत्..22..
5.244.m: By the word of Brahmā, the remainder of the rite was completed by him. / But at the time of consuming the sacrificial boiled rice, he revealed five faces.

5.244.s:
sahitaḥ sakalairdevaiḥ kutūhalaparāyaṇaḥ..
girijārthaṃ samāyukto varaḥ so'pi maheśvaraḥ..23..
5.244.d:
सहितः सकलैर्देवैः कुतूहलपरायणः..
गिरिजार्थं समायुक्तो वरः सोऽपि महेश्वरः..23..
5.244.m: Accompanied by all the gods, devoted to wonder, / united for the sake of the mountain's daughter was that bridegroom, Maheśvara.

5.244.s:
navakoṭimukhāṃ dṛṣṭvā sāṭṭahāso jano'bhavat..
vaidikī śrutirityuktā śiva tvaṃ sthiratāṃ vraja..24..
5.244.d:
नवकोटिमुखां दृष्ट्वा साट्टहासो जनोऽभवत्..
वैदिकी श्रुतिरित्युक्ता शिव त्वं स्थिरतां व्रज..24..
5.244.m: Seeing ninety million faces, the people burst into loud laughter. / 'This is stated by Vedic revelation: O Śiva, attain steadiness!'

5.244.s:
lajjitā sā parityāgaṃ nākarotpaṃcajanmasu ..
bharttāramasitāpāṃgī haramevābhyagacchata .. 25 ..
5.244.d:
लज्जिता सा परित्यागं नाकरोत्पंचजन्मसु ..
भर्त्तारमसितापांगी हरमेवाभ्यगच्छत .. 25 ..
5.244.m: Though embarrassed, she did not abandon him through five lifetimes; / the dark-eyed lady approached none other than Hara as her husband.

5.244.s:
devānāṃ parvatānāṃ ca prahṛṣṭaṃ sakalaṃ kulam ..
tato vivāhe saṃpūrṇe haro'gātkautukaukasi .. 26 ..
5.244.d:
देवानां पर्वतानां च प्रहृष्टं सकलं कुलम् ..
ततो विवाहे संपूर्णे हरोऽगात्कौतुकौकसि .. 26 ..
5.244.m: The entire family of gods and of mountains rejoiced. / Then, the wedding being completed, Hara went to the bridal chamber.

5.244.s:
gaṇānāṃ cāpi sānnidhye sā nāmarṣayadaṃbikā ..
pāribarhaṃ tato dattvā śailena sa visarjitaḥ .. 27 ..
5.244.d:
गणानां चापि सान्निध्ये सा नामर्षयदंबिका ..
पारिबर्हं ततो दत्त्वा शैलेन स विसर्जितः .. 27 ..
5.244.m: And in the presence of the gaṇas, Ambikā did not tolerate [their presence]. / Then, having given the dowry, he was sent off by the mountain.

5.244.s:
mānitaḥ satkṛtaścāpi mandarācalamabhyagāt..
viśvakarmā tatastasya kṣaṇena maṇimadgṛham .. 28 ..
5.244.d:
मानितः सत्कृतश्चापि मन्दराचलमभ्यगात्..
विश्वकर्मा ततस्तस्य क्षणेन मणिमद्गृहम् .. 28 ..
5.244.m: Respected and honored, he went to Mount Mandara. / Then, in an instant, Viśvakarman constructed a jewel-studded house for him,

5.244.s:
nirmame devadevasya svecchāvarddhiṣṇumaṃdiram ..
sarvarddhimatpraśastābhaṃ maṇividrumabhūṣitam .. 29 ..
5.244.d:
निर्ममे देवदेवस्य स्वेच्छावर्द्धिष्णुमंदिरम् ..
सर्वर्द्धिमत्प्रशस्ताभं मणिविद्रुमभूषितम् .. 29 ..
5.244.m: a palace for the God of gods that expanded at his will, / possessing all prosperity, of splendid luster, adorned with gems and corals,

5.244.s:
sthūṇāsahasrasaṃyuktaṃ maṇivedimanoharam ..
gaṇā naṃdiprabhṛtayo yasya dvāri samāśritāḥ .. 6.245.30 ..
5.244.d:
स्थूणासहस्रसंयुक्तं मणिवेदिमनोहरम् ..
गणा नंदिप्रभृतयो यस्य द्वारि समाश्रिताः .. 6.245.30 ..
5.244.m: furnished with a thousand pillars, captivating with a jeweled platform, / at the door of which the gaṇas, Nandin and others, took their station,

5.244.s:
trinetrāḥ śūlahastāśca babhuḥ śaṃkararūpiṇaḥ ..
vāṭikā asya paritaḥ pārijātāḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 31 ..
5.244.d:
त्रिनेत्राः शूलहस्ताश्च बभुः शंकररूपिणः ..
वाटिका अस्य परितः पारिजाताः सहस्रशः .. 31 ..
5.244.m: three-eyed, holding tridents in hand, shining in the form of Śaṃkara. / All around it were gardens containing thousands of pārijāta trees;

5.244.s:
kāmadhenurmaṇirdivyo yasya dvāri samāśritau ..
tasminmanoharatare kāmavṛddhikare gṛhe .. 32 ..
5.244.d:
कामधेनुर्मणिर्दिव्यो यस्य द्वारि समाश्रितौ ..
तस्मिन्मनोहरतरे कामवृद्धिकरे गृहे .. 32 ..
5.244.m: at its door Kāmadhenu and the celestial jewel were situated. / In that most delightful house which augmented desire,

5.244.s:
pārvatyā vasataḥ sārddhaṃ kāmo dṛṣṭipathaṃ yayau ..
vāyurūpaḥ śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmaḥ provāca śaṃkaram .. 33 ..
5.244.d:
पार्वत्या वसतः सार्द्धं कामो दृष्टिपथं ययौ ..
वायुरूपः शिवं दृष्ट्वा कामः प्रोवाच शंकरम् .. 33 ..
5.244.m: as he dwelt together with Pārvatī, Kāma came into the range of his sight. / Assuming the form of wind and seeing Śiva, Kāma spoke to Śaṃkara:

5.244.s:
namaste sarvarūpāya namaste vṛṣabhadhvaja ..
namaste gaṇanāthāya pāhi nātha namo'stu te ..34..
5.244.d:
नमस्ते सर्वरूपाय नमस्ते वृषभध्वज ..
नमस्ते गणनाथाय पाहि नाथ नमोऽस्तु ते ..34..
5.244.m: 'Salutations to you whose form is everything! Salutations to you who have the bull on your banner! / Salutations to you, the lord of the gaṇas! Protect me, O Lord, salutations to you!

5.244.s:
tvayā virahitaṃ lokaṃ śavavatspṛśate mahī ..
na tvayā rahitaṃ kiñci ddṛśyate sacarācare .. 35 ..
5.244.d:
त्वया विरहितं लोकं शववत्स्पृशते मही ..
न त्वया रहितं किञ्चि द्दृश्यते सचराचरे .. 35 ..
5.244.m: Bereft of you, the earth touches the world like a corpse. / Nothing in the moving and unmoving creation is seen devoid of you.

5.244.s:
tvaṃ goptā tvaṃ vidhātā ca lokasaṃhārakārakaḥ ..
kṛpāṃ kuru mahādeva dehadānaṃ prayaccha me .. 36 ..
5.244.d:
त्वं गोप्ता त्वं विधाता च लोकसंहारकारकः ..
कृपां कुरु महादेव देहदानं प्रयच्छ मे .. 36 ..
5.244.m: You are the protector, you are the creator, and the cause of the dissolution of the worlds. / Show mercy, O Mahādeva, and grant me the gift of a body!'

5.244.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. .. ..
yanmayā tvaṃ purā dagdhaḥ parvate purato'nagha ..
tasyā eva samīpe tvaṃ punarbhava svadehavān .. 37 ..
5.244.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. .. ..
यन्मया त्वं पुरा दग्धः पर्वते पुरतोऽनघ ..
तस्या एव समीपे त्वं पुनर्भव स्वदेहवान् .. 37 ..
5.244.m: Īśvara said: / 'Because you were burned by me of old upon the mountain in her presence, O sinless one, / you shall become embodied again in her presence alone.'

5.244.s:
evamuktastataḥ kāmaḥ svaśarīramupāgataḥ ..
vavaṃde caraṇau śūdra vinayāvanato'bhavat .. 38 ..
5.244.d:
एवमुक्तस्ततः कामः स्वशरीरमुपागतः ..
ववंदे चरणौ शूद्र विनयावनतोऽभवत् .. 38 ..
5.244.m: Having been spoken to thus, Kāma then regained his own body; / he bowed to his feet, O Śūdra, and bowed low with humility.

5.244.s:
tato nanāma caraṇau pārvatyāḥ saṃprahṛṣṭavān ..
labdhaprasādastu tayoḥ samīpādbhuvanatraye .. 39 ..
5.244.d:
ततो ननाम चरणौ पार्वत्याः संप्रहृष्टवान् ..
लब्धप्रसादस्तु तयोः समीपाद्भुवनत्रये .. 39 ..
5.244.m: Then, exceedingly delighted, he bowed to the feet of Pārvatī; / having obtained favor from the presence of the two of them throughout the three worlds,

5.244.s:
cacāra sumahātejā mahāmohabalānvitaḥ ..
puṣpadhanvā puṣpabāṇastvākuñcitaśiroruhaḥ .. 6.245.40 ..
5.244.d:
चचार सुमहातेजा महामोहबलान्वितः ..
पुष्पधन्वा पुष्पबाणस्त्वाकुञ्चितशिरोरुहः .. 6.245.40 ..
5.244.m: Possessing great splendor and endowed with the power of great infatuation, the god with the flower-bow, flower-arrows, and curled hair roamed about.

5.244.s:
sadā ghūrṇitanetraśca tayordehamupāviśat ..
divyāsavairdivyagaṃdhairvastramālyādibhistathā .. 41 ..
5.244.d:
सदा घूर्णितनेत्रश्च तयोर्देहमुपाविशत् ..
दिव्यासवैर्दिव्यगंधैर्वस्त्रमाल्यादिभिस्तथा .. 41 ..
5.244.m: With his eyes ever rolling, he entered the bodies of the two. / With divine wines, divine fragrances, and likewise with garments, garlands, and other things,

5.244.s:
sakhyaḥ saṃbhogasamaye paricakruḥ samaṃtataḥ ..
evaṃ prakrīḍatastasya vatsarāṇāṃ śataṃ yayau .. 42 ..
5.244.d:
सख्यः संभोगसमये परिचक्रुः समंततः ..
एवं प्रक्रीडतस्तस्य वत्सराणां शतं ययौ .. 42 ..
5.244.m: female friends attended on them all around at the time of enjoyment. / While he was thus sporting, a hundred years passed by

5.244.s:
sāgramekā niśā yadvanmaithune saktacetasaḥ ..
etasminnaṃtare devāstārakapradrutā bhayāt ..
brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ stutvā taṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ .. 43 ..
5.244.d:
साग्रमेका निशा यद्वन्मैथुने सक्तचेतसः ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवास्तारकप्रद्रुता भयात् ..
ब्रह्माणं शरणं जग्मुः स्तुत्वा तं शरणं गताः .. 43 ..
5.244.m: just like a single night to him whose mind was intent on sexual union. / In the meantime, the gods, fleeing out of fear of Tāraka,

5.244.s:
.. devā ucuḥ .. ..
tārako'sau mahāraudrastvayā dattavaraḥ purā .. 44 ..
5.244.d:
.. देवा उचुः .. ..
तारकोऽसौ महारौद्रस्त्वया दत्तवरः पुरा .. 44 ..
5.244.m: The gods said: / "That Tāraka is exceedingly fierce, to whom a boon was given by you in former times.

5.244.s:
vijitya tarasā śakraṃ bhuṃkte trailokyapūjitaḥ ..
vadhopāyo yathā tasya jāyate tvaṃ kuru svayam .. .. 45 ..
5.244.d:
विजित्य तरसा शक्रं भुंक्ते त्रैलोक्यपूजितः ..
वधोपायो यथा तस्य जायते त्वं कुरु स्वयम् .. .. 45 ..
5.244.m: Having swiftly conquered Indra, he enjoys [the realm], worshipped by the three worlds. / Do you yourself bring about the means by which his slaying may occur."

5.244.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
mayā dattavaraścāsau mayaivocchidyate nahi ..
svayaṃ saṃvardhya kaṭukaṃ chettuṃ ko'pi na cārhati .. 46 ..
5.244.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
मया दत्तवरश्चासौ मयैवोच्छिद्यते नहि ..
स्वयं संवर्ध्य कटुकं छेत्तुं कोऽपि न चार्हति .. 46 ..
5.244.m: Brahmā said: / "Since the boon was given to him by me, he cannot be destroyed by me. / Having raised a bitter [plant] oneself, no one ought to cut it down.

5.244.s:
tasmāttasya vadhopāyaṃ kathayāmi mahātmanaḥ ..
pārvatyāṃ yo maheśānātsūnurutpatsyate hi saḥ .. 47 ..
5.244.d:
तस्मात्तस्य वधोपायं कथयामि महात्मनः ..
पार्वत्यां यो महेशानात्सूनुरुत्पत्स्यते हि सः .. 47 ..
5.244.m: Therefore, I will tell you the means for the slaying of that mighty one. / The son who will be born from Maheśāna in Pārvatī—

5.244.s:
dinasaptakavānbhūtvā tārakaṃ sa haniṣyati ..
iti vākyaṃ tu te śrutvā maṃdaraṃ lokasuṃdaram.. 48 ..
5.244.d:
दिनसप्तकवान्भूत्वा तारकं स हनिष्यति ..
इति वाक्यं तु ते श्रुत्वा मंदरं लोकसुंदरम्.. 48 ..
5.244.m: having become seven days old, he will slay Tāraka." / Having heard this speech, [the gods went] to Mandara, beautiful to the world;

5.244.s: brahmalokātsamājagmuḥ pīḍitā daityadānavaiḥ .. 49 ..
5.244.d: ब्रह्मलोकात्समाजग्मुः पीडिता दैत्यदानवैः .. 49 ..
5.244.m: afflicted by Daityas and Dānavas, they came from the world of Brahmā.

5.244.s:
tatra naṃdiprabhṛtayo gaṇāḥ śūlabhṛtaḥ puraḥ ..
gṛhadvāre hyupā vṛtya tasthuḥ saṃyatacetasaḥ .. 6.245.50 ..
5.244.d:
तत्र नंदिप्रभृतयो गणाः शूलभृतः पुरः ..
गृहद्वारे ह्युपा वृत्य तस्थुः संयतचेतसः .. 6.245.50 ..
5.244.m: There, Nandī and the other gaṇas of the trident-bearing [lord] stood before the door of the house, / having turned back [the gods], with restrained minds.

5.244.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
devāśca duḥkhāturacetaso bhṛśaṃ hataprabhāstyaktagṛhāśrayākhilāḥ ..
saṃprāpya māsāṃścaturaḥ stapaḥ sthitā deve prasupte haratoṣaṇaṃ param .. 51 ..
5.244.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
देवाश्च दुःखातुरचेतसो भृशं हतप्रभास्त्यक्तगृहाश्रयाखिलाः ..
संप्राप्य मासांश्चतुरः स्तपः स्थिता देवे प्रसुप्ते हरतोषणं परम् .. 51 ..
5.244.m: The gods said: / "The gods, their minds deeply distressed by sorrow, their luster destroyed, all having abandoned their home and shelter, / having attained the four months [of Cāturmāsya], have stood in tapas while the god is asleep, pleasing Hara supreme."

5.244.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye paijavanopākhyāne tārakopadrutānāṃ devānāṃ śivadarśanārthaṃ maṃdarācalaṃpratigamanavarṇanaṃnāma pañcacatvāriṃśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 245 ..
5.244.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्याने तारकोपद्रुतानां देवानां शिवदर्शनार्थं मंदराचलंप्रतिगमनवर्णनंनाम पञ्चचत्वारिंशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 245 ..
5.244.m: Thus ends the two hundred and forty-fifth chapter, titled "Description of the Departure of the Gods Afflicted by Tāraka to Mount Mandara to See Śiva," in the Paijavana Episode, in the Greatness of the Cāturmāsya, in the Dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, in the Account of the Lord Resting on Śeṣa, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Sixth Section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Great Skanda Purāṇa of Eighty-One Thousand Verses.

5.245.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
śakrādayastu deveśā duḥkhasaṃtaptamānasāḥ .. ..
īśvarādarśanabhrāṃtamanaḥ karmeṃdriyā ratim .. 1 ..
5.245.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
शक्रादयस्तु देवेशा दुःखसंतप्तमानसाः .. ..
ईश्वरादर्शनभ्रांतमनः कर्मेंद्रिया रतिम् .. 1 ..
5.245.m: Gālava said: / "Śakra and the other lords of the gods, their minds burning with sorrow, / their sensory and motor organs agitated because they did not see Īśvara, found no delight.

5.245.s:
na prāpurlokanāthaṃ te kṛtvā yaḥ pratimākṛtim ..
tapasārādhayāmāsuḥ sarvabhūtahṛdisthitam .. 2 ..
5.245.d:
न प्रापुर्लोकनाथं ते कृत्वा यः प्रतिमाकृतिम् ..
तपसाराधयामासुः सर्वभूतहृदिस्थितम् .. 2 ..
5.245.m: They, having made an iconographic form, / worshipped with tapas the Lord of the World who dwells in the hearts of all beings:

5.245.s:
kapardaśirasaṃ devaṃ śūlahastaṃ pinākinam ..
kapālakhaṭvāṃgadharaṃ daśahastaṃ kirīṭinam.. 3 ..
5.245.d:
कपर्दशिरसं देवं शूलहस्तं पिनाकिनम् ..
कपालखट्वांगधरं दशहस्तं किरीटिनम्.. 3 ..
5.245.m: the god with matted hair, trident in hand, wielder of the Pināka, / holding a skull and a khaṭvāṅga, ten-armed, wearing a diadem;

5.245.s:
umāsahitamīśānaṃ paṃcavaktraṃ mahābhujam..
karpūragauradehābhaṃ sitabhūtivibhūṣitam.. .. 4 ..
5.245.d:
उमासहितमीशानं पंचवक्त्रं महाभुजम्..
कर्पूरगौरदेहाभं सितभूतिविभूषितम्.. .. 4 ..
5.245.m: Īśāna accompanied by Umā, five-faced, mighty-armed, / with a bodily luster white like camphor, adorned with white ashes;

5.245.s:
nāgayajñopavītena gajacarmasamanvitam ..
kṛṣṇasāratvacā cāpi kṛtaprāvaraṇaṃ vibhum .. 5 ..
5.245.d:
नागयज्ञोपवीतेन गजचर्मसमन्वितम् ..
कृष्णसारत्वचा चापि कृतप्रावरणं विभुम् .. 5 ..
5.245.m: accompanied by an elephant hide and a serpent as sacred thread, / and the all-pervading Lord wearing an upper garment made of the skin of a black buck.

5.245.s:
kṛtadhyānāḥ surāstatra vṛkṣādhāre samāśritāḥ ..
vratacaryāṃ samāśritya pracakrustapa uttamam .. 6 ..
5.245.d:
कृतध्यानाः सुरास्तत्र वृक्षाधारे समाश्रिताः ..
व्रतचर्यां समाश्रित्य प्रचक्रुस्तप उत्तमम् .. 6 ..
5.245.m: Having undertaken meditation there, taking shelter at the base of a tree, / the gods, resorting to the performance of a vow, performed supreme tapas.

5.245.s:
ṣaḍakṣareṇa maṃtreṇa śaivena vihitāḥ surāḥ ..
.. śūdra uvāca .. ..
vratacaryā tvayā yā sā proktā saṃjā yate katham .. 7 ..
5.245.d:
षडक्षरेण मंत्रेण शैवेन विहिताः सुराः ..
.. शूद्र उवाच .. ..
व्रतचर्या त्वया या सा प्रोक्ता संजा यते कथम् .. 7 ..
5.245.m: The gods were established by the six-syllabled Śaiva mantra." / The śūdra said: / "How is that performance of the vow, which was spoken of by you, performed?

5.245.s: brahmanvistarato brūhi na tṛpyete vaco'mṛtaiḥ .. 8 ..
5.245.d: ब्रह्मन्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि न तृप्येते वचोऽमृतैः .. 8 ..
5.245.m: Tell me in detail, O brahmin; [my ears] are not satiated with the nectar of your words."

5.245.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
japanbhasma ca khaṭvāṃgaṃ kapālaṃ sphāṭikaṃ tathā ..
ruṃḍamālāṃ paṃcavaktramarddhacaṃdraṃ ca mūrddhani .. 9 ..
5.245.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
जपन्भस्म च खट्वांगं कपालं स्फाटिकं तथा ..
रुंडमालां पंचवक्त्रमर्द्धचंद्रं च मूर्द्धनि .. 9 ..
5.245.m: Gālava said: / "Reciting [the mantra], [wearing] ashes, a khaṭvāṅga, a skull, crystal, / a garland of severed heads, [meditating on] the five-faced [god] with the half-moon on his crest;

5.245.s:
citrakṛttiparīdhānaṃ kaupīnakuṇḍaladvayam ..
ghaṃṭāyugmaṃ triśūlaṃ ca sūtraṃ caryāsvarūpakam .. 6.246.10 ..
5.245.d:
चित्रकृत्तिपरीधानं कौपीनकुण्डलद्वयम् ..
घंटायुग्मं त्रिशूलं च सूत्रं चर्यास्वरूपकम् .. 6.246.10 ..
5.245.m: wearing a variegated hide, a loincloth, a pair of earrings, / a pair of bells, a trident, and a sacred cord—this is the nature of the practice.

5.245.s:
amībhirlakṣaṇairlakṣyaṃ mayoktaṃ tava śūdraja ..
anena vidhinā sarve devā vahnipurogamāḥ .. 11 ..
5.245.d:
अमीभिर्लक्षणैर्लक्ष्यं मयोक्तं तव शूद्रज ..
अनेन विधिना सर्वे देवा वह्निपुरोगमाः .. 11 ..
5.245.m: The mark defined by these characteristics has been told to you by me, O son of a śūdra. / By this rule, all the gods headed by Fire

5.245.s:
sarva ārādhayāmāsuḥ sarvopāyairvarapradam ..
cāturmāsye ca saṃpūrṇe sapūrṇe kārtike'male .. 12 ..
5.245.d:
सर्व आराधयामासुः सर्वोपायैर्वरप्रदम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये च संपूर्णे सपूर्णे कार्तिकेऽमले .. 12 ..
5.245.m: worshipped the granter of boons by all means. / When the four months were completed, and the pure month of Kārtika was full,

5.245.s:
cīrṇavratānsurāndṛṣṭvā viśuddhāṃśca maheśvaraḥ ..
matiṃ teṣāṃ dadau tuṣṭo jīvātmā sarvabhūtadṛk .. 13 ..
5.245.d:
चीर्णव्रतान्सुरान्दृष्ट्वा विशुद्धांश्च महेश्वरः ..
मतिं तेषां ददौ तुष्टो जीवात्मा सर्वभूतदृक् .. 13 ..
5.245.m: seeing the gods who had performed the vow and were purified, Maheśvara, / pleased, the Living Self who beholds all beings, bestowed [favorable] intent on them.

5.245.s:
śatarudrīyajāpyena vidhānasahitena ca ..
dhyānena dīpadānena cāturmāsye tutoṣa saḥ .. 14 ..
5.245.d:
शतरुद्रीयजाप्येन विधानसहितेन च ..
ध्यानेन दीपदानेन चातुर्मास्ये तुतोष सः .. 14 ..
5.245.m: By the recitation of the Śatarudrīya accompanied by ritual, / by meditation, and by the gift of lamps in the Cāturmāsya, he was pleased.

5.245.s:
pūjanaiḥ ṣoḍaśavidhairyathā viṣṇostathā hare ..
kurvāṇānbhaktibhāvena jñātvā devānsamāgatān .. 15 ..
5.245.d:
पूजनैः षोडशविधैर्यथा विष्णोस्तथा हरे ..
कुर्वाणान्भक्तिभावेन ज्ञात्वा देवान्समागतान् .. 15 ..
5.245.m: With the sixteen kinds of worship, as done for Viṣṇu, so done for Hara— / knowing that the gods who arrived were performing it with a feeling of devotion,

5.245.s:
prahṛṣṭo bhagavānrudro dadau teṣāṃ śubhā matim ..
tataḥ saṃmaṃtrya te devā vahniṃ stutvā yathārthataḥ .. 16 ..
5.245.d:
प्रहृष्टो भगवान्रुद्रो ददौ तेषां शुभा मतिम् ..
ततः संमंत्र्य ते देवा वह्निं स्तुत्वा यथार्थतः .. 16 ..
5.245.m: the blessed Rudra, joyful, granted them a propitious mind. / Then the gods, having consulted together and praised Fire fittingly,

5.245.s:
prasannavadanaṃ cakruḥ kāryasādhanatatparam ..
karmasākṣī mahātejāḥ kṛtvā pārāvataṃ vapu .. 17 ..
5.245.d:
प्रसन्नवदनं चक्रुः कार्यसाधनतत्परम् ..
कर्मसाक्षी महातेजाः कृत्वा पारावतं वपु .. 17 ..
5.245.m: made his face gracious, intent on accomplishing their objective. / The witness of deeds, of great splendor, assuming the form of a pigeon,

5.245.s:
praviveśa tato madhye draṣṭuṃ devaṃ maheśvaram ..
cakāra gativikṣepaṃ guṃṭhanairavaguṃṭhanaiḥ ..18..
5.245.d:
प्रविवेश ततो मध्ये द्रष्टुं देवं महेश्वरम् ..
चकार गतिविक्षेपं गुंठनैरवगुंठनैः ..18..
5.245.m: then entered inside to see the god Maheśvara. / He made steps and strides with coverings and uncoverings,

5.245.s:
luṃṭhanaiḥ sarpaṇaiścaiva cārurūpo'dbhutāṃ gatim ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavāṃstatra kāraṇaṃ samabuddhyata ..19..
5.245.d:
लुंठनैः सर्पणैश्चैव चारुरूपोऽद्भुतां गतिम् ..
तं दृष्ट्वा भगवांस्तत्र कारणं समबुद्ध्यत ..19..
5.245.m: with rollings and creepings, of charming form and marvelous movement. / Seeing him there, the Lord perceived the reason.

5.245.s:
ūrdhvaretāstatastasminsasarjādau dadhāra tat ..
vīryaṃ vahnimukhe caiva sotpapāta gṛhādbahiḥ .. 6.246.20 ..
5.245.d:
ऊर्ध्वरेतास्ततस्तस्मिन्ससर्जादौ दधार तत् ..
वीर्यं वह्निमुखे चैव सोत्पपात गृहाद्बहिः .. 6.246.20 ..
5.245.m: Then he of restrained semen discharged it upon him, and he held it at first. / And [when the seed was] in Fire's mouth, he flew out of the house.

5.245.s:
gate tasminpataṃge'tha pārvatī viphalaśramā ..
saṃkruddhā sarvadevānāṃ sā śaśāpa maheśvarī .. 21 ..
5.245.d:
गते तस्मिन्पतंगेऽथ पार्वती विफलश्रमा ..
संक्रुद्धा सर्वदेवानां सा शशाप महेश्वरी .. 21 ..
5.245.m: When that bird had gone, Pārvatī, her efforts rendered fruitless, / enraged, Maheśvarī cursed all the gods:

5.245.s:
yasmānmamecchā vihatā bhavadbhirduṣṭabuddhibhiḥ ..
tasmātpāṣāṇatāmāśu vrajaṃtu tridivaukasaḥ .. 22 ..
5.245.d:
यस्मान्ममेच्छा विहता भवद्भिर्दुष्टबुद्धिभिः ..
तस्मात्पाषाणतामाशु व्रजंतु त्रिदिवौकसः .. 22 ..

You are endowed with mantras and yantras in Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others; / eternal-formed, vast-formed, all-formed, taintless;
granting the highest good to people assailed by the three faults; / Mahālakṣmī, Mahākālī, Mahādevī, Maheśvarī!"
Sovereign of the universe, great cosmic illusion, giver of boons by the seed-syllable of illusion, / you of excellent form, most worthy of choice, bestower of boons, excellent daughter.
Those men who always worship you with auspicious bilva leaves, / to them you grant kingship, fulfil desires, and constantly bestow perfection.
For those by whom you are worshipped especially with bilva leaves during Cāturmāsya, / you yourself have become a wish-granting cow to accomplish their desires.
Those who always worship [you] united with Maheśvara in the world / with great devotion through bilva leaves have neither sorrow nor wrongdoing.
Especially during Cāturmāsya, worship of you bears great fruit. / From this day onward, for those people by whom you are worshipped with bilva leaves,
O Maheśānī, you will grant unsurpassed knowledge. / During Cāturmāsya, bilva leaves bear extraordinary fruit, O fair-faced one.

5.245.m:
Offered according to rule for the pleasure of Umā and Maheśvara, it is imperishable. / As Śrī is in the tulasī plant, so is Pārvatī in the bilva.
In your form you are seen as the universe, granter of all desired things. / Especially during Cāturmāsya, the two, when attended upon, bear great fruit.
Thus ends the two hundred and forty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Account of Pārvatī's Cursing of Indra and Others', in the Account of Paijavana, in the Greatness of Cāturmāsya, in the Dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, in the Account of the One Reclining on Śeṣa, in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra, in the Sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Great Purāṇa of Skanda containing eighty-one thousand verses.

5.246.d:
पार्वतीं बिल्ववृक्षस्थां लक्ष्मीं च तुलसीगताम् ..
आदौ सर्वं वृक्षमयं पूर्वं विश्वमजायत .. 21 ..
5.246.m: Pārvatī residing in the bilva tree, and Lakṣmī in the tulasī. / In the beginning, this entire universe first came to be composed of trees.

5.246.s:
ete vṛkṣā mahāśreṣṭhāḥ sarve devāṃśasaṃbhavāḥ ..
eteṣāṃ sparśanādeva sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate [. 22 ..
5.246.d:
एते वृक्षा महाश्रेष्ठाः सर्वे देवांशसंभवाः ..
एतेषां स्पर्शनादेव सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते [. 22 ..
5.246.m: These trees are exceedingly exalted, all born from portions of the gods. / Merely by touching them, one is freed from all sins,

5.246.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa mahāpāpaughahāriṇaḥ ..
yadā tenaiva dadṛśurdevāstribhuvaneśvaram .. 23 ..
5.246.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण महापापौघहारिणः ..
यदा तेनैव ददृशुर्देवास्त्रिभुवनेश्वरम् .. 23 ..
5.246.m: which especially during Cāturmāsya take away heaps of great sins. / When the gods saw the lord of the three worlds by that very means,

5.246.s:
tadākāśabhavā vāṇīṃ prāha devānyathārthataḥ ..
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ kṛpayā vṛkṣamāśritaḥ .. 24 ..
5.246.d:
तदाकाशभवा वाणीं प्राह देवान्यथार्थतः ..
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां कृपया वृक्षमाश्रितः .. 24 ..
5.246.m: then a voice originating from the sky spoke truly to the gods: / 'The Lord, out of compassion for all beings, has taken refuge in a tree.

5.246.s:
cāturmāsye'tha saṃprāpte sarvabhūtadayākaraḥ ..
aśvattho'taḥ sadā sevyo maṃdavāre viśeṣataḥ .. 25 .
5.246.d:
चातुर्मास्येऽथ संप्राप्ते सर्वभूतदयाकरः ..
अश्वत्थोऽतः सदा सेव्यो मंदवारे विशेषतः .. 25 .
5.246.m: When Cāturmāsya has arrived, he who shows mercy to all beings [is there]. / Therefore the aśvattha tree should always be served, especially on Saturdays.

5.246.s:
nityamaśvatthasaṃsparśātpāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā ..
dugdhena tarpaṇaṃ ye vai tilamiśreṇa bhaktitaḥ .. 26 ..
5.246.d:
नित्यमश्वत्थसंस्पर्शात्पापं याति सहस्रधा ..
दुग्धेन तर्पणं ये वै तिलमिश्रेण भक्तितः .. 26 ..
5.246.m: By daily touching the aśvattha, sin is dispersed in a thousand ways. / For those who with devotion make an offering with milk mixed with sesame seeds,

5.246.s:
secanaṃ vā kariṣyaṃti tṛptistatpūrvajeṣu ca ..
darśanādeva vṛkṣasya pātakaṃ tu vinaśyati .. 27 ..
5.246.d:
सेचनं वा करिष्यंति तृप्तिस्तत्पूर्वजेषु च ..
दर्शनादेव वृक्षस्य पातकं तु विनश्यति .. 27 ..
5.246.m: or who perform watering, there will be satisfaction for their ancestors. / Merely by seeing the tree, sin is destroyed.

5.246.s:
pippalaḥ pūjito dhyāto dṛṣṭaḥ sevita eva vā ..
pāparogavināśāya cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
aśvatthaṃ pūjitaṃ siktaṃ sarvabhūtasukhāvaham .. 28 ..
5.246.d:
पिप्पलः पूजितो ध्यातो दृष्टः सेवित एव वा ..
पापरोगविनाशाय चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
अश्वत्थं पूजितं सिक्तं सर्वभूतसुखावहम् .. 28 ..
5.246.m: The pippala tree, worshipped, meditated upon, seen, or served, / serves to destroy sins and diseases, especially during Cāturmāsya. / The aśvattha, worshipped and watered, brings happiness to all beings.

5.246.s:
sarvāmayaharaṃ caiva sarvapāpaughahāriṇam ..
ye narāḥ kīrtayiṣyaṃti nāmāpyaśvatthavṛkṣajam .. 29 ..
5.246.d:
सर्वामयहरं चैव सर्वपापौघहारिणम् ..
ये नराः कीर्तयिष्यंति नामाप्यश्वत्थवृक्षजम् .. 29 ..
5.246.m: It removes all illnesses and carries away heaps of all sins. / Those men who even recite the names born of the aśvattha tree

5.246.s:
na teṣāṃ yamalokasya bhayaṃ mārge prajāyate ..
kuṃkumaiścaṃdanaiścaiva suliptaṃ yaśca kārayeta .. 6.247.30 ..
5.246.d:
न तेषां यमलोकस्य भयं मार्गे प्रजायते ..
कुंकुमैश्चंदनैश्चैव सुलिप्तं यश्च कारयेत .. 6.247.30 ..
5.246.m: have no fear on the path to the realm of Yama. / And he who causes it to be well anointed with saffron and sandalwood

5.246.s:
tasya tāpatrayābhāvo vaikuṃṭhe gaṇatā bhavet ..
duḥsvapnaṃ duṣṭaciṃtāñca duṣṭajvaraparābhavān .. 31 ..
5.246.d:
तस्य तापत्रयाभावो वैकुंठे गणता भवेत् ..
दुःस्वप्नं दुष्टचिंताञ्च दुष्टज्वरपराभवान् .. 31 ..
5.246.m: will be free from the three kinds of suffering and will become an attendant in Vaikuṇṭha. / 'O pippala, beloved of Hari, bring to dissolution bad dreams,

5.246.s:
vilayaṃ naya pāpāni pippala tvaṃ haripriya ..
maṃtreṇānena ye devāḥ pūjayiṣyaṃti pippalam .. 32 ..
5.246.d:
विलयं नय पापानि पिप्पल त्वं हरिप्रिय ..
मंत्रेणानेन ये देवाः पूजयिष्यंति पिप्पलम् .. 32 ..
5.246.m: evil thoughts, defeats from violent fevers, and sins!' / Those gods who worship the pippala with this mantra,

5.246.s:
tatasteṣāṃ dharmarājo jāyate vākyakārakaḥ ..
aśvattho vacanenāpi prokto jñānaprado nṛṇām .1 33 ..
5.246.d:
ततस्तेषां धर्मराजो जायते वाक्यकारकः ..
अश्वत्थो वचनेनापि प्रोक्तो ज्ञानप्रदो नृणाम् .1 33 ..
5.246.m: to them the King of Dharma becomes obedient to their word. / The aśvattha, even by its name, is declared to bestow knowledge upon men.

5.246.s:
śruto harati pāpaṃ ca janmādi maraṇāvadhi ..
aśvatthasevanaṃ puṇyaṃ cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 34 ..
supte deve vṛkṣamadhyamāsthāya bhagavānprabhuḥ ..
jalaṃ pṛthvīgataṃ sarvaṃ prapibanniva sevate .. 35 ..
5.246.d:
श्रुतो हरति पापं च जन्मादि मरणावधि ..
अश्वत्थसेवनं पुण्यं चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 34 ..
सुप्ते देवे वृक्षमध्यमास्थाय भगवान्प्रभुः ..
जलं पृथ्वीगतं सर्वं प्रपिबन्निव सेवते .. 35 ..
5.246.m:
And when heard [of], it removes sin up to the end of life from birth onward. / The veneration of the aśvattha is meritorious, especially during Cāturmāsya.
While the Lord is asleep, having entered the interior of the tree, the blessed sovereign Lord / dwells there, as if drinking up all the water residing upon the earth.

5.246.s:
jalaṃ viṣṇurjalatvena viṣṇureva raso mahān ..
tasmādvṛkṣagato viṣṇuścāturmāsye'ghanāśanaḥ .. 36 ..
5.246.d:
जलं विष्णुर्जलत्वेन विष्णुरेव रसो महान् ..
तस्माद्वृक्षगतो विष्णुश्चातुर्मास्येऽघनाशनः .. 36 ..
5.246.m: Water is Viṣṇu, by virtue of being water; Viṣṇu himself is the great essence. / Therefore, Viṣṇu residing in the tree is the destroyer of sins during Cāturmāsya.

5.246.s:
sarvabhūtagato viṣṇurāpyāyayati vai jagat ..
tathāśvatthagataṃ viṣṇuṃ yo namasyenna nārakī .. 37 ..
5.246.d:
सर्वभूतगतो विष्णुराप्याययति वै जगत् ..
तथाश्वत्थगतं विष्णुं यो नमस्येन्न नारकी .. 37 ..
5.246.m: Viṣṇu, present in all living beings, indeed nourishes the universe. / Likewise, whoever bows to Viṣṇu present in the aśvattha does not go to hell.

5.246.s:
aśvatthaṃ ropayedyastu pṛthivyāṃ prayato naraḥ ..
tasya pāpasahasrāṇi vilayaṃ yāṃti tatkṣaṇāt .. 38 ..
5.246.d:
अश्वत्थं रोपयेद्यस्तु पृथिव्यां प्रयतो नरः ..
तस्य पापसहस्राणि विलयं यांति तत्क्षणात् .. 38 ..
5.246.m: Whoever, being restrained, plants an aśvattha upon the earth— / thousands of his sins vanish instantly.

5.246.s:
aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ pavitro maṃgalānvitaḥ ..
muktido ropito dhyātaścāturmāsye'ghanāśanaḥ .. 39 ..
5.246.d:
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां पवित्रो मंगलान्वितः ..
मुक्तिदो रोपितो ध्यातश्चातुर्मास्येऽघनाशनः .. 39 ..
5.246.m: Among all trees, the aśvattha is pure and endowed with auspiciousness; / when planted and meditated upon, it grants liberation; in Cāturmāsya, it destroys sins.

5.246.s:
aśvatthe caraṇaṃ dattvā brahmahatyā prajāyate ..
niṣkāraṇaṃ saṃkuthitvā narake pacyate dhruvam .. 6.247.40 ..
5.246.d:
अश्वत्थे चरणं दत्त्वा ब्रह्महत्या प्रजायते ..
निष्कारणं संकुथित्वा नरके पच्यते ध्रुवम् .. 6.247.40 ..
5.246.m: Placing a foot upon the aśvattha produces [the sin of] killing a brahmin. / Having hacked it without cause, one is surely cooked in hell.

5.246.s:
mūle viṣṇuḥ sthito nityaṃ skaṃdhe keśava eva ca ..
nārāyaṇastu śākhāsu patreṣu bhagavānhariḥ .. 41 ..
5.246.d:
मूले विष्णुः स्थितो नित्यं स्कंधे केशव एव च ..
नारायणस्तु शाखासु पत्रेषु भगवान्हरिः .. 41 ..
5.246.m: Viṣṇu is constantly situated at the root, and Keśava in the trunk; / Nārāyaṇa is in the branches, and the Blessed Lord Hari in the leaves.

5.246.s:
phale'cyuto na saṃdehaḥ sarvadevaiḥ samanvitaḥ ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa drumapūjī sa muktibhāk .. 42 ..
5.246.d:
फलेऽच्युतो न संदेहः सर्वदेवैः समन्वितः ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण द्रुमपूजी स मुक्तिभाक् .. 42 ..
5.246.m: Acyuta is in the fruit, without doubt, accompanied by all the gods. / Especially during Cāturmāsya, one who worships this tree partakes of liberation.

5.246.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena sadaivāśvatthasevanam ..
yaḥ karoti naro bhaktyā pāpaṃ yāti dinodbhavam .. 43 ..
5.246.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन सदैवाश्वत्थसेवनम् ..
यः करोति नरो भक्त्या पापं याति दिनोद्भवम् .. 43 ..
5.246.m: Therefore, with every effort, constantly honoring the aśvattha— / the sin arisen that day departs from the man who performs it with devotion.

5.246.s:
sa eva viṣṇurdruma eva mūrto mahātmabhiḥ sevitapuṇyamūlaḥ ..
yasyāśrayaḥ pāpasahasrahaṃtā bhavennṛṇāṃ kāmadugho guṇāḍhyaḥ .. 44 ..
5.246.d:
स एव विष्णुर्द्रुम एव मूर्तो महात्मभिः सेवितपुण्यमूलः ..
यस्याश्रयः पापसहस्रहंता भवेन्नृणां कामदुघो गुणाढ्यः .. 44 ..
5.246.m: He alone is Viṣṇu, indeed the tree incarnate, whose meritorious root is served by great-souled ones; / whose shelter destroys thousands of sins, yielding all desires and abounding in virtues for humankind.

5.246.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye paijavanopākhyāna aśvatthamahimavarṇanaṃnāma saptacatvāriṃśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 247 ..
5.246.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्यान अश्वत्थमहिमवर्णनंनाम सप्तचत्वारिंशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 247 ..
5.246.m: Thus ends the two hundred and forty-seventh chapter, entitled “Description of the Greatness of the Aśvattha,” in the Paijavana narrative within the Māhātmya of Cāturmāsya, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada within the narrative of the Sleeper on Śeṣa, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 247

5.247.s:
.. vāṇyuvāca .. ..
palāśo harirūpeṇa sevyate hi purāvidaiḥ ..
bahubhirhyupacāraistu brahmavṛkṣasya sevanam .. 1 ..
5.247.d:
.. वाण्युवाच .. ..
पलाशो हरिरूपेण सेव्यते हि पुराविदैः ..
बहुभिर्ह्युपचारैस्तु ब्रह्मवृक्षस्य सेवनम् .. 1 ..
5.247.m: Vāṇī said: / The palāśa is indeed served in the form of Hari by those who know the past. / Indeed, the service of the brahma-tree with many offerings

5.247.s:
sarvakāmapradaṃ proktaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam ..
trīṇi patrāṇi pālāśe madhyamaṃ viṣṇuśāpitam .. 2 ..
5.247.d:
सर्वकामप्रदं प्रोक्तं महापातकनाशनम् ..
त्रीणि पत्राणि पालाशे मध्यमं विष्णुशापितम् .. 2 ..
5.247.m: is said to grant all desires and to destroy heinous sins. / There are three leaves on the palāśa; the middle one is assigned to Viṣṇu.

5.247.s:
vāme brahmā dakṣiṇe ca hara ekaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
palāśapātre yo bhuṃkte nityameva narottamaḥ .. 3 ..
5.247.d:
वामे ब्रह्मा दक्षिणे च हर एकः प्रकीर्तितः ..
पलाशपात्रे यो भुंक्ते नित्यमेव नरोत्तमः .. 3 ..
5.247.m: Brahmā is said to be on the left, and Hara alone on the right. / The best of men who constantly eats from a palāśa leaf-plate

5.247.s:
aśvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa bhokturmokṣapradaṃ bhavet .. 4 ..
5.247.d:
अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण भोक्तुर्मोक्षप्रदं भवेत् .. 4 ..
5.247.m: undoubtedly attains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices. / Especially during Cāturmāsya, it grants liberation to the eater.

5.247.s:
payasā vātha dugdhena ravivāre'niśaṃ yadi ..
cāturmāsye'rcito yaistu te yāṃti paramaṃpadam ..5..
5.247.d:
पयसा वाथ दुग्धेन रविवारेऽनिशं यदि ..
चातुर्मास्येऽर्चितो यैस्तु ते यांति परमंपदम् ..5..
5.247.m: If it is worshipped constantly on a Sunday with water or with milk / during Cāturmāsya, those [worshippers] go to the supreme abode.

5.247.s:
dṛśyate yadi pālāśaḥ prātarutthāya mānavaiḥ ..
narakānāśu nirdhūya gamyate paramaṃ padam .. 6 ..
5.247.d:
दृश्यते यदि पालाशः प्रातरुत्थाय मानवैः ..
नरकानाशु निर्धूय गम्यते परमं पदम् .. 6 ..
5.247.m: If the palāśa is seen by men upon waking in the morning, / hells are swiftly shaken off, and the supreme abode is attained.

5.247.s:
pālāśaḥ sarvadevānāmādhāro dharmasādhanam ..
yatra lobhastu tasya syāttatra pūjyo mahātaruḥ ..7..
5.247.d:
पालाशः सर्वदेवानामाधारो धर्मसाधनम् ..
यत्र लोभस्तु तस्य स्यात्तत्र पूज्यो महातरुः ..7..
5.247.m: The palāśa is the support of all the gods and the instrument of dharma. / Where one has a desire for it, there the great tree is to be worshipped.

5.247.s:
yathā sarveṣu varṇeṣu vipro mukhyatamo bhavet ..
madhye sarvatarūṇāṃ ca brahmavṛkṣo mahottamaḥ ..8..
5.247.d:
यथा सर्वेषु वर्णेषु विप्रो मुख्यतमो भवेत् ..
मध्ये सर्वतरूणां च ब्रह्मवृक्षो महोत्तमः ..8..
5.247.m: Just as among all varṇas the brahmin is the foremost, / so among all trees the brahma-tree is pre-eminent,

5.247.s:
yasya mūle haro nityaṃ skaṃdhe śūladharaḥsvayam ..
śākhāsu bhagavānrudraḥ puṣpeṣu tripurāṃtakaḥ .. 9 ..
5.247.d:
यस्य मूले हरो नित्यं स्कंधे शूलधरःस्वयम् ..
शाखासु भगवान्रुद्रः पुष्पेषु त्रिपुरांतकः .. 9 ..
5.247.m: at whose root Hara constantly dwells, and the trident-bearer himself in the trunk; / the Blessed Lord Rudra is in the branches, the destroyer of Tripura in the flowers;

5.247.s:
śivaḥ patreṣu vasati phale gaṇapatistathā ..
gaṃgāpatistvacāyāṃ tu majjāyāṃ bhagavā nbhavaḥ .. 6.248.10 ..
5.247.d:
शिवः पत्रेषु वसति फले गणपतिस्तथा ..
गंगापतिस्त्वचायां तु मज्जायां भगवा न्भवः .. 6.248.10 ..
5.247.m: Śiva resides in the leaves, and Gaṇapati in the fruit; / the lord of Gaṅgā is in the bark, and the Blessed Lord Bhava in the marrow;

5.247.s:
īśvarastu praśākhāsu sarvo'yaṃ haravallabhaḥ ..
haraḥ karpūradhavalo yathāvadvarṇitaḥ sadā .. 11 ..
5.247.d:
ईश्वरस्तु प्रशाखासु सर्वोऽयं हरवल्लभः ..
हरः कर्पूरधवलो यथावद्वर्णितः सदा .. 11 ..
5.247.m: Īśvara is in the twigs; this entire [tree] is beloved of Hara. / Hara is always described as being white as camphor;

5.247.s:
tathā hyayaṃ brahmarūpaḥ sitavarṇo mahābhagaḥ..
ciṃtito ripunāśāya pāpasaṃśoṣaṇāya ca .. 12 ..
5.247.d:
तथा ह्ययं ब्रह्मरूपः सितवर्णो महाभगः..
चिंतितो रिपुनाशाय पापसंशोषणाय च .. 12 ..
5.247.m: likewise indeed is this [tree], having the form of Brahman, white-colored and very auspicious. / Contemplated for the destruction of enemies and the drying up of sins,

5.247.s:
manorathapradānāya jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
guruvāre samāyāte cāturmāsye tathaiva ca .. 13 ..
5.247.d:
मनोरथप्रदानाय जायते नात्र संशयः ..
गुरुवारे समायाते चातुर्मास्ये तथैव च .. 13 ..
5.247.m: it serves to grant desired wishes, there is no doubt here. / When Thursday arrives, and likewise during Cāturmāsya,
worshipped, praised, and meditated upon, it is the destroyer of all sorrows.

5.247.s:
devastutyo devabījaṃ paraṃ yanmūrtaṃ brahma brahmavṛkṣatvamāptam ..
nityaṃ sevyaḥ śraddhayā sthāṇurūpaścāturmāsye sevitaḥ pāpahā syāt.. 15 ..
5.247.d:
देवस्तुत्यो देवबीजं परं यन्मूर्तं ब्रह्म ब्रह्मवृक्षत्वमाप्तम् ..
नित्यं सेव्यः श्रद्धया स्थाणुरूपश्चातुर्मास्ये सेवितः पापहा स्यात्.. 15 ..
5.247.m: Praised by the gods, the seed of the gods, the supreme Brahman manifest that has attained the state of the brahma-tree— / this form of Sthāṇu should be constantly served with faith; served in Cāturmāsya, it destroys sins.

5.247.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye paijavanopākhyāne pālāśamahimavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 248 ..
5.247.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्याने पालाशमहिमवर्णनंनामाष्टचत्वारिंशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 248 ..
5.247.m: Thus ends the two hundred and forty-eighth chapter, entitled “Description of the Greatness of the Palāśa,” in the Paijavana narrative within the Māhātmya of Cāturmāsya, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada within the narrative of the Sleeper on Śeṣa, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 248

5.248.s:
vāṇyuvāca .. ..
tulasī ropitā yena gṛhasthena mahāphalā ..
gṛhe tasya na dāridryaṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 1 ..
5.248.d:
वाण्युवाच .. ..
तुलसी रोपिता येन गृहस्थेन महाफला ..
गृहे तस्य न दारिद्र्यं जायते नात्र संशयः .. 1 ..
5.248.m: Vāṇī said: / By whichever householder the highly fruitful tulasī is planted, / in his house poverty does not arise; there is no doubt about this.

5.248.s:
tulasyā darśanādeva pāparāśirnivartate ..
śriye'mṛtakaṇotpannā tulasī harivallabhā .. 2 ..
5.248.d:
तुलस्या दर्शनादेव पापराशिर्निवर्तते ..
श्रियेऽमृतकणोत्पन्ना तुलसी हरिवल्लभा .. 2 ..
5.248.m: By the mere sight of tulasī, a heap of sins is averted. / Born from a drop of nectar for prosperity, tulasī is beloved of Hari.

5.248.s:
pibantyā ruciraṃ pānaṃ prāṇināṃ pāpahāriṇī ..
yasyā rūpe vasellakṣmīḥ skandhe sāgarasaṃbhavā .. 3 ..
5.248.d:
पिबन्त्या रुचिरं पानं प्राणिनां पापहारिणी ..
यस्या रूपे वसेल्लक्ष्मीः स्कन्धे सागरसंभवा .. 3 ..
5.248.m: For living beings who drink its pleasing juice, it removes sins. / Lakṣmī, born from the ocean, dwells in her form, in the trunk;

5.248.s:
patreṣu satataṃ śrīśca śākhāsu kamalā svayam ..
indirā puṣpagā nityaṃ phale kṣīrābdhisaṃbhavā .. 4 ..
5.248.d:
पत्रेषु सततं श्रीश्च शाखासु कमला स्वयम् ..
इन्दिरा पुष्पगा नित्यं फले क्षीराब्धिसंभवा .. 4 ..
5.248.m: Śrī constantly resides in the leaves, Kamalā herself in the branches; / Indirā is always in the flowers, and the one born of the ocean of milk in the fruit.

5.248.s:
tulasī śuṣkakāṣṭheṣu yā rūpā viśvavyāpinī ..
majjāyāṃ padmavāsā ca tvacāsu ca haripriyā .. 5 ..
5.248.d:
तुलसी शुष्ककाष्ठेषु या रूपा विश्वव्यापिनी ..
मज्जायां पद्मवासा च त्वचासु च हरिप्रिया .. 5 ..
5.248.m: Tulasī, whose form pervades the universe, resides in the dried wood; / she who dwells in the lotus is in the marrow, and the beloved of Hari is in the barks.

5.248.s:
sarvarūpā ca sarveśā paramānandadāyinī ..
tulasī prāśako martyo yamalokaṃ na gacchati . 6 .
5.248.d:
सर्वरूपा च सर्वेशा परमानन्ददायिनी ..
तुलसी प्राशको मर्त्यो यमलोकं न गच्छति . 6 .
5.248.m: Having all forms, the sovereign mistress of all, bestowing supreme bliss— / the mortal who consumes tulasī does not go to the realm of Yama.

5.248.s:
śirasthā tulasī yasya na yāmyairanubhūyate ..
mukhasthā tulasī yasya nirvāṇapadadāyinī .. 7 ..
5.248.d:
शिरस्था तुलसी यस्य न याम्यैरनुभूयते ..
मुखस्था तुलसी यस्य निर्वाणपददायिनी .. 7 ..
5.248.m: He on whose head tulasī is placed is not perceived by the minions of Yama; / tulasī in the mouth bestows the state of nirvāṇa.

5.248.s:
hastasthātulasīyasya sa tāpatrayavarjitaḥ ..
tulasī hṛdayasthā ca prāṇināṃ sarvakāmadā .. 8 ..
5.248.d:
हस्तस्थातुलसीयस्य स तापत्रयवर्जितः ..
तुलसी हृदयस्था च प्राणिनां सर्वकामदा .. 8 ..
5.248.m: He in whose hand tulasī is placed is freed from the threefold suffering; / and tulasī placed upon the heart grants all desires to living beings.

5.248.s:
skandhasthā tulasī yasya sa pāpairna ca lipyate ..
kaṇṭhagā tulasī yasya jīvanmuktaḥ sadā hi saḥ .. 9 ..
5.248.d:
स्कन्धस्था तुलसी यस्य स पापैर्न च लिप्यते ..
कण्ठगा तुलसी यस्य जीवन्मुक्तः सदा हि सः .. 9 ..
5.248.m: He on whose shoulder tulasī rests is not tainted by sins; / he on whose neck tulasī rests is indeed forever liberated while alive.

5.248.s:
tulasīsaṃbhavaṃ patraṃ sadā vahati yo naraḥ ..
manasā cintitāṃ siddhiṃ saṃprāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ .. .. 6.249.10 ..
5.248.d:
तुलसीसंभवं पत्रं सदा वहति यो नरः ..
मनसा चिन्तितां सिद्धिं संप्राप्नोति न संशयः .. .. 6.249.10 ..
5.248.m: A man who constantly carries a leaf born of tulasī / undoubtedly attains the perfection conceived in his mind.

5.248.s:
tulasīṃsarvakāyārthasādhinīṃ duṣṭavāriṇīm ..
yo naraḥ pratyahaṃ siñcenna sa yāti yamālayam .. 11 ..
5.248.d:
तुलसींसर्वकायार्थसाधिनीं दुष्टवारिणीम् ..
यो नरः प्रत्यहं सिञ्चेन्न स याति यमालयम् .. 11 ..
5.248.m: A man who sprinkles tulasī daily—which accomplishes all goals of the body and wards off wickedness— / does not go to the abode of Yama.

5.248.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa vanditāpi vimuktidā ..
nārāyaṇaṃ jalagataṃ jñātvā vṛkṣagataṃ tathā .. 12 ..
5.248.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण वन्दितापि विमुक्तिदा ..
नारायणं जलगतं ज्ञात्वा वृक्षगतं तथा .. 12 ..
5.248.m: Especially during Cāturmāsya, even when merely greeted, it bestows liberation. / Knowing Nārāyaṇa to be in the water, and likewise in the tree,

5.248.s:
prāṇināṃ kṛpayā lakṣmīstulasīvṛkṣamāśritā ..
cāturmāsye samāyāte tulasī sevitā yadi .. 13 ..
5.248.d:
प्राणिनां कृपया लक्ष्मीस्तुलसीवृक्षमाश्रिता ..
चातुर्मास्ये समायाते तुलसी सेविता यदि .. 13 ..
5.248.m: out of compassion for living beings Lakṣmī has taken resort in the tulasī plant. / When Cāturmāsya arrives, if tulasī is served,

5.248.s:
teṣāṃ pāpasahasrāṇi yāṃti nityaṃ sahasradhā ..
govindasmaraṇaṃ nityaṃ tulasīvanasevanam .. 14 ..
5.248.d:
तेषां पापसहस्राणि यांति नित्यं सहस्रधा ..
गोविन्दस्मरणं नित्यं तुलसीवनसेवनम् .. 14 ..
5.248.m: their thousands of sins are perpetually dispersed in a thousand ways. / Constant remembrance of Govinda and tending of the tulasī grove,

5.248.s:
tulasīsecanaṃ dugdhai ścāturmāsye'tidurlabham ..
tulasīṃ varddhayedyastu mānavo yadi śraddhayā .. 15 ..
5.248.d:
तुलसीसेचनं दुग्धै श्चातुर्मास्येऽतिदुर्लभम् ..
तुलसीं वर्द्धयेद्यस्तु मानवो यदि श्रद्धया .. 15 ..
5.248.m: and the watering of tulasī with milk during Cāturmāsya are extremely hard to attain. / If a human being should nurture a tulasī with faith,

5.248.s:
ālavālāṃbudānaiśca pāvitaṃ sakalaṃ kulam ..
yathā śrīstulasīsaṃsthā nityameva hi varddhate .. 16 ..
5.248.d:
आलवालांबुदानैश्च पावितं सकलं कुलम् ..
यथा श्रीस्तुलसीसंस्था नित्यमेव हि वर्द्धते .. 16 ..
5.248.m: the entire family is purified through gifts of water in its basin. / Just as Śrī residing in the tulasī indeed ever grows,

5.248.s:
tathātathā gṛhasthasya kāmavṛddhiḥ prajāyate ..
brahmacārīgṛhasthaśca vānaprastho yatistathā .. 17 ..
5.248.d:
तथातथा गृहस्थस्य कामवृद्धिः प्रजायते ..
ब्रह्मचारीगृहस्थश्च वानप्रस्थो यतिस्तथा .. 17 ..
5.248.m: so also does the householder's increase of desires come to be. / The student, the householder, the forest-dweller, and likewise the ascetic,

5.248.s:
tathā prakṛtayaḥ sarvāstulasīsevane ratāḥ ..
śraddhayā yadi jāyante na tāsāṃ duḥkhado hariḥ .. 18 ..
5.248.d:
तथा प्रकृतयः सर्वास्तुलसीसेवने रताः ..
श्रद्धया यदि जायन्ते न तासां दुःखदो हरिः .. 18 ..
5.248.m: as well as all the subjects, if engaged in serving tulasī / with faith, Hari does not cause them suffering.

5.248.s:
eko hariḥ sakalavṛkṣagato vibhāti nānārasaistu paribhāvitamūrtireva ..
vṛkṣādhivāsamagamatkamalā ca devī duḥkhādināśanakarī satataṃ smṛtā'pi .. 19 ..
5.248.d:
एको हरिः सकलवृक्षगतो विभाति नानारसैस्तु परिभावितमूर्तिरेव ..
वृक्षाधिवासमगमत्कमला च देवी दुःखादिनाशनकरी सततं स्मृताऽपि .. 19 ..
5.248.m: One Hari, having entered into every tree, shines forth, His form indeed permeated with diverse essences; / and the goddess Kamalā, the destroyer of sorrow and the like, though merely remembered constantly, came to abide in trees. 19

5.248.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇaekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭha nāga rakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye paijavanopākhyāne tulasīmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikonapañcāśaduttara dviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..249..
5.248.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराणएकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठ नाग रखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्याने तुलसीमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकोनपञ्चाशदुत्तर द्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..249..
5.248.m: Thus ends the two hundred and forty-ninth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Greatness of Tulasī' in the Story of Paijavana, in the Greatness of Cāturmāsya, in the Dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, in the Story of the One Reclining on Śeṣa, in the Greatness of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. 249

5.249.s:
.. vāṇyuvāca .. ..
bilvapatrasya māhātmyaṃ kathituṃ naiva śakyate..
tavoddeśena vakṣyāmi mahendra śṛṇu tattvataḥ ..1..
5.249.d:
.. वाण्युवाच .. ..
बिल्वपत्रस्य माहात्म्यं कथितुं नैव शक्यते..
तवोद्देशेन वक्ष्यामि महेन्द्र शृणु तत्त्वतः ..1..
5.249.m: The heavenly voice said: / It is impossible indeed to describe the greatness of the bilva leaf. / In brief, I shall tell you, O Mahendra; listen to it accurately. 1

5.249.s:
vihāraśramamāpannā devī girisutā śubhā ..
lalāṭaphalake tasyāḥ svedabindurajāyata ..2..
5.249.d:
विहारश्रममापन्ना देवी गिरिसुता शुभा ..
ललाटफलके तस्याः स्वेदबिन्दुरजायत ..2..
5.249.m: The auspicious goddess, the Daughter of the Mountain, overcome with the fatigue of strolling, / had a drop of sweat arise on her forehead. 2

5.249.s:
sa bhavānyā vinikṣipto bhūtale nipapāta ca ..
mahātarurayaṃ jāto mandare parvatottame .. 3 ..
5.249.d:
स भवान्या विनिक्षिप्तो भूतले निपपात च ..
महातरुरयं जातो मन्दरे पर्वतोत्तमे .. 3 ..
5.249.m: Flicked away by Bhavānī, it fell onto the ground. / This great tree arose on Mandara, the best of mountains. 3

5.249.s:
tataḥ śailasutā tatra ramamāṇā yayau punaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā vanagataṃ vṛkṣaṃ vismayotphullalocanā .. 4 ..
5.249.d:
ततः शैलसुता तत्र रममाणा ययौ पुनः ..
दृष्ट्वा वनगतं वृक्षं विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचना .. 4 ..
5.249.m: Then the Daughter of the Mountain, wandering there in delight, came again; / seeing the tree standing in the forest, her eyes widened in astonishment. 4

5.249.s:
jayāṃ ca vijayāṃ caiva papraccha ca sakhīdvayam ..
ko'yaṃ mahātarurdivyo vibhāti vanamadhyagaḥ ..
dṛśyate rucirākāro mahāharṣakaro hyayam .. 5 ..
5.249.d:
जयां च विजयां चैव पप्रच्छ च सखीद्वयम् ..
कोऽयं महातरुर्दिव्यो विभाति वनमध्यगः ..
दृश्यते रुचिराकारो महाहर्षकरो ह्ययम् .. 5 ..
5.249.m: And she asked the two companions, Jayā and Vijayā: / 'What is this divine great tree shining in the middle of the forest? / It appears lovely of form and indeed causes great delight.' 5

5.249.s:
.. jayovāca .. ..
devi tvaddehasaṃbhūto vṛkṣo'yaṃ svedabindujaḥ ..
nāmā'sya kuru vai kṣipraṃ pūjitaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ .. 6 ..
5.249.d:
.. जयोवाच .. ..
देवि त्वद्देहसंभूतो वृक्षोऽयं स्वेदबिन्दुजः ..
नामाऽस्य कुरु वै क्षिप्रं पूजितः पापनाशनः .. 6 ..
5.249.m: Jayā said: / 'O Goddess, this tree arose from your body, born from a drop of sweat. / Give it a name quickly; worshipped, it destroys sins.' 6

5.249.s:
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
yasmātkṣoṇītalaṃ bhittvā viśiṣṭo'yaṃ mahātaruḥ .. 7 ..
5.249.d:
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
यस्मात्क्षोणीतलं भित्त्वा विशिष्टोऽयं महातरुः .. 7 ..
5.249.m: Pārvatī said: / 'Because, cleaving the surface of the earth, this excellent, great tree 7

5.249.s:
udatiṣṭhatsamīpe me tasmādbilvo bhavatvayam ..
imaṃ vṛkṣaṃ samāsādya bhaktitaḥ patrasaṃcayam .. 8 ..
5.249.d:
उदतिष्ठत्समीपे मे तस्माद्बिल्वो भवत्वयम् ..
इमं वृक्षं समासाद्य भक्तितः पत्रसंचयम् .. 8 ..
5.249.m: stood up near me, therefore let this be the bilva. / Approaching this tree with devotion, the collection of leaves 8

5.249.s:
āhariṣyatyasau rājā bhaviṣyatyeva bhūtale ..
yaḥ kariṣyati me pūjāṃ patraiḥ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .. 9 ..
5.249.d:
आहरिष्यत्यसौ राजा भविष्यत्येव भूतले ..
यः करिष्यति मे पूजां पत्रैः श्रद्धासमन्वितः .. 9 ..
5.249.m: he will gather, [and] he shall surely become a king on earth. / Whoever performs my worship with its leaves, full of faith, 9

5.249.s:
yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyettasya siddhiḥ prajāyate ..
yo dṛṣṭvā bilvapatrāṇi śraddhāmapi kariṣyati .. 6.250.10 ..
5.249.d:
यंयं काममभिध्यायेत्तस्य सिद्धिः प्रजायते ..
यो दृष्ट्वा बिल्वपत्राणि श्रद्धामपि करिष्यति .. 6.250.10 ..
5.249.m: whatever desire he contemplates, fulfillment of that arises for him. / Whoever, having seen bilva leaves, shall even show faith 10

5.249.s:
pūjanārthāya vidhaye dhanadā'haṃ na saṃśayaḥ ..
patrāgraprāśane yastu kariṣyati mano yadi ..
tasya pāpasahasrāṇi yāsyaṃti vilayaṃ svayama .. 11 ..
5.249.d:
पूजनार्थाय विधये धनदाऽहं न संशयः ..
पत्राग्रप्राशने यस्तु करिष्यति मनो यदि ..
तस्य पापसहस्राणि यास्यंति विलयं स्वयम .. 11 ..
5.249.m: in the rite for the purpose of worship, I am the giver of wealth [to him], no doubt. / If someone sets their mind upon consuming the tip of a leaf, / his thousands of sins will automatically dissolve away. 11

5.249.s:
śiraḥ patrāgrasaṃyuktaṃ karoti yadi mānavaḥ ..
na yāmyā yātanā hyasya duḥkhadātrī bhaviṣyati .. 12 ..
5.249.d:
शिरः पत्राग्रसंयुक्तं करोति यदि मानवः ..
न याम्या यातना ह्यस्य दुःखदात्री भविष्यति .. 12 ..
5.249.m: If a person applies the tip of a leaf to their head, / the torment of Yama will not cause him sorrow.' 12

5.249.s:
ityuktvā pārvatī hṛṣṭā jagāma bhavanaṃ svakam ..
sakhībhiḥ sahitā devī gaṇairapi samanvitā .. 13 ..
5.249.d:
इत्युक्त्वा पार्वती हृष्टा जगाम भवनं स्वकम् ..
सखीभिः सहिता देवी गणैरपि समन्विता .. 13 ..
5.249.m: Having spoken thus, Pārvatī, delighted, went to her own abode, / the goddess accompanied by her companions and attended by her gaṇas. 13

5.249.s:
.. vāṇyuvāca .. ..
ayaṃ bilvataruḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pavitraḥ pāpanāśanaḥ ..
tasya mūle sthitā devī girijā nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 14 ..
5.249.d:
.. वाण्युवाच .. ..
अयं बिल्वतरुः श्रेष्ठः पवित्रः पापनाशनः ..
तस्य मूले स्थिता देवी गिरिजा नात्र संशयः .. 14 ..
5.249.m: The heavenly voice said: / This bilva tree is eminent, pure, and the destroyer of sins. / The goddess Girijā resides at its root, there is no doubt in this. 14

5.249.s:
skandhe dākṣāyaṇī devī śākhāsu ca maheśvarī ..
patreṣu pārvatī devī phale kātyā yanī smṛtā .. 15 ..
5.249.d:
स्कन्धे दाक्षायणी देवी शाखासु च महेश्वरी ..
पत्रेषु पार्वती देवी फले कात्या यनी स्मृता .. 15 ..
5.249.m: On the trunk is goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, and on the branches is Maheśvarī; / on the leaves is goddess Pārvatī, [and] on the fruit Kātyāyanī is remembered. 15

5.249.s:
tvaci gaurī samākhyātā aparṇā madhyavalkale ..
puṣpe durgā samākhyātā umā śākhāṃgakeṣu ca .. 16 ..
5.249.d:
त्वचि गौरी समाख्याता अपर्णा मध्यवल्कले ..
पुष्पे दुर्गा समाख्याता उमा शाखांगकेषु च .. 16 ..
5.249.m: Gaurī is declared to be on the bark, Aparṇā on the inner bark; / Durgā is declared to be on the flower, and Umā on the branch-joints. 16

5.249.s:
kaṇṭakeṣu ca sarveṣu koṭayo navasaṃkhyayā .
śaktayaḥ prāṇirakṣārthaṃ saṃsthitā girijā''jñayā ..17 ..
5.249.d:
कण्टकेषु च सर्वेषु कोटयो नवसंख्यया .
शक्तयः प्राणिरक्षार्थं संस्थिता गिरिजा'ऽज्ञया ..17 ..
5.249.m: And on all the thorns, nine crores in number / of Śaktis reside by order of Girijā for the protection of living beings. 17

5.249.s:
tāṃ bhajaṃti supatraiśca pūjayaṃti sanātanīm ..
yaṃyaṃ kāmayate kāmaṃ tasya siddhirbhaveddhruvam.. 18 ..
5.249.d:
तां भजंति सुपत्रैश्च पूजयंति सनातनीम् ..
यंयं कामयते कामं तस्य सिद्धिर्भवेद्ध्रुवम्.. 18 ..
5.249.m: They revere her and worship the eternal goddess with excellent leaves; / whatever desire one desires, its fulfillment will surely come to pass. 18

5.249.s:
maheśvarī sā girijā maheśvarī viśuddharūpā janamokṣadātrī..
haraṃ ca dṛṣṭvātha palāśamāśritaṃ svalīlayā bilvavapuścakāra sā .. 19 ..
5.249.d:
महेश्वरी सा गिरिजा महेश्वरी विशुद्धरूपा जनमोक्षदात्री..
हरं च दृष्ट्वाथ पलाशमाश्रितं स्वलीलया बिल्ववपुश्चकार सा .. 19 ..
5.249.m: She is Maheśvarī, Girijā, Maheśvarī of pure form, the giver of liberation to people. / And seeing Hara residing in the palāśa, she assumed the form of the bilva by her own play. 19

5.249.s: iti śrīskāṃdemahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ sahitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cātu rmāsyamāhātmye paijavanopākhyāne bilvotpattivarṇanaṃnāma pañcāśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..250...
5.249.d: इति श्रीस्कांदेमहापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां सहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातु र्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्याने बिल्वोत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम पञ्चाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..250...
5.249.m: Thus ends the two hundred and fiftieth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Origin of Bilva' in the Story of Paijavana, in the Greatness of Cāturmāsya, in the Dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, in the Story of the One Reclining on Śeṣa, in the Greatness of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. 250

5.250.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
ityuktvā''kāśajāvāṇī virarāma śubhapradā ..
te'pi devāstadāścaryaṃ mahaddṛṣṭvā mahāvratāḥ .. 1 ..
5.250.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
इत्युक्त्वा'ऽकाशजावाणी विरराम शुभप्रदा ..
तेऽपि देवास्तदाश्चर्यं महद्दृष्ट्वा महाव्रताः .. 1 ..
5.250.m: Gālava said: / Having spoken thus, the voice born from the sky, which bestows auspiciousness, fell silent. / Then those gods of great vows, having seen that great wonder, 1

5.250.s:
catuṣṭayaṃ ca vṛkṣāṇāṃ cāturmāsye samāgate ..
apūjayaṃśca vidhivadaikyabhāvena śūdraja .. 2 ..
5.250.d:
चतुष्टयं च वृक्षाणां चातुर्मास्ये समागते ..
अपूजयंश्च विधिवदैक्यभावेन शूद्रज .. 2 ..
5.250.m: worshipped the group of four trees when Cāturmāsya arrived / in accordance with the rules with a sense of oneness, O son of a Śūdra. 2

5.250.s:
cāturmāsye'tha saṃpūrṇe devo hariharātmakaḥ ..
prasannastānuvācātha bhaktyā pratyakṣarūpadhṛk .. 3 ..
5.250.d:
चातुर्मास्येऽथ संपूर्णे देवो हरिहरात्मकः ..
प्रसन्नस्तानुवाचाथ भक्त्या प्रत्यक्षरूपधृक् .. 3 ..
5.250.m: When Cāturmāsya was completed, the Lord whose essence is Hari and Hara, / being pleased through their devotion, assuming a visible form, then said to them: 3

5.250.s:
yūyaṃ gacchata deveśa mahā vrataparāyaṇāḥ ..
bhuṃkta svānsvāṃścādhikārānmayā te dānavā hatāḥ .. 4 ..
5.250.d:
यूयं गच्छत देवेश महा व्रतपरायणाः ..
भुंक्त स्वान्स्वांश्चाधिकारान्मया ते दानवा हताः .. 4 ..
5.250.m: 'Go, O lords of the gods, devoted to great vows; / enjoy your respective authorities; the Dānavas have been slain by me.' 4

5.250.s:
ityuktvā devadeveśāvaikyarūpadharau yadā ..
gaṇānāṃ devatānāṃ ca buddhiṃ nirbhedatāṃ tadā .. 5 ..
5.250.d:
इत्युक्त्वा देवदेवेशावैक्यरूपधरौ यदा ..
गणानां देवतानां च बुद्धिं निर्भेदतां तदा .. 5 ..
5.250.m: Having said this, when the two Lords of the gods, assuming a unified form, / were bringing the intellect of the gaṇas and the deities to non-differentiation, 5

5.250.s:
nayantau tau tadā ceśā babhūvaturarindamau..
te'pi devā nirābādhā hṛṣṭacittā hyabhedataḥ .. 6 ..
5.250.d:
नयन्तौ तौ तदा चेशा बभूवतुररिन्दमौ..
तेऽपि देवा निराबाधा हृष्टचित्ता ह्यभेदतः .. 6 ..
5.250.m: then those two Lords, subduers of enemies, existed [as one]. / Those gods too, free from distress, rejoicing in mind through non-duality, 6

5.250.s:
prayayuḥ svāṃścādhikārānvimānagaṇa koṭibhiḥ ..
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
tathā tatrāpi te devāḥ pārvatyāḥ śāpamohitāḥ .. 7 ..
5.250.d:
प्रययुः स्वांश्चाधिकारान्विमानगण कोटिभिः ..
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
तथा तत्रापि ते देवाः पार्वत्याः शापमोहिताः .. 7 ..
5.250.m: departed to their respective offices on crores of aerial chariots. / Gālava said: / Then, there too, those gods, deluded by Pārvatī's curse, 7

5.250.s:
stutvā tāṃ bilvapatraiśca pūjayitvā maheśvarīm ..
prasannavadanāṃ stutvā praṇipatya punaḥpunaḥ .. 8 ..
5.250.d:
स्तुत्वा तां बिल्वपत्रैश्च पूजयित्वा महेश्वरीम् ..
प्रसन्नवदनां स्तुत्वा प्रणिपत्य पुनःपुनः .. 8 ..
5.250.m: having praised her and worshipped Maheśvarī with bilva leaves, / praising her whose face was gracious, prostrating again and again, 8

5.250.s:
sā provāca tato devānviśvamātā tu saṃstutā ..
mama śāpo vṛthā naiva bhaviṣyati surottamāḥ .. 9 ..
5.250.d:
सा प्रोवाच ततो देवान्विश्वमाता तु संस्तुता ..
मम शापो वृथा नैव भविष्यति सुरोत्तमाः .. 9 ..
5.250.m: the Mother of the Universe, being thus praised, then said to the gods: / 'My curse shall not be in vain, O best of gods. 9

5.250.s:
tathāpi kṛtapāpānāṃ karavāṇi kṛpāṃ ca vaḥ ..
svarge dṛṣanmayā naiva bhaviṣyatha surottamāḥ .. 6.251.10 ..
5.250.d:
तथापि कृतपापानां करवाणि कृपां च वः ..
स्वर्गे दृषन्मया नैव भविष्यथ सुरोत्तमाः .. 6.251.10 ..
5.250.m: Nevertheless, I shall show grace to you who have committed sin: / you shall not become made of stone in heaven, O best of gods; 10

5.250.s:
martyalokaṃ ca saṃprāpya pratimāsu ca sarvaśaḥ ..
sarve devāśca varadā lokānāṃ prabhaviṣyatha .. 11 ..
5.250.d:
मर्त्यलोकं च संप्राप्य प्रतिमासु च सर्वशः ..
सर्वे देवाश्च वरदा लोकानां प्रभविष्यथ .. 11 ..
5.250.m: having reached the mortal world, in images everywhere, / all you gods shall become boongivers to people. 11

5.250.s:
pāṇigraheṇa vihitā ye kumārāḥ kumārikāḥ ..
teṣāṃteṣāṃ prajāścaiva bhaviṣyatha na saṃśayaḥ .. 12 ..
5.250.d:
पाणिग्रहेण विहिता ये कुमाराः कुमारिकाः ..
तेषांतेषां प्रजाश्चैव भविष्यथ न संशयः .. 12 ..
5.250.m: Those young men and maidens who are joined in marriage, / you shall indeed become their offspring, without a doubt.' 12

5.250.s:
ityuktvā sā bhagavatī devatānāṃ varapradā ..
viṣṇuṃ maheśvaraṃ caiva provāca kupitā bhṛśam .. 13 ..
5.250.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सा भगवती देवतानां वरप्रदा ..
विष्णुं महेश्वरं चैव प्रोवाच कुपिता भृशम् .. 13 ..
5.250.m: Having spoken thus, that goddess, bestower of boons upon the deities, / addressed Viṣṇu and Maheśvara, extremely enraged: 13

5.250.s:
devāstasyā bhayānnaṣṭā martyeṣu pratimāṃ gatāḥ ..
bhaktānāṃ mānasaṃ bhāvaṃ pūrayantaḥ susaṃsthitāḥ .. 14 ..
5.250.d:
देवास्तस्या भयान्नष्टा मर्त्येषु प्रतिमां गताः ..
भक्तानां मानसं भावं पूरयन्तः सुसंस्थिताः .. 14 ..
5.250.m: Out of fear of her, the gods vanished and took form as images among mortals, / remaining well established and fulfilling the desires of devotees' hearts. 14

5.250.s:
yasmādviṣṇo maheśānastvayā'pi na niṣedhitaḥ ..
tasmāttvamapi pāṣāṇo bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ .. 15 ..
5.250.d:
यस्माद्विष्णो महेशानस्त्वयाऽपि न निषेधितः ..
तस्मात्त्वमपि पाषाणो भविष्यसि न संशयः .. 15 ..
5.250.m: “Because, O Viṣṇu, you too did not stop the Great Lord, / therefore you also will become stone, without a doubt. 15

5.250.s:
haro'pyaśmamayaṃ rūpaṃ prāpya lokavigarhitam ..
liṃgākāraṃ vipraśāpānmahadduḥkhamavāpsyati .. 16 ..
5.250.d:
हरोऽप्यश्ममयं रूपं प्राप्य लोकविगर्हितम् ..
लिंगाकारं विप्रशापान्महद्दुःखमवाप्स्यति .. 16 ..
5.250.m: Hara, too, having assumed a form of stone despised by the world, / having the shape of a liṅga, will undergo great suffering through the brahmin's curse.” 16

5.250.s:
tacchrutvā bhagavānviṣṇuḥ pārvatīmanukūlayan ..
uvāca praṇato bhūtvā harabhāryāṃ maheśvarīm .. 17 ..
5.250.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्विष्णुः पार्वतीमनुकूलयन् ..
उवाच प्रणतो भूत्वा हरभार्यां महेश्वरीम् .. 17 ..
5.250.m: Hearing that, Lord Viṣṇu, propitiating Pārvatī, / bowed down and spoke to the wife of Hara, the Great Goddess. 17

5.250.s:
.. śrīviṣṇuruvāca .. ..
mahāvrate mahādevi mahādevapriyā sadā ..
tvaṃ hi sattvarajaḥsthā ca tāmasī śaktiruttamā .. 18 ..
5.250.d:
.. श्रीविष्णुरुवाच .. ..
महाव्रते महादेवि महादेवप्रिया सदा ..
त्वं हि सत्त्वरजःस्था च तामसी शक्तिरुत्तमा .. 18 ..
5.250.m: Lord Viṣṇu said: / “O lady of great vows, O great goddess, ever beloved of the Great God, / you abide in sattva and rajas, and you are the supreme tāmasic Śakti. 18

5.250.s:
mātrātrayasamopetā guṇatrayavibhāvinī ..
māyādīnāṃ janitrī tvaṃ viśvavyāpakarūpiṇī .. 19 ..
5.250.d:
मात्रात्रयसमोपेता गुणत्रयविभाविनी ..
मायादीनां जनित्री त्वं विश्वव्यापकरूपिणी .. 19 ..
5.250.m: Endowed with the three measures, manifesting the three guṇas, / you are the mother of māyā and the rest, having a form that pervades the universe. 19

5.250.s:
vedatrayastutā tvaṃ ca sādhyārūpeṇa rāgiṇī ..
arūpā sarvarūpā tvaṃ janasantānadāyinī .. 6.251.20 ..
5.250.d:
वेदत्रयस्तुता त्वं च साध्यारूपेण रागिणी ..
अरूपा सर्वरूपा त्वं जनसन्तानदायिनी .. 6.251.20 ..
5.250.m: You are praised by the three Vedas, passionate in the form of what is to be attained; / formless yet possessing all forms, you grant continuity of offspring. 20

5.250.s:
phalavelā mahākālī mahālakṣmīḥ sarasvatī ..
oṃkāraśca vaṣaṭkārastvameva hi sureśvari .. 21 ..
5.250.d:
फलवेला महाकाली महालक्ष्मीः सरस्वती ..
ओंकारश्च वषट्कारस्त्वमेव हि सुरेश्वरि .. 21 ..
5.250.m: The time of harvest, Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī, Sarasvatī, / the syllable Oṃ and the call vaṣaṭ—you alone indeed are these, O queen of gods! 21

5.250.s:
bhūtadhātri namaste'stu śivāyai ca namo'stu te ..
rāgiṇyai ca virāgiṇyai vikarāle namaḥ śubhe .. 22 ..
5.250.d:
भूतधात्रि नमस्तेऽस्तु शिवायै च नमोऽस्तु ते ..
रागिण्यै च विरागिण्यै विकराले नमः शुभे .. 22 ..
5.250.m: O supporter of creatures, praise be to you; praise be to Śivā! / Praise be to the passionate and the dispassionate, O dreadful and auspicious one! 22

5.250.s:
evaṃ stutā prasannākṣī prasannenāṃtarātmanā ..
uvāca paramodāraṃ mithyāroṣayutaṃ vacaḥ .. 23 ..
5.250.d:
एवं स्तुता प्रसन्नाक्षी प्रसन्नेनांतरात्मना ..
उवाच परमोदारं मिथ्यारोषयुतं वचः .. 23 ..
5.250.m: Praised in this manner, with pleased eyes and a serene inner self, / she spoke words of supreme generosity, mingled with feigned anger: 23

5.250.s:
macchāpo nā'nyathā bhāvī janārdana tavāpyayam ..
tatrā'pi saṃsthitastvaṃ hi yogīśvaravimuktidaḥ .. 24 ..
5.250.d:
मच्छापो नाऽन्यथा भावी जनार्दन तवाप्ययम् ..
तत्राऽपि संस्थितस्त्वं हि योगीश्वरविमुक्तिदः .. 24 ..
5.250.m: “This curse of mine shall not be otherwise, Janārdana, even for you; / yet abiding there, you shall indeed bestow liberation on the lords of yoga. 24

5.250.s:
kāmapradaśca bhaktānāṃ cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
nimnagā gaṃḍakīnāma brahmaṇo dayitā sutā .. 25 ..
5.250.d:
कामप्रदश्च भक्तानां चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
निम्नगा गंडकीनाम ब्रह्मणो दयिता सुता .. 25 ..
5.250.m: And you shall grant desires to devotees, especially during the Cāturmāsya. / There is a river named Gaṇḍakī, the beloved daughter of Brahmā, 25

5.250.s:
pāṣāṇasārasaṃbhūtā puṇyadātrī mahājalā ..
tasyāḥ suvimale nīre tava vāso bhaviṣyati .. 26 ..
5.250.d:
पाषाणसारसंभूता पुण्यदात्री महाजला ..
तस्याः सुविमले नीरे तव वासो भविष्यति .. 26 ..
5.250.m: born from the essence of stone, conferring merit, having vast waters. / In her pure waters your dwelling shall be. 26

5.250.s:
caturviṃśatibhedena purāṇajñairnirīkṣitaḥ .
mukhe jāṃbūnadaṃ caiva śālagrāmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 27 ..
5.250.d:
चतुर्विंशतिभेदेन पुराणज्ञैर्निरीक्षितः .
मुखे जांबूनदं चैव शालग्रामः प्रकीर्तितः .. 27 ..
5.250.m: Perceived in twenty-four varieties by those who know the Purāṇas, / having gold in its mouth, it is celebrated as the Śālagrāma. 27

5.250.s:
varttulastejasaḥ piṃḍaḥ śriyā yukto bhaviṣyasi ..
sarvasāmarthyasaṃyukto yogināmapi mokṣadaḥ .. 28 ..
5.250.d:
वर्त्तुलस्तेजसः पिंडः श्रिया युक्तो भविष्यसि ..
सर्वसामर्थ्यसंयुक्तो योगिनामपि मोक्षदः .. 28 ..
5.250.m: You will be a round mass of splendor, united with Śrī, / endowed with all power, bestowing liberation even on yogins. 28

5.250.s:
ye tvāṃ śilāgataṃ viṣṇuṃ pūjayiṣyaṃti mānavāḥ ..
teṣāṃ sucintitāṃ siddhiṃ bhaktānāṃ saṃprayacchasi .. 29 ..
5.250.d:
ये त्वां शिलागतं विष्णुं पूजयिष्यंति मानवाः ..
तेषां सुचिन्तितां सिद्धिं भक्तानां संप्रयच्छसि .. 29 ..
5.250.m: Those mortals who worship you, Viṣṇu, residing in the stone— / to those devotees you grant their desired perfection. 29

5.250.s:
śilāgataṃ ca deveśaṃ tulasyā bhakti tatparāḥ ..
pūjayiṣyaṃti manujāsteṣāṃ muktirna dūrataḥ .. 6.251.30 ..
5.250.d:
शिलागतं च देवेशं तुलस्या भक्ति तत्पराः ..
पूजयिष्यंति मनुजास्तेषां मुक्तिर्न दूरतः .. 6.251.30 ..
5.250.m: And the mortals devoted to bhakti who worship the lord of the gods in stone / with tulasī—for them liberation is not far away. 30

5.250.s:
śilāsthitaṃ ca yaḥ paśyettvāṃ viṣṇuṃ pratimāgatam ..
sucakrāṃkitasarvāṃgaṃ na sa gacchedyamālayam .. 31 ..
5.250.d:
शिलास्थितं च यः पश्येत्त्वां विष्णुं प्रतिमागतम् ..
सुचक्रांकितसर्वांगं न स गच्छेद्यमालयम् .. 31 ..
5.250.m: And whoever sees you, Viṣṇu, present in an image and situated in stone, / all of whose limbs are marked with auspicious discuses, does not go to the abode of Yama.” 31

5.250.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
iti te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ śālagrāmasya kāraṇam ..
yathā sa bhagavānviṣṇuḥ pāṣāṇatvamupā gataḥ .. 32 ..
5.250.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
इति ते कथितं सर्वं शालग्रामस्य कारणम् ..
यथा स भगवान्विष्णुः पाषाणत्वमुपा गतः .. 32 ..
5.250.m: Gālava said: / Thus has been told to you the entire origin of the Śālagrāma, / how the blessed Viṣṇu attained the state of being a stone. 32

5.250.s:
govindo'pi mahāśāpaṃ labdhvā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ ..
pārvatī ca maheśānaṃ kupitā praṇamayya ca .. 33 .
5.250.d:
गोविन्दोऽपि महाशापं लब्ध्वा स्वभवनं गतः ..
पार्वती च महेशानं कुपिता प्रणमय्य च .. 33 .
5.250.m: Govinda too, having received that great curse, went to his own abode. / And Pārvatī, making the Great Lord bow, wrathfully departed. 33

5.250.s:
evaṃ sa eva bhagavānbhavabhūta bhavyabhūtādikṛtsakalasaṃsthitināśanāṃkaḥ ..
so'pi śriyā saha bhavo'pi girīśaputryā sārddhaṃ caturṣu ca drumeṣu nivāsamāpa .. 34 ..
5.250.d:
एवं स एव भगवान्भवभूत भव्यभूतादिकृत्सकलसंस्थितिनाशनांकः ..
सोऽपि श्रिया सह भवोऽपि गिरीशपुत्र्या सार्द्धं चतुर्षु च द्रुमेषु निवासमाप .. 34 ..
5.250.m: Thus that Lord, creator of beings past, present, and future, marked by the destruction of all existence, / he along with Śrī, and Bhava along with the daughter of the Mountain Lord, took up their residence in four trees. 34

5.250.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye paija vanopākhyāne viṣṇuśāponāmaikapañcāśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 251 ..
5.250.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैज वनोपाख्याने विष्णुशापोनामैकपञ्चाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 251 ..
5.250.m: Thus ends the two hundred fifty-first chapter, entitled “The Curse of Viṣṇu,” in the narrative of Paijavana, in the glorification of the Cāturmāsya, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the account of the one who reclines on Śeṣa, in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa in the Skandamahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. 251

5.251.s:
.. śūdra uvāca .. ..
mahadāścaryametaddhi yatsurā vṛkṣarūpiṇaḥ ..
cāturmāsye samāyāte sarvavṛkṣanivāsinaḥ .. 1 ..
5.251.d:
.. शूद्र उवाच .. ..
महदाश्चर्यमेतद्धि यत्सुरा वृक्षरूपिणः ..
चातुर्मास्ये समायाते सर्ववृक्षनिवासिनः .. 1 ..
5.251.m: The Śūdra said: / “This is indeed a great wonder: that the gods take the form of trees, / dwelling in all trees when the Cāturmāsya has arrived! 1

5.251.s:
bhagavanke surāste tu keṣukeṣu nivāsinaḥ ..
etadvistarato brūhi mamānugrahakāmyayā .. 2 ..
5.251.d:
भगवन्के सुरास्ते तु केषुकेषु निवासिनः ..
एतद्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि ममानुग्रहकाम्यया .. 2 ..
5.251.m: O lord, which gods are they, and in which [trees] do they dwell? / Tell me this in detail, out of a desire to show favor to me.” 2

5.251.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
amṛtaṃ jalamityāhuścāturmāsye tadicchayā ..
līlayā vidhṛtaṃ devaiḥ pibaṃti drumadevatāḥ .. 3 ..
5.251.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
अमृतं जलमित्याहुश्चातुर्मास्ये तदिच्छया ..
लीलया विधृतं देवैः पिबंति द्रुमदेवताः .. 3 ..
5.251.m: Gālava said: / “Water is called nectar; during the Cāturmāsya, by their own desire, / held in sport by the gods, the tree-deities drink it. 3

5.251.s:
tasya pānānmahātṛptirjāyate nā'tra saṃśayaḥ ..
balaṃ tejaśca kāṃtiśca sauṣṭhavaṃ laghuvikramaḥ .. 4 ..
5.251.d:
तस्य पानान्महातृप्तिर्जायते नाऽत्र संशयः ..
बलं तेजश्च कांतिश्च सौष्ठवं लघुविक्रमः .. 4 ..
5.251.m: From drinking it, great satisfaction arises, of this there is no doubt: / strength, splendor, beauty, excellence, and swift valor. 4

5.251.s:
guṇā ete prajāyante pānātkṛṣṇāṃśasaṃbhavāt ..
nityāmṛtasyapānena balaṃ svalpaṃ prajāyate .. 5 ..
5.251.d:
गुणा एते प्रजायन्ते पानात्कृष्णांशसंभवात् ..
नित्यामृतस्यपानेन बलं स्वल्पं प्रजायते .. 5 ..
5.251.m: These qualities arise from drinking that which originates from a portion of Kṛṣṇa; / by drinking ordinary nectar, only little strength is produced. 5

5.251.s:
bhojanaṃ tatpraśaṃsaṃti nityametanna saṃśayaḥ ..
tasmāccaturṣu māseṣu pibanti jalameva hi .. 6..
5.251.d:
भोजनं तत्प्रशंसंति नित्यमेतन्न संशयः ..
तस्माच्चतुर्षु मासेषु पिबन्ति जलमेव हि .. 6..
5.251.m: They praise that consumption always, without a doubt; / therefore, during the four months, they drink water alone. 6

5.251.s:
vṛkṣasthāḥ pitaro devāḥ prāṇināṃ hita kāmyayā ..
vṛkṣāṇāṃ sevanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvamāseṣu sarvadā .. 7 ..
5.251.d:
वृक्षस्थाः पितरो देवाः प्राणिनां हित काम्यया ..
वृक्षाणां सेवनं श्रेष्ठं सर्वमासेषु सर्वदा .. 7 ..
5.251.m: The ancestors and gods reside in trees wishing for the welfare of living beings; / honoring trees is best in all months, at all times. 7

5.251.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa sevitāḥ saukhyakārakāḥ ..
tilodakena vṛkṣāṇāṃ secanaṃ sarvakāma dam .. 8 ..
5.251.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण सेविताः सौख्यकारकाः ..
तिलोदकेन वृक्षाणां सेचनं सर्वकाम दम् .. 8 ..
5.251.m: Especially when honored during the Cāturmāsya, they produce happiness; / watering trees with water mixed with sesame seeds fulfills all desires. 8

5.251.s:
kṣīravṛkṣāḥ kṣīrayuktaistoyaiḥ siktāḥ śubhapradāḥ ..
catuṣṭayaṃ ca vṛkṣāṇāṃ yaccoktaṃ pūrvato mayā .. 9 ..
5.251.d:
क्षीरवृक्षाः क्षीरयुक्तैस्तोयैः सिक्ताः शुभप्रदाः ..
चतुष्टयं च वृक्षाणां यच्चोक्तं पूर्वतो मया .. 9 ..
5.251.m: Milky trees sprinkled with waters mixed with milk bestow good fortune. / And as for the group of four trees that was mentioned earlier by me, 9

5.251.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa sarvakāma phalapradam ..
brahmā tu vaṭamāśritya prāṇināṃ sa varapradaḥ .. 6.252.10 ..
5.251.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण सर्वकाम फलप्रदम् ..
ब्रह्मा तु वटमाश्रित्य प्राणिनां स वरप्रदः .. 6.252.10 ..
5.251.m: it yields the fruits of all desires, especially during the Cāturmāsya. / Brahmā, resorting to the banyan tree, grants boons to living beings. 10

5.251.s:
sāvitrīṃ tilamāsthāya pavitraṃ śvetabhūṣaṇam ..
supte deve viśeṣeṇa tilasevā mahāphalā .. 11 ..
5.251.d:
सावित्रीं तिलमास्थाय पवित्रं श्वेतभूषणम् ..
सुप्ते देवे विशेषेण तिलसेवा महाफला .. 11 ..
5.251.m: Sāvitrī resorts to sesame, pure with white adornments; / while the god sleeps, the service of sesame yields great fruit. 11

5.251.s:
tilāḥ pavitramatulaṃ tilā dharmārthasādhakāḥ ..
tilā mokṣapradāścaiva tilāḥ pāpāpahāriṇaḥ .. 12 ..
5.251.d:
तिलाः पवित्रमतुलं तिला धर्मार्थसाधकाः ..
तिला मोक्षप्रदाश्चैव तिलाः पापापहारिणः .. 12 ..
5.251.m: Sesame is incomparably pure; sesame fulfills dharma and artha; / sesame bestows liberation; and sesame takes away sin. 12

5.251.s:
tilā viśeṣaphaladāstilāḥ śatruvināśanāḥ .
tilāḥ sarveṣu puṇyeṣu prathamaṃ samudāhṛtāḥ .. 13 ..
5.251.d:
तिला विशेषफलदास्तिलाः शत्रुविनाशनाः .
तिलाः सर्वेषु पुण्येषु प्रथमं समुदाहृताः .. 13 ..
5.251.m: Sesame gives extraordinary fruit; sesame destroys enemies; / among all meritorious things, sesame is mentioned first. 13

5.251.s:
na tilā dhānyamityāhurdevadhānyamiti smṛtam ..
tasmātsarveṣu dāneṣu tila dānaṃ mahottamam .. 14 ..
5.251.d:
न तिला धान्यमित्याहुर्देवधान्यमिति स्मृतम् ..
तस्मात्सर्वेषु दानेषु तिल दानं महोत्तमम् .. 14 ..
5.251.m: They say sesame is not mere grain; it is remembered as the grain of the gods; / therefore, among all gifts, the gift of sesame is supremely excellent. 14

5.251.s:
kanakena yutā yena tilādattāstu śūdraja ..
brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ vināśastena vai kṛtaḥ .. 15 ..
5.251.d:
कनकेन युता येन तिलादत्तास्तु शूद्रज ..
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानां विनाशस्तेन वै कृतः .. 15 ..
5.251.m: By whoever sesame seeds are given together with gold, O Śūdra, / the destruction of sins such as the murder of a brahmin is indeed accomplished. 15

5.251.s:
sāvitrī ca tilāḥ proktā sarvakāryārthasādhakāḥ ..
