tilaistu tarpaṇaṃ kuryāccāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 16 ..
5.251.d:
सावित्री च तिलाः प्रोक्ता सर्वकार्यार्थसाधकाः ..
तिलैस्तु तर्पणं कुर्याच्चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 16 ..
5.251.m: Sāvitrī and sesame are said to accomplish all purposes and goals. / One should offer libations with sesame, especially during the Cāturmāsya. 16

5.251.s:
tilānāṃ darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ sparśanaṃ sevanaṃ tathā ..
havanaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ caiva śarīrodvarttanaṃ tathā .. 17 ..
5.251.d:
तिलानां दर्शनं पुण्यं स्पर्शनं सेवनं तथा ..
हवनं भक्षणं चैव शरीरोद्वर्त्तनं तथा .. 17 ..
5.251.m: The sight of sesame is meritorious, as are touching and using it, / offering it into fire, eating it, and anointing the body with it. 17

5.251.s:
sarvathā tilavṛkṣo'yaṃ darśanādeva pāpahā ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa sevitaḥ sarvasaukhyadaḥ .. 18 ..
5.251.d:
सर्वथा तिलवृक्षोऽयं दर्शनादेव पापहा ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण सेवितः सर्वसौख्यदः .. 18 ..
5.251.m: In every way, this sesame plant removes sins merely by being seen; / especially during the Cāturmāsya, when honored, it bestows all happiness. 18

5.251.s:
mahendro yavamā sthāya sthito bhūtahite rataḥ ..
yavasya sevanaṃ puṇyaṃ darśanaṃ sparśanaṃ tathā .. 19 ..
5.251.d:
महेन्द्रो यवमा स्थाय स्थितो भूतहिते रतः ..
यवस्य सेवनं पुण्यं दर्शनं स्पर्शनं तथा .. 19 ..
5.251.m: Mahendra, resorting to barley, remains intent on the welfare of creatures; / the tending of barley is meritorious, as are seeing and touching it. 19

5.251.s:
yavaistu tarpaṇaṃ kuryāddevānāṃ dattamakṣayam ..
prajānāṃ patayaḥ sarve cūtavṛkṣamupāśritāḥ .. 6.252.20 ..
5.251.d:
यवैस्तु तर्पणं कुर्याद्देवानां दत्तमक्षयम् ..
प्रजानां पतयः सर्वे चूतवृक्षमुपाश्रिताः .. 6.252.20 ..
5.251.m: One should offer tarpaṇa to the gods with barley, which yields imperishable [merit]. / All the lords of progeny have taken resort in the mango tree.

5.251.s:
gandharvā malayaṃ vṛkṣamaguruṃ gaṇanāyakaḥ ..
samudrā vetasaṃ vṛkṣaṃ yakṣā punnāgameva ca .. 21 ..
5.251.d:
गन्धर्वा मलयं वृक्षमगुरुं गणनायकः ..
समुद्रा वेतसं वृक्षं यक्षा पुन्नागमेव च .. 21 ..
5.251.m: The Gandharvas [reside in] the sandalwood tree, the lord of gaṇas in the aloe tree, / the oceans in the cane, and the Yakṣas in the punnāga tree.

5.251.s:
nāgavṛkṣaṃ tathā nāgāḥ siddhāḥ kaṃkolakaṃ drumam ..
guhyakāḥ panasaṃ caiva kinnarā maricaṃ śritāḥ .. 22 ..
5.251.d:
नागवृक्षं तथा नागाः सिद्धाः कंकोलकं द्रुमम् ..
गुह्यकाः पनसं चैव किन्नरा मरिचं श्रिताः .. 22 ..
5.251.m: The Nāgas have taken resort in the nāga tree, the Siddhas in the kaṅkolaka tree, / the Guhyakas in the jackfruit tree, and the Kinnaras in the black pepper plant.

5.251.s:
yaṣṭīmadhu samāśritya kandarpo'bhūdvyavasthitaḥ ..
raktāṃjanaṃ mahāvṛkṣaṃ vahnirāśritya tiṣṭhati .. 23 ..
5.251.d:
यष्टीमधु समाश्रित्य कन्दर्पोऽभूद्व्यवस्थितः ..
रक्तांजनं महावृक्षं वह्निराश्रित्य तिष्ठति .. 23 ..
5.251.m: Kandarpa has taken up residence, having resorted to the liquorice plant; / Fire stays, having taken resort in the great red sandalwood tree.

5.251.s:
yamo vibhītakaṃ caiva bakulaṃ nairṛtādhipaḥ ..
varuṇaḥ kharjurīvṛkṣaṃ pūgavṛkṣaṃ ca mārutaḥ .. 24 ..
5.251.d:
यमो विभीतकं चैव बकुलं नैरृताधिपः ..
वरुणः खर्जुरीवृक्षं पूगवृक्षं च मारुतः .. 24 ..
5.251.m: Yama [resides in] the bibhītaka tree, the lord of the south-west in the bakula tree, / Varuṇa in the date palm, and the Wind god in the betel-nut tree.

5.251.s:
dhanado'kṣoṭakaṃ vṛkṣaṃ rudrāśca badarīdrumam..
saptarṣīṇāṃ mahātālā bahulaścāmarairvṛtaḥ .. 25 ..
5.251.d:
धनदोऽक्षोटकं वृक्षं रुद्राश्च बदरीद्रुमम्..
सप्तर्षीणां महाताला बहुलश्चामरैर्वृतः .. 25 ..
5.251.m: The giver of wealth [Kubera resides] in the walnut tree, and the Rudras in the jujube tree; / the great palmyra palm tree belonging to the Seven Seers is abundant and surrounded by chowries.

5.251.s:
jaṃbūrmeghaiḥ parivṛtaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇo'ghanāśanaḥ ..
kṛṣṇasya sadṛśo varṇastena jaṃbū nagottamaḥ .. 26 ..
5.251.d:
जंबूर्मेघैः परिवृतः कृष्णवर्णोऽघनाशनः ..
कृष्णस्य सदृशो वर्णस्तेन जंबू नगोत्तमः .. 26 ..
5.251.m: The rose-apple tree, surrounded by clouds, is dark in color and destroys sins; / its color is like that of Kṛṣṇa; therefore the rose-apple is the foremost among trees.

5.251.s:
tatphalairvāsudevastu prīto bhavati dānataḥ ..
jaṃbūvṛkṣaṃ samāśritya kurvaṃti dvijabhojanam .. 27 ..
5.251.d:
तत्फलैर्वासुदेवस्तु प्रीतो भवति दानतः ..
जंबूवृक्षं समाश्रित्य कुर्वंति द्विजभोजनम् .. 27 ..
5.251.m: Vāsudeva becomes pleased by giving its fruits as a gift. / Those who feed brahmins while taking resort beneath a rose-apple tree—

5.251.s:
teṣāṃ prīto harirdadyātpu ruṣārthacatuṣṭayam..
cāturmāsye samāyāte supte deve janārdane .. 28 ..
5.251.d:
तेषां प्रीतो हरिर्दद्यात्पु रुषार्थचतुष्टयम्..
चातुर्मास्ये समायाते सुप्ते देवे जनार्दने .. 28 ..
5.251.m: to them Hari, being pleased, grants the four goals of human life / when the Cāturmāsya arrives and Lord Janārdana is asleep.

5.251.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayedyastu sapatnīkāñchuciḥ sthitaḥ ..
tena nārāyaṇastuṣṭo bhave llakṣmīsahāyavān .. 29 ..
5.251.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेद्यस्तु सपत्नीकाञ्छुचिः स्थितः ..
तेन नारायणस्तुष्टो भवे ल्लक्ष्मीसहायवान् .. 29 ..
5.251.m: He who, remaining pure, feeds brahmins accompanied by their wives, / by him Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by Lakṣmī, becomes pleased.

5.251.s:
lakṣmīnārāyaṇaprītyai vastrālaṃkaraṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ..
paridhāya sapatnīkaḥ kṛtakṛtyo bhavennaraḥ .. 6.252.30 ..
5.251.d:
लक्ष्मीनारायणप्रीत्यै वस्त्रालंकरणैः शुभैः..
परिधाय सपत्नीकः कृतकृत्यो भवेन्नरः .. 6.252.30 ..
5.251.m: For the pleasure of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, a man, accompanied by his wife, / by dressing [them] in auspicious garments and ornaments, becomes one who has accomplished his purpose.

5.251.s:
yadrātritritayenaiva vaṭā śokabhavena ca ..
phalaṃ saṃjāyate tacca jaṃbunā dvijabhojanāt .. 31 ..
5.251.d:
यद्रात्रित्रितयेनैव वटा शोकभवेन च ..
फलं संजायते तच्च जंबुना द्विजभोजनात् .. 31 ..
5.251.m: Whatever fruit is obtained by three nights [of vow] produced under a banyan or aśoka tree, / that very [fruit] is produced by feeding brahmins under a rose-apple tree.

5.251.s:
tasmindine ekabhuktaṃ kārayetkṛtyakṛttadā ..
bahunā ca kimuktena jaṃbūvṛkṣa prapūjanāt .. 32 ..
5.251.d:
तस्मिन्दिने एकभुक्तं कारयेत्कृत्यकृत्तदा ..
बहुना च किमुक्तेन जंबूवृक्ष प्रपूजनात् .. 32 ..
5.251.m: On that day the performer of the rite should observe a single meal. / What is the use of speaking at length? From the worship of the rose-apple tree,

5.251.s:
putrapautradhanairyukto jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
jaṃbūrmeghaiḥ parivṛtā vidyutā'śoka eva ca .. 33 ..
5.251.d:
पुत्रपौत्रधनैर्युक्तो जायते नात्र संशयः ..
जंबूर्मेघैः परिवृता विद्युताऽशोक एव च .. 33 ..
5.251.m: one is endowed with sons, grandsons, and wealth—there is no doubt about this. / The rose-apple tree is enveloped by clouds, and the aśoka tree by lightning.

5.251.s:
vasubhiḥ svīkṛto nityaṃ priyālaśca mahānagaḥ ..
ādityaistu japāvṛkṣo hyaśvibhyāṃ madanastathā .. 34 ..
5.251.d:
वसुभिः स्वीकृतो नित्यं प्रियालश्च महानगः ..
आदित्यैस्तु जपावृक्षो ह्यश्विभ्यां मदनस्तथा .. 34 ..
5.251.m: The great priyāla tree is always appropriated by the Vasus, / the hibiscus tree by the Ādityas, and the madana tree by the two Aśvins.

5.251.s:
viśvebhiśca madhūkaśca guggulaḥ piśitāśanaiḥ ..
sūryeṇārkaḥ pavitreṇa some nātha tripatrakaḥ .. 35 ..
5.251.d:
विश्वेभिश्च मधूकश्च गुग्गुलः पिशिताशनैः ..
सूर्येणार्कः पवित्रेण सोमे नाथ त्रिपत्रकः .. 35 ..
5.251.m: The madhūka is occupied by the Viśvedevas, and bdellium by the flesh-eaters; / the arka tree by the pure Sun, and the three-leaved tree by the Moon;

5.251.s:
khadiro bhūmiputreṇa apāmārgo budhena ca ..
aśvattho guruṇā caiva śukreṇodumbarastathā .. 36 ..
5.251.d:
खदिरो भूमिपुत्रेण अपामार्गो बुधेन च ..
अश्वत्थो गुरुणा चैव शुक्रेणोदुम्बरस्तथा .. 36 ..
5.251.m: the khadira by the son of Earth [Mars], and the apāmārga by Budha; / the peepal by the preceptor [Jupiter], and the udumbara by Śukra;

5.251.s:
śamī śanaiścareṇātha svīkṛtā śūdrajātibhiḥ..
rāhuṇā svīkṛtā dūrvā pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇocitā..37..
5.251.d:
शमी शनैश्चरेणाथ स्वीकृता शूद्रजातिभिः..
राहुणा स्वीकृता दूर्वा पितॄणां तर्पणोचिता..37..
5.251.m: the śamī by Śanaiścara and adopted by the Śūdra castes; / the dūrvā grass, suitable for offering oblations to the ancestors, is adopted by Rāhu;

5.251.s:
viṣṇośca dayitā nityaṃ cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ..
ketunā svīkṛto darbho yājñikeyo mahāphalaḥ..38..
5.251.d:
विष्णोश्च दयिता नित्यं चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः..
केतुना स्वीकृतो दर्भो याज्ञिकेयो महाफलः..38..
5.251.m: and it is always dear to Viṣṇu, especially during the Cāturmāsya. / The darbha grass, suitable for sacrifice and yielding great fruit, was adopted by Ketu;

5.251.s:
vinā yena śubhaṃ karma saṃpūrṇaṃ naiva jāyate..
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ yo maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam..39..
5.251.d:
विना येन शुभं कर्म संपूर्णं नैव जायते..
पवित्राणां पवित्रं यो मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम्..39..
5.251.m: without which no auspicious rite is complete; / which is the purest of the pure and the most auspicious of the auspicious;

5.251.s:
mumūrṣūṇāṃ mokṣarūpo dharāsaṃstho mahādrumaḥ ..
asminvasaṃti satataṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivāḥ sadā .. 6.252.40 ..
5.251.d:
मुमूर्षूणां मोक्षरूपो धरासंस्थो महाद्रुमः ..
अस्मिन्वसंति सततं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवाः सदा .. 6.252.40 ..
5.251.m: which is the embodiment of liberation for the dying, a great plant situated upon the earth. / In it Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva always reside continuously,

5.251.s:
mūle madhye tathā'gre ca yasya nāmāpi tṛpti dam ..
anye'pi devā vṛkṣāṃstānadhiśritya mahādrumāḥ .. 41 ..
5.251.d:
मूले मध्ये तथाऽग्रे च यस्य नामापि तृप्ति दम् ..
अन्येऽपि देवा वृक्षांस्तानधिश्रित्य महाद्रुमाः .. 41 ..
5.251.m: at its root, middle, and tip; its very name gives satisfaction. / Other deities also, having taken resort in those trees, those great plants,

5.251.s:
pravarttaṃte hi māseṣu caturṣu ca na saṃśayaḥ ..
cāturmāsye devapatnyaḥ sarvā vallīsamāśri tāḥ .. 42 ..
5.251.d:
प्रवर्त्तंते हि मासेषु चतुर्षु च न संशयः ..
चातुर्मास्ये देवपत्न्यः सर्वा वल्लीसमाश्रि ताः .. 42 ..
5.251.m: become active during these four months; of this there is no doubt. / During the Cāturmāsya, all the wives of the gods reside in climbing vines;

5.251.s:
prayacchaṃti nṛṇāṃ kāmānvāṃchitānsevitā api ..
tasmātsarvātmabhāvena pippalo yena sevitaḥ .. 43 ..
5.251.d:
प्रयच्छंति नृणां कामान्वांछितान्सेविता अपि ..
तस्मात्सर्वात्मभावेन पिप्पलो येन सेवितः .. 43 ..
5.251.m: they bestow desired pleasures upon men when they are served. / Therefore, he by whom the pippala tree is served with all one's heart,

5.251.s:
sevitāḥ sakalā vṛkṣā ścāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
tulasī sevitā yena sarvavalyaśca sevitāḥ .. 44 ..
5.251.d:
सेविताः सकला वृक्षा श्चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
तुलसी सेविता येन सर्ववल्यश्च सेविताः .. 44 ..
5.251.m: by him all trees are served, especially during the Cāturmāsya. / He by whom tulasī is served, all creepers are served;

5.251.s:
āpyāyitaṃ jagatsarvamābrahmastaṃbasevitam ..
cāturmāsye gṛha sthena vānaprasthena vā punaḥ .. 45..
5.251.d:
आप्यायितं जगत्सर्वमाब्रह्मस्तंबसेवितम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये गृह स्थेन वानप्रस्थेन वा पुनः .. 45..
5.251.m: the entire world, extending up to the realm of Brahmā, is gladdened and served. / During the Cāturmāsya, whether by a householder or by a forest-dweller,

5.251.s:
brahmacāriyatibhyāṃ ca sevitā mokṣadāyinī ..
eteṣāṃ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ chedanaṃ naiva kārayet .. 46 ..
5.251.d:
ब्रह्मचारियतिभ्यां च सेविता मोक्षदायिनी ..
एतेषां सर्ववृक्षाणां छेदनं नैव कारयेत् .. 46 ..
5.251.m: or by a celibate student and an ascetic, when served, she bestows liberation. / One should never cause the cutting of all these trees,

5.251.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa vinā yajñādikāraṇam..
etaduktamaśeṣeṇa yatpṛṣṭo'hamiha tvayā .. 47 ..
5.251.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण विना यज्ञादिकारणम्..
एतदुक्तमशेषेण यत्पृष्टोऽहमिह त्वया .. 47 ..
5.251.m: especially during the Cāturmāsya, except for the purpose of a sacrifice and the like. / All this has been told completely as was asked of me here by you,

5.251.s: yathā vṛkṣatvamāpannā devāḥ sarve'pi śūdraja .. 48 ..
5.251.d: यथा वृक्षत्वमापन्ना देवाः सर्वेऽपि शूद्रज .. 48 ..
5.251.m: namely, how all the gods assumed the state of trees, O Śūdra.

5.251.s:
aśvatthamekaṃ picumandamekaṃ nyagrodhamekaṃ daśa tittiḍīśca ..
kapitthabilvāmalakītrayaṃ ca etāṃśca dṛṣṭvā narakaṃ na paśyet .. 49 ..
5.251.d:
अश्वत्थमेकं पिचुमन्दमेकं न्यग्रोधमेकं दश तित्तिडीश्च ..
कपित्थबिल्वामलकीत्रयं च एतांश्च दृष्ट्वा नरकं न पश्येत् .. 49 ..
5.251.m: One peepal tree, one neem tree, one banyan tree, and ten tamarind trees, / three wood-apple, bael, and myrobalan trees—having seen these, one would not see hell.

5.251.s:
sarve devā viśvavṛkṣeśayāśca kṛṣṇā dhārā kṛṣṇamadhyāgrakāśca ..
yasmindeve sevite viśvapūjye sarvaṃ tṛptaṃ jāyate viśvametat ..6.252.50 ..
5.251.d:
सर्वे देवा विश्ववृक्षेशयाश्च कृष्णा धारा कृष्णमध्याग्रकाश्च ..
यस्मिन्देवे सेविते विश्वपूज्ये सर्वं तृप्तं जायते विश्वमेतत् ..6.252.50 ..
5.251.m: All the gods dwell in the tree of the universe: the dark stream, and those in its dark middle and tip. / When that God who is adored by the universe is worshipped, this entire universe becomes completely satisfied.

5.251.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhenāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye vṛkṣamāhātmyakathanaṃ nāma dvipañcāśaduttaradviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ .. 252 .. cha .. ..
5.251.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठेनागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये वृक्षमाहात्म्यकथनं नाम द्विपञ्चाशदुत्तरद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः .. 252 .. छ .. ..
5.251.m: Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-second chapter, titled 'The Account of the Glory of Trees' in the Glory of Cāturmāsya within the narration of him who reclines on Śeṣa, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the Glory of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.252.s:
.. śūdra uvāca .. ..
pārvatīkupitā devī kathaṃ devena śūlinā ..
prasādaṃ ca gatā śaptvā yatkopātkṣubhyate jagat .. 1 ..
5.252.d:
.. शूद्र उवाच .. ..
पार्वतीकुपिता देवी कथं देवेन शूलिना ..
प्रसादं च गता शप्त्वा यत्कोपात्क्षुभ्यते जगत् .. 1 ..
5.252.m: The Śūdra said: / How did the goddess Pārvatī, when angered, become gracious to the trident-bearing God / after uttering a curse, she by whose anger the world is agitated?

5.252.s:
kathaṃ sa bhagavānrudro bhāryāśāpamavāpa ha ..
vaikṛtaṃ rūpamāsādya punardivyaṃ vapuḥ śritaḥ .. 2 ..
5.252.d:
कथं स भगवान्रुद्रो भार्याशापमवाप ह ..
वैकृतं रूपमासाद्य पुनर्दिव्यं वपुः श्रितः .. 2 ..
5.252.m: How did the blessed Rudra incur his wife's curse, / and after assuming a deformed shape, resort once again to his divine body?

5.252.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
devā rūpāṇyadṛśyāni kṛtvā devyā mahābhayāt..
manuṣyaloke sakale pratimāsu ca saṃsthitāḥ .. 3 ..
5.252.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
देवा रूपाण्यदृश्यानि कृत्वा देव्या महाभयात्..
मनुष्यलोके सकले प्रतिमासु च संस्थिताः .. 3 ..
5.252.m: Gālava said: / The gods, having made their forms invisible out of great fear of the Goddess, / resided in images throughout the entire world of mortals.

5.252.s:
teṣāmapi prasannā sā'nugrahaṃ samupākarot ..
viṣṇustutā mahābhāgā viśvamātā'ghanāśinī .. 4 [.
teṣāṃ balācca pārvatyāḥ śāpabhāreṇa yantritaḥ ..
tāṃ nityamevānunayannṛce sovāca śaṃkaram .. 5 ..
5.252.d:
तेषामपि प्रसन्ना साऽनुग्रहं समुपाकरोत् ..
विष्णुस्तुता महाभागा विश्वमाताऽघनाशिनी .. 4 [.
तेषां बलाच्च पार्वत्याः शापभारेण यन्त्रितः ..
तां नित्यमेवानुनयन्नृचे सोवाच शंकरम् .. 5 ..
5.252.m: She was also pleased with them and granted her favor. / Praised by Viṣṇu, the highly fortunate mother of the universe who destroys sins, / and constrained by the burden of Pārvatī's curse through their power, / she, constantly placating Śaṃkara, spoke to him:

5.252.s:
ete devā viśva pūjyā viśvasya ca varapradāḥ ..
matprasādādbhaviṣyaṃti bhaktitastoṣitā naraiḥ .. 6 ..
5.252.d:
एते देवा विश्व पूज्या विश्वस्य च वरप्रदाः ..
मत्प्रसादाद्भविष्यंति भक्तितस्तोषिता नरैः .. 6 ..
5.252.m: These gods, worthy of worship by the universe and granters of boons to the universe, / shall become gratified by men through devotion, by my grace.

5.252.s:
tvāmṛte mama karmedaṃ kṛtaṃ sādhuvininditam ..
vedyāṃ vivāha kāle ca pratyakṣaṃ sarvasākṣikam .. 7 ..
5.252.d:
त्वामृते मम कर्मेदं कृतं साधुविनिन्दितम् ..
वेद्यां विवाह काले च प्रत्यक्षं सर्वसाक्षिकम् .. 7 ..
5.252.m: Except by you, this deed condemned by the virtuous was performed by me / upon the altar at the time of marriage, in plain sight before all witnesses,

5.252.s:
yatsaptamaṃḍalānāṃ ca gamanaṃ ca karārpaṇam ..
vahniśca varuṇaḥ kṛṣṇo devatāśca savallabhāḥ .. 8 ..
5.252.d:
यत्सप्तमंडलानां च गमनं च करार्पणम् ..
वह्निश्च वरुणः कृष्णो देवताश्च सवल्लभाः .. 8 ..
5.252.m: the walking of the seven steps and the taking of hands. / Fire, Varuṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and the deities along with their beloveds,

5.252.s:
caturdikṣvaṃga saṃyuktā devabrāhmaṇasaṃyutāḥ ..
eteṣāmagrato dibyaṃ kṛtvā tvaṃ janasaṃsadi .. 9 ..
5.252.d:
चतुर्दिक्ष्वंग संयुक्ता देवब्राह्मणसंयुताः ..
एतेषामग्रतो दिब्यं कृत्वा त्वं जनसंसदि .. 9 ..
5.252.m: accompanied by their attendants in the four directions, together with the gods and brahmins— / having made a solemn vow in the presence of these, in an assembly of people,

5.252.s:
pramādātsattvamāpanno vyabhicāraṃ kathaṃ kṛthāḥ ..
guruvo'pi na sanmārge pravarttaṃte janaughavat .. 6.253.10 ..
5.252.d:
प्रमादात्सत्त्वमापन्नो व्यभिचारं कथं कृथाः ..
गुरुवोऽपि न सन्मार्गे प्रवर्त्तंते जनौघवत् .. 6.253.10 ..
5.252.m: how did you commit infidelity, overcome by error? / Even venerable elders do not continue on the right path when following the crowd;

5.252.s:
nigrāhyāḥ sarvalokeṣu prabuddhaiḥ śrūyate śrutau ..
putreṇāpi pitā śāsyaḥ śiṣyeṇāpi guruḥ svayam .. 11 ..
5.252.d:
निग्राह्याः सर्वलोकेषु प्रबुद्धैः श्रूयते श्रुतौ ..
पुत्रेणापि पिता शास्यः शिष्येणापि गुरुः स्वयम् .. 11 ..
5.252.m: they are to be restrained in all worlds by the wise, as is heard in the Veda: / even a father is to be chastised by a son, and a teacher by a disciple himself.

5.252.s:
kṣatriyairbrāhmaṇaḥ śāsyo bhāryayā ca patistathā ..
unmārgagāminaṃ śreṣṭhamapi vedāntapāragam .. 12 ..
5.252.d:
क्षत्रियैर्ब्राह्मणः शास्यो भार्यया च पतिस्तथा ..
उन्मार्गगामिनं श्रेष्ठमपि वेदान्तपारगम् .. 12 ..
5.252.m: A kṣatriya must correct a brahmin, and a wife her husband likewise; / even an eminent person gone astray, though master of the Vedānta,

5.252.s:
nīcairapi praśāsyeta śrutirāha sanātanī ..
sanmārga eva sarvatra pūjyate nāpathaḥ kvacit .. 13 ..
5.252.d:
नीचैरपि प्रशास्येत श्रुतिराह सनातनी ..
सन्मार्ग एव सर्वत्र पूज्यते नापथः क्वचित् .. 13 ..
5.252.m: should be corrected even by the lowborn: so says the eternal Veda. / Only the right path is honoured everywhere, never the wrong path anywhere.

5.252.s:
yena svakulajo dharmastyaktaḥ sa patito bhavet ..
mṛtaśca narakaṃ prāpya duḥkhabhāreṇa yujyate .. .. 14 ..
5.252.d:
येन स्वकुलजो धर्मस्त्यक्तः स पतितो भवेत् ..
मृतश्च नरकं प्राप्य दुःखभारेण युज्यते .. .. 14 ..
5.252.m: He who abandons the duty belonging to his own family becomes fallen; / and upon dying, reaching hell, he is joined to a heavy burden of sorrow.

5.252.s:
dharmaṃ tyajati nāstikyājjñātibhedamupāgataḥ ..
sa nigrāhyaḥ sarvalokairmanudharmaparāyaṇaiḥ .. 15 ..
5.252.d:
धर्मं त्यजति नास्तिक्याज्ज्ञातिभेदमुपागतः ..
स निग्राह्यः सर्वलोकैर्मनुधर्मपरायणैः .. 15 ..
5.252.m: He who abandons dharma out of disbelief, causing dissension among his kin, / is to be restrained by all people devoted to Manu’s law.

5.252.s:
kuladharmāñjñātidharmāndeśadharmānmaheśvara ..
ye tyajaṃti ca te'vaśyaṃ kulācca patitā janāḥ .. 16 ..
5.252.d:
कुलधर्माञ्ज्ञातिधर्मान्देशधर्मान्महेश्वर ..
ये त्यजंति च तेऽवश्यं कुलाच्च पतिता जनाः .. 16 ..
5.252.m: O Maheśvara, those people who abandon the customs of their family, / their kin, and their country are surely fallen from their clan.

5.252.s:
agnityāgo vratatyāgo vacanatyāga eva ca ..
dharmatyāgo naiva kāryaḥ kurvanpatita eva hi .. .. 17 ..
5.252.d:
अग्नित्यागो व्रतत्यागो वचनत्याग एव च ..
धर्मत्यागो नैव कार्यः कुर्वन्पतित एव हि .. .. 17 ..
5.252.m: Abandoning the sacred fire, abandoning a vow, abandoning one’s word, / and abandoning dharma must never be done; doing so, one is fallen indeed.

5.252.s:
na pitā na ca te mātā na bhrātā svajano'pi ca ..
paśyate tava vārtāṃ ca aspṛśyastvamadanviṣam .. 18 ..
5.252.d:
न पिता न च ते माता न भ्राता स्वजनोऽपि च ..
पश्यते तव वार्तां च अस्पृश्यस्त्वमदन्विषम् .. 18 ..
5.252.m: You have neither father, nor mother, nor brother, nor relative; / looking at your state, you are untouchable, like poison to me.

5.252.s:
asthimālācitābhasma jaṭādhārī kucailavān ..
capalo muktamaryādastasthuṃ nārhasi me'grataḥ .. 19 ..
5.252.d:
अस्थिमालाचिताभस्म जटाधारी कुचैलवान् ..
चपलो मुक्तमर्यादस्तस्थुं नार्हसि मेऽग्रतः .. 19 ..
5.252.m: Wearing a garland of bones, smeared with funeral ashes, wearing matted hair, dressed in rags, / fickle, breaking all bounds of propriety—you do not deserve to stand before me!

5.252.s:
abrahmaṇyo'vratī bhikṣurduṣṭātmā kapaṭī sadā ..
nārhasi tvaṃ mama puraḥ saṃbhāṣayitumīśvara .. 6.253.20 ..
5.252.d:
अब्रह्मण्योऽव्रती भिक्षुर्दुष्टात्मा कपटी सदा ..
नार्हसि त्वं मम पुरः संभाषयितुमीश्वर .. 6.253.20 ..
5.252.m: Hostile to brahmins, devoid of vows, a beggar, evil-minded, always deceitful— / you do not deserve to speak before me, O Īśvara!”

5.252.s:
evaṃ sā rudatī devī bāṣpavyākulalocanā ..
mahāduḥkhayutaivāsīddeveśe'nunayatyapi .. 21 ..
5.252.d:
एवं सा रुदती देवी बाष्पव्याकुललोचना ..
महादुःखयुतैवासीद्देवेशेऽनुनयत्यपि .. 21 ..
5.252.m: Thus the goddess, weeping with eyes filled with tears, / remained overcome with great grief, even as the Lord of Gods sought to appease her.

5.252.s:
punareva prakupitā haraṃ provāca bhāminī ..
tavārjavaṃ na hṛdaye kāṭhinyaṃ vedmi nityadā .. 22 ..
5.252.d:
पुनरेव प्रकुपिता हरं प्रोवाच भामिनी ..
तवार्जवं न हृदये काठिन्यं वेद्मि नित्यदा .. 22 ..
5.252.m: Furious once more, the passionate woman spoke to Hara: / “There is no straightforwardness in your heart; I know your perpetual hardness.

5.252.s:
brāhmaṇaistvāsurairuktaṃ tanmṛṣā pratibhāti me ..
yasmānmayi mahāduṣṭabhāva eva kṛtastvayā .. 23 ..
5.252.d:
ब्राह्मणैस्त्वासुरैरुक्तं तन्मृषा प्रतिभाति मे ..
यस्मान्मयि महादुष्टभाव एव कृतस्त्वया .. 23 ..
5.252.m: What the brahmins and asuras said seems false to me, / since you have shown only the most wicked disposition towards me.

5.252.s:
brāhmaṇā vaṃcitā yasmādbrāhmaṇaistvaṃ haniṣyase ..
evamuktvā bhagavatī punarāha na kiñcana .. 24 ..
5.252.d:
ब्राह्मणा वंचिता यस्माद्ब्राह्मणैस्त्वं हनिष्यसे ..
एवमुक्त्वा भगवती पुनराह न किञ्चन .. 24 ..
5.252.m: Because the brahmins were deceived, you will be struck down by brahmins!” / Having spoken thus, the goddess said nothing more.

5.252.s:
īśaḥ prasannavadanāmupacārairathākarot ..
śanairnītimayairvākyairhetumadbhirmaheśvaraḥ .. 25 ..
5.252.d:
ईशः प्रसन्नवदनामुपचारैरथाकरोत् ..
शनैर्नीतिमयैर्वाक्यैर्हेतुमद्भिर्महेश्वरः .. 25 ..
5.252.m: Then the Lord, Maheśvara, made her face cheerful by means of courtesies, / and gently with reasoned words full of good counsel.

5.252.s:
prasannalocanāṃ jñātvā kiṃcitprāha harastataḥ ..
kopena kaluṣaṃ vaktraṃ pūrṇacandra samaprabham .. 26 ..
5.252.d:
प्रसन्नलोचनां ज्ञात्वा किंचित्प्राह हरस्ततः ..
कोपेन कलुषं वक्त्रं पूर्णचन्द्र समप्रभम् .. 26 ..
5.252.m: Seeing her eyes turn calm, Hara then said a few words: / “Why do you make your face, radiant like the full moon,

5.252.s:
kasmāttvaṃ kuruṣe bhadre yuktameva vaco na te ..
sarvabhūtadayā kāryā prāṇināṃ hi hitecchayā .. 27 ..
5.252.d:
कस्मात्त्वं कुरुषे भद्रे युक्तमेव वचो न ते ..
सर्वभूतदया कार्या प्राणिनां हि हितेच्छया .. 27 ..
5.252.m: sullied with anger, O gentle lady? Your words are not proper. / Compassion must be shown to all beings, with a desire for the welfare of creatures.

5.252.s:
yadyapīṣṭo hi yasyārtho na kāryaṃ parapīḍanam ..
jagatsarvaṃ sutaprāyaṃ tavāsti varavarṇini .. 28 ..
5.252.d:
यद्यपीष्टो हि यस्यार्थो न कार्यं परपीडनम् ..
जगत्सर्वं सुतप्रायं तवास्ति वरवर्णिनि .. 28 ..
5.252.m: Even if an end is desired, harm must not be done to another. / All the universe is like your own child, O fair-complexioned lady.

5.252.s:
jagatpūjyā tvamevaikā sarvarūpadharānaghe ..
mayā yadi kṛtaṃ karmāvadyaṃ deva hitāya vai .. 29 ..
5.252.d:
जगत्पूज्या त्वमेवैका सर्वरूपधरानघे ..
मया यदि कृतं कर्मावद्यं देव हिताय वै .. 29 ..
5.252.m: You alone are worshipped by the world, bearing every form, O sinless one! / If a blameworthy deed was done by me, it was indeed for the good of the gods.

5.252.s:
tathāpyevaṃ tava suto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ..
athavā mama sarvebhyaḥ prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī .. 6.253.30 ..
5.252.d:
तथाप्येवं तव सुतो भविष्यति न संशयः ..
अथवा मम सर्वेभ्यः प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी .. 6.253.30 ..
5.252.m: Even so, you will have a son; of this there is no doubt. / Moreover, you are dearer to me than all my vital breaths.

5.252.s:
yadicchasi tathā kuryāṃ tathā tava manorathān..
prasannavadanā bhūtvā kathayasva varānane .. 31 ..
5.252.d:
यदिच्छसि तथा कुर्यां तथा तव मनोरथान्..
प्रसन्नवदना भूत्वा कथयस्व वरानने .. 31 ..
5.252.m: Whatever you wish, I will do; so too I will fulfill your desires. / Becoming cheerful-faced, speak, O fair-faced lady!”

5.252.s:
ityuktā sā bhagavatī punarāha maheśvaram ..
cāturmāsye ca saṃprāpte mahāvrata dharo yadi .. 32 ..
5.252.d:
इत्युक्ता सा भगवती पुनराह महेश्वरम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये च संप्राप्ते महाव्रत धरो यदि .. 32 ..
5.252.m: Thus addressed, the goddess spoke again to Maheśvara: / “When the Cāturmāsya arrives, if you undertake the Great Vow,

5.252.s:
devatānāṃ ca pratyakṣaṃ tāṃḍavaṃ nartase yadi ..
pārayitvā vrataṃ samyagbrahmacaryaṃ maheśvara .. 33 [.
matprītyai yadi dehārthaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca prayacchasi ..
śāpasyānugrahaṃ kuryāṃ prasavavadanā satī .. 34 ..
5.252.d:
देवतानां च प्रत्यक्षं तांडवं नर्तसे यदि ..
पारयित्वा व्रतं सम्यग्ब्रह्मचर्यं महेश्वर .. 33 [.
मत्प्रीत्यै यदि देहार्थं वैष्णवं च प्रयच्छसि ..
शापस्यानुग्रहं कुर्यां प्रसववदना सती .. 34 ..
5.252.m: and if you dance the tāṇḍava in the direct sight of the deities, / properly completing the vow of celibacy, O Maheśvara, / and if, for my pleasure, you give half your body to Viṣṇu, / then, faithful and cheerful-faced, I shall grant grace from the curse.

5.252.s:
nānyathā mama cittaṃ tvāṃ viśvāsamanugacchati ..
tacchrutvā bhagavāṃstuṣṭastatheti pratyuvāca tām .. 35 ..
5.252.d:
नान्यथा मम चित्तं त्वां विश्वासमनुगच्छति ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवांस्तुष्टस्तथेति प्रत्युवाच ताम् .. 35 ..
5.252.m: Otherwise, my heart will not trust you.” / Hearing that, the Lord was pleased and replied to her, “So be it!”

5.252.s: sāpi hṛṣṭā bhagavatī śāpasyānugrahe vṛtā .. 36 ..
5.252.d: सापि हृष्टा भगवती शापस्यानुग्रहे वृता .. 36 ..
5.252.m: She too, the goddess, was delighted, disposed to mitigate the curse.

5.252.s:
idaṃ purāṇaṃ manujaḥ śṛṇoti śraddhāyukto bhedabuddhyā dṛḍhatvam ..
tasyā vaśyaṃ jīvitaṃ sarvasiddhaṃ martyāḥ satyāttacchrayatvaṃ prayāṃti .. 37 ..
5.252.d:
इदं पुराणं मनुजः शृणोति श्रद्धायुक्तो भेदबुद्ध्या दृढत्वम् ..
तस्या वश्यं जीवितं सर्वसिद्धं मर्त्याः सत्यात्तच्छ्रयत्वं प्रयांति .. 37 ..
5.252.m: If a man hears this Purāṇa with faith and firmness against divisive thought, / his life is surely accomplished in everything; mortals attain to that refuge by virtue of truth.

5.252.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye śaṃkarakṛtapārvatyanunayo nāma tripaṃcāśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 253 ..
5.252.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये शंकरकृतपार्वत्यनुनयो नाम त्रिपंचाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. .. 253 ..
5.252.m: Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-third chapter, entitled “Śaṃkara’s Appeasement of Pārvatī,” in the Praise of Cāturmāsya, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the account of Śeṣaśāyin, in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section] of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.253.s:
śūdra uvāca .. ..
idamāścaryarūpaṃ me pratibhāti vacastava ..
yadyapi syānmahākleśo vadatastava suvrata .. 1 ..
5.253.d:
शूद्र उवाच .. ..
इदमाश्चर्यरूपं मे प्रतिभाति वचस्तव ..
यद्यपि स्यान्महाक्लेशो वदतस्तव सुव्रत .. 1 ..
5.253.m: The Śūdra said: / “These words of yours seem wondrous to me. / Although it may be a great hardship for you to speak, O you of noble vows,

5.253.s:
tathāpi mama bhāgyena matpuṇyairmadgṛhaṃ gataḥ ..
na tṛpye tvanmukhāṃbhojāccyutaṃ vākyāmṛtaṃ punaḥ .. 2 ..
5.253.d:
तथापि मम भाग्येन मत्पुण्यैर्मद्गृहं गतः ..
न तृप्ये त्वन्मुखांभोजाच्च्युतं वाक्यामृतं पुनः .. 2 ..
5.253.m: nevertheless, by my good fortune and my merits, you have come to my house. / I am never sated as I drink again the nectar of speech fallen from your lotus mouth,

5.253.s:
pibangaurīkathākhyānaṃ viśeṣaguṇapūritam ..
kathaṃ maheśvaro nṛtyaṃ cakāra surasaṃvṛtaḥ .. 3 ..
5.253.d:
पिबन्गौरीकथाख्यानं विशेषगुणपूरितम् ..
कथं महेश्वरो नृत्यं चकार सुरसंवृतः .. 3 ..
5.253.m: the narrative of the story of Gaurī, filled with exceptional virtues. / How did Maheśvara perform the dance surrounded by the gods?

5.253.s:
cāturmāsye kathaṃ jātaṃ ki grāhyaṃ vratamucyate ..
anugrahaṃ kṛtavatī sā kathaṃ ko hyanugrahaḥ .. 4 ..
5.253.d:
चातुर्मास्ये कथं जातं कि ग्राह्यं व्रतमुच्यते ..
अनुग्रहं कृतवती सा कथं को ह्यनुग्रहः .. 4 ..
5.253.m: How did it come about during Cāturmāsya? What is this vow that is enjoined to be undertaken? / How did she grant grace, and what indeed was the grace?

5.253.s:
etadvistarato brūhi pṛcchato me dvijottama ..
bhagavānpūjyate loke mamānugrahakārakaḥ .. 5 ..
5.253.d:
एतद्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि पृच्छतो मे द्विजोत्तम ..
भगवान्पूज्यते लोके ममानुग्रहकारकः .. 5 ..
5.253.m: Tell this in full to me who asks, O best of the twice-born! / The Lord is worshipped in the world; you are the one who grants grace to me.

5.253.s:
prasannavadano bhūtvā svasthaḥ kathaya suvrata ..
gālavaścāpi tacchrutvā punarāha prahṛṣṭavān .. 6 ..
5.253.d:
प्रसन्नवदनो भूत्वा स्वस्थः कथय सुव्रत ..
गालवश्चापि तच्छ्रुत्वा पुनराह प्रहृष्टवान् .. 6 ..
5.253.m: With a pleasant face, at ease, relate it, O you of noble vows!” / Having heard that, Gālava too spoke again, greatly delighted.

5.253.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
itihāsamimaṃ puṇyaṃ kathayāmi tavānagha ..
śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā yajñāyutaphalapradam.. 7 ..
5.253.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
इतिहासमिमं पुण्यं कथयामि तवानघ ..
शृणुष्वावहितो भूत्वा यज्ञायुतफलप्रदम्.. 7 ..
5.253.m: Gālava said: / “I shall tell you this sacred tradition, O sinless one; / listen attentively to it, which yields the fruit of ten thousand sacrifices.

5.253.s:
cāturmāsye'tha saṃprāpte haro bhaktisamanvitaḥ ..
brahmacaryavrataparaḥ prahṛṣṭavadano'bhavat .. 8 ..
5.253.d:
चातुर्मास्येऽथ संप्राप्ते हरो भक्तिसमन्वितः ..
ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतपरः प्रहृष्टवदनोऽभवत् .. 8 ..
5.253.m: When Cāturmāsya arrived, Hara, filled with devotion, / intent upon the vow of celibacy, became cheerful-faced.

5.253.s:
devatānāṃ ca saṃkalpaṃ maharṣīṇāṃ cakāra ha ..
samāgatya tato devā mandarācalamāsthitāḥ .. 9 ..
5.253.d:
देवतानां च संकल्पं महर्षीणां चकार ह ..
समागत्य ततो देवा मन्दराचलमास्थिताः .. 9 ..
5.253.m: He made the solemn resolve of the gods and great seers. / Then the gods, having assembled, went to Mount Mandara.

5.253.s:
praṇamya te maheśānaṃ tasthuḥ prāṃjalayo'grataḥ ..
tānuvāca surānsarvānharo dṛṣṭvā samāgatān..6.254.10 ..
5.253.d:
प्रणम्य ते महेशानं तस्थुः प्रांजलयोऽग्रतः ..
तानुवाच सुरान्सर्वान्हरो दृष्ट्वा समागतान्..6.254.10 ..
5.253.m: Having bowed to Maheśāna, they stood before him with folded hands. / Seeing all the gods assembled, Hara spoke to them.

5.253.s:
pārvatyābhihitaṃ prāha kasminkāryāṃtare sati ..
mayā niyukte'bhinaye yatra sāhāyyakāriṇaḥ .. 11 ..
5.253.d:
पार्वत्याभिहितं प्राह कस्मिन्कार्यांतरे सति ..
मया नियुक्तेऽभिनये यत्र साहाय्यकारिणः .. 11 ..
5.253.m: He recounted what Pārvatī had spoken: ‘When another matter arises, / when dramatic dance is undertaken by me, let there be helpers in it,

5.253.s:
bhavaṃtviṃdrapurogāśca cāturmāsye samāgate ..
te tathocuśca saṃhṛṣṭā namaskṛtya ca śūlinam .. 12 ..
5.253.d:
भवंत्विंद्रपुरोगाश्च चातुर्मास्ये समागते ..
ते तथोचुश्च संहृष्टा नमस्कृत्य च शूलिनम् .. 12 ..
5.253.m: led by Indra, when Cāturmāsya arrives.’ / Greatly rejoiced, they said, ‘So be it,’ and bowed to the Bearer of the Trident.

5.253.s:
svaṃsvaṃ bhavanamājagmurvimānaiḥ sūryasannibhaiḥ ..
tathā''ṣāḍhe śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ maheśvaraḥ .. 13 ..
5.253.d:
स्वंस्वं भवनमाजग्मुर्विमानैः सूर्यसन्निभैः ..
तथा'ऽषाढे शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां महेश्वरः .. 13 ..
5.253.m: They went each to his own abode in aerial chariots bright as the sun. / Then, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, Maheśvara

5.253.s:
pranarttayitumārebhe bhavānītoṣaṇāya ca ..
maṃdare parvataśreṣṭhe tatra jagmurmaharṣayaḥ .. 14 ..
5.253.d:
प्रनर्त्तयितुमारेभे भवानीतोषणाय च ..
मंदरे पर्वतश्रेष्ठे तत्र जग्मुर्महर्षयः .. 14 ..
5.253.m: began to dance to please Bhavānī / on Mandara, best of mountains. The great seers went there:

5.253.s:
nārado devalo vyāsaḥ śukadvaipāyanādayaḥ ..
aṃgirāśca marīciśca kardamaśca prajāpatiḥ .. 15 ..
5.253.d:
नारदो देवलो व्यासः शुकद्वैपायनादयः ..
अंगिराश्च मरीचिश्च कर्दमश्च प्रजापतिः .. 15 ..
5.253.m: Nārada, Devala, Vyāsa, Śuka, Dvaipāyana, and others; / Aṅgiras, Marīci, and the progenitor Kardama;

5.253.s:
kaśyapo gautamaścātrirvasiṣṭho bhṛgureva ca ..
jamadagnistathottaṃko rāmo bhārgava eva ca .. 16 ..
5.253.d:
कश्यपो गौतमश्चात्रिर्वसिष्ठो भृगुरेव च ..
जमदग्निस्तथोत्तंको रामो भार्गव एव च .. 16 ..
5.253.m: Kaśyapa, Gautama, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, and Bhṛgu; / Jamadagni, and Uttaṅka, and Rāma son of Bhṛgu.

5.253.s:
agastyaśca pulomā ca pulastyaḥ pulahastathā ..
pracetāśca kratuścaiva tathaivānye maharṣayaḥ .. 17 ..
5.253.d:
अगस्त्यश्च पुलोमा च पुलस्त्यः पुलहस्तथा ..
प्रचेताश्च क्रतुश्चैव तथैवान्ये महर्षयः .. 17 ..
5.253.m: And Agastya, Puloman, Pulastya, and Pulaha, / and Pracetas and Kratu, as well as other great seers,

5.253.s:
siddhā yakṣāḥ piśācāśca cāraṇāścāraṇaiḥ saha ..
ādityā guhyakāścaiva sā dhyāśca vasavo'śvinau .. 18 ..
5.253.d:
सिद्धा यक्षाः पिशाचाश्च चारणाश्चारणैः सह ..
आदित्या गुह्यकाश्चैव सा ध्याश्च वसवोऽश्विनौ .. 18 ..
5.253.m: siddhas, yakṣas, piśācas, and cāraṇas along with bards, / the ādityas, guhyakas, sādhyas, vasus, and the two Aśvins—

5.253.s:
ete sarve tathendrādyā brahmaviṣṇupurogamāḥ ..
samājagmurmaheśasya nṛtyadarśanalālasāḥ .. 19 ..
5.253.d:
एते सर्वे तथेन्द्राद्या ब्रह्मविष्णुपुरोगमाः ..
समाजग्मुर्महेशस्य नृत्यदर्शनलालसाः .. 19 ..
5.253.m: all these, led by Indra, preceded by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, / arrived, longing to see the dance of the great lord.

5.253.s:
tato gaṇā naṃdimukhā ratnāni pradadustathā ..
bhūṣaṇāni ca vāsāṃsi munyādibhyo yathākramam .. 6.254.20 ..
5.253.d:
ततो गणा नंदिमुखा रत्नानि प्रददुस्तथा ..
भूषणानि च वासांसि मुन्यादिभ्यो यथाक्रमम् .. 6.254.20 ..
5.253.m: Then the gaṇas, led by Nandin, gave jewels, / ornaments, and garments in order to the sages and the rest.

5.253.s:
tato vādyasahasreṣu vāditreṣu samaṃtataḥ ..
sarvairjayeti caivoktā bhagavā nvratamādiśat.. 21 ..
5.253.d:
ततो वाद्यसहस्रेषु वादित्रेषु समंततः ..
सर्वैर्जयेति चैवोक्ता भगवा न्व्रतमादिशत्.. 21 ..
5.253.m: Then, as thousands of musical instruments were played on every side / and all shouted, “Victory!”, the Lord commanded the ritual observance.

5.253.s:
bhavānī hṛṣṭahṛdayā mahādevaṃ vyalokayat ..
jayā ca vijayā caiva jayantī maṃgalāruṇā .. 22 ..
5.253.d:
भवानी हृष्टहृदया महादेवं व्यलोकयत् ..
जया च विजया चैव जयन्ती मंगलारुणा .. 22 ..
5.253.m: Bhavānī, with a joyful heart, gazed upon Mahādeva, / [surrounded by] Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, and Maṅgalāruṇā.

5.253.s:
catuṣṭayasakhīmadhye vira rāja śubhānanā ..
tasyāḥ sānnidhyayogena jagadbhāti guṇottaram .. 23 ..
5.253.d:
चतुष्टयसखीमध्ये विर राज शुभानना ..
तस्याः सान्निध्ययोगेन जगद्भाति गुणोत्तरम् .. 23 ..
5.253.m: The auspicious-faced goddess shone amidst her four companions; / through the connection of her presence, the world shines endowed with supreme excellence.

5.253.s:
yasyāḥ śarīrajā śobhā varṇituṃ naiva śakyate ..
īśo'pi gaṇakoṭībhirnā nāvakttrābhirīkṣitaḥ .. 24 ..
5.253.d:
यस्याः शरीरजा शोभा वर्णितुं नैव शक्यते ..
ईशोऽपि गणकोटीभिर्ना नावक्त्त्राभिरीक्षितः .. 24 ..
5.253.m: The beauty born of her body cannot be described at all; / even the Lord was gazed upon by tens of millions of gaṇas with various faces.

5.253.s:
piśācabhūtasaṃghaiśca vṛtaḥ paramaśobhanaḥ ..
svarṇavetradharo nandī babhau kapimukho'grataḥ .. 25 ..
5.253.d:
पिशाचभूतसंघैश्च वृतः परमशोभनः ..
स्वर्णवेत्रधरो नन्दी बभौ कपिमुखोऽग्रतः .. 25 ..
5.253.m: Surrounded by hosts of piśācas and bhūtas, exceedingly splendid, / Nandin, holding a golden staff, monkey-faced, shone in front.

5.253.s:
vidyādharāśca gaṃdharvāści trasenādayastathā ..
citranyastā iva babhustatra nāgā munīśvarāḥ .. 26 ..
5.253.d:
विद्याधराश्च गंधर्वाश्चि त्रसेनादयस्तथा ..
चित्रन्यस्ता इव बभुस्तत्र नागा मुनीश्वराः .. 26 ..
5.253.m: Vidyādharas and gandharvas, Citrasena and the rest, / the serpents, and the lords of sages shone there as if painted in a picture.

5.253.s:
śrīrāgapramukhā rāgāstasya putrā mahaujasaḥ ..
amūrttāścaiva te putrā haradeva samudbhavāḥ .. 27 ..
5.253.d:
श्रीरागप्रमुखा रागास्तस्य पुत्रा महौजसः ..
अमूर्त्ताश्चैव ते पुत्रा हरदेव समुद्भवाः .. 27 ..
5.253.m: The rāgas, of great majesty, with Śrīrāga as their foremost, were his sons; / and formless were those sons born of the god Hara.

5.253.s:
ekaikasya ca ṣaḍbhāryāḥ sarvāsāṃ ca pitāmahaḥ ..
tābhiḥ sahaiva te rāgā līlāvapurdharāstathā .. 28 ..
5.253.d:
एकैकस्य च षड्भार्याः सर्वासां च पितामहः ..
ताभिः सहैव ते रागा लीलावपुर्धरास्तथा .. 28 ..
5.253.m: Each had six wives, and Brahmā was the grandfather of them all; / together with them those rāgas, assuming bodily forms for their sport,

5.253.s:
prādurbabhūvuḥ sahasā ciṃtitāstena śaṃbhunā ..
teṣāṃ nāmāni te vacmi śṛṇuṣva tvaṃ mahādhana .. 29 ..
5.253.d:
प्रादुर्बभूवुः सहसा चिंतितास्तेन शंभुना ..
तेषां नामानि ते वच्मि शृणुष्व त्वं महाधन .. 29 ..
5.253.m: manifested suddenly when thought of by that Śambhu. / I will tell you their names; listen, O wealthy one:

5.253.s:
śrīrāgaḥ prathamaḥ putra īśvarasya vimohanaḥ ..
āsāṃ cakre bhruvormadhye parabrahma pradāyakaḥ .. 6.254.30 ..
5.253.d:
श्रीरागः प्रथमः पुत्र ईश्वरस्य विमोहनः ..
आसां चक्रे भ्रुवोर्मध्ये परब्रह्म प्रदायकः .. 6.254.30 ..
5.253.m: Śrīrāga was the first son of Īśvara, bewitching all, / residing between his eyebrows, granter of the Supreme Brahman;

5.253.s:
tanmadhyaścaiva māheśātsamudbhūto gaṇottamaḥ ..
dvitīyo'tha vasanto'bhūtkaṭideśānmahāyaśāḥ .. 31 ..
5.253.d:
तन्मध्यश्चैव माहेशात्समुद्भूतो गणोत्तमः ..
द्वितीयोऽथ वसन्तोऽभूत्कटिदेशान्महायशाः .. 31 ..
5.253.m: from its center, from the Great Lord, arose the best of gaṇas. / Then Vasanta was the second, of great renown, [born] from his waist;

5.253.s:
mahadaṃkaśca bhūtānāṃ cakrāccaiva viśuddhitaḥ ..
paṃcamastu tṛtīyo'bhūtsuto viśvavibhūṣaṇaḥ .. 32 ..
5.253.d:
महदंकश्च भूतानां चक्राच्चैव विशुद्धितः ..
पंचमस्तु तृतीयोऽभूत्सुतो विश्वविभूषणः .. 32 ..
5.253.m: [he was] the great mark of the elements, and from the viśuddha-cakra / the son Pañcama was the third, an ornament of the universe.

5.253.s:
maheśvarahṛdo jātaṃ cakraṃ caivamanāhatam ..
nāsādeśātsamudbhūto bhairavo bhairavaḥ svayam.. .. 33 ..
5.253.d:
महेश्वरहृदो जातं चक्रं चैवमनाहतम् ..
नासादेशात्समुद्भूतो भैरवो भैरवः स्वयम्.. .. 33 ..
5.253.m: From the heart of the great lord arose the cakra indeed [known as] anāhata; / from the region of the nose Bhairava himself was born, terrible.

5.253.s:
maṇipūrakanāmedaṃ cakraṃ taddhi vimuktidam ..
paṃcāśacca tathā varṇā aṃkā nāma maheśvarāt .. 34 ..
5.253.d:
मणिपूरकनामेदं चक्रं तद्धि विमुक्तिदम् ..
पंचाशच्च तथा वर्णा अंका नाम महेश्वरात् .. 34 ..
5.253.m: This cakra, indeed named maṇipūraka, bestows supreme liberation; / and fifty phonemes, names, and numbers [arose] from the Great Lord.

5.253.s:
rāśayo dvādaśa tathā nakṣatrāṇi tathaiva ca ..
svādhiṣṭhānasamudbhūtā jagadbījasamanvitāḥ .. 35 ..
5.253.d:
राशयो द्वादश तथा नक्षत्राणि तथैव च ..
स्वाधिष्ठानसमुद्भूता जगद्बीजसमन्विताः .. 35 ..
5.253.m: Likewise the twelve zodiac signs and the lunar mansions / arose from the svādhiṣṭhāna-cakra, joined with the seed of the world.

5.253.s:
kṣaṇena vṛddhimāyāṃti tato retaḥ pravartate ..
retasastu jagatsṛṣṭaṃ tadīśajananeṃdriyam .. 36 ..
5.253.d:
क्षणेन वृद्धिमायांति ततो रेतः प्रवर्तते ..
रेतसस्तु जगत्सृष्टं तदीशजननेंद्रियम् .. 36 ..
5.253.m: In an instant they increase, and thence the semen comes forth; / from that semen the world was created; it is the generative organ of the Lord.

5.253.s:
ādhārācca mahānṣaṣṭho naṭo nārāyaṇo'bhavat ..
maheśavallabhaḥ putro nīlo viṣṇuparākramaḥ .. 37 ..
5.253.d:
आधाराच्च महान्षष्ठो नटो नारायणोऽभवत् ..
महेशवल्लभः पुत्रो नीलो विष्णुपराक्रमः .. 37 ..
5.253.m: And from the ādhāra-cakra arose the great sixth, Naṭanārāyaṇa, / a son dear to the Great Lord, dark blue, possessing the prowess of Viṣṇu.

5.253.s:
ete mūrtidharā rāgā jātā bhāryāsahāyinaḥ ..
bhāryāsteṣāṃ samudbhūtāḥ śirobhāgātpinākinaḥ .. 38 ..
5.253.d:
एते मूर्तिधरा रागा जाता भार्यासहायिनः ..
भार्यास्तेषां समुद्भूताः शिरोभागात्पिनाकिनः .. 38 ..
5.253.m: These embodied rāgas were born, accompanied by their wives; / their wives were born from the head of the wielder of the Pināka.

5.253.s:
ṣaṭtriṃśatparimāṇena tatastāstvaṃ niśāmaya ..
gaurī kolāhalī dhīrā drāviḍī māla kauśikī .. 39 ..
5.253.d:
षट्त्रिंशत्परिमाणेन ततस्तास्त्वं निशामय ..
गौरी कोलाहली धीरा द्राविडी माल कौशिकी .. 39 ..
5.253.m: Thirty-six in number—now hear about them: / Gaurī, Kolāhalī, Dhīrā, Drāviḍī, Mālakauśikī,

5.253.s:
ṣaṣṭhī syāddevagāṃdhārī śrīrāgatya priyā imāḥ ..
āndolā kauśikī caiva tathā caramamaṃjarī .. 6.254.40 ..
5.253.d:
षष्ठी स्याद्देवगांधारी श्रीरागत्य प्रिया इमाः ..
आन्दोला कौशिकी चैव तथा चरममंजरी .. 6.254.40 ..
5.253.m: the sixth is Devagāndhārī: these are the beloved [wives] of Śrīrāga. / Āndolā, Kauśikī, and also Caramamañjarī,

5.253.s:
gaṃḍagirī devaśākhā rāma girī vasantagā ..
triguṇā stambhatīrthā ca ahirī kuṃkumā tathā .. 41 ..
5.253.d:
गंडगिरी देवशाखा राम गिरी वसन्तगा ..
त्रिगुणा स्तम्भतीर्था च अहिरी कुंकुमा तथा .. 41 ..
5.253.m: Gaṇḍagirī, Devaśākhā, and Rāmagirī belong to Vasanta. / Triguṇā, Stambhatīrthā, Ahirī, and Kuṅkumā,

5.253.s:
vairāṭī sāmaverī ca ṣaḍbhāryāḥ paṃcame matāḥ..
bhairavī gurjarī caiva bhāṣā velāgulī tathā .. 42 ..
5.253.d:
वैराटी सामवेरी च षड्भार्याः पंचमे मताः..
भैरवी गुर्जरी चैव भाषा वेलागुली तथा .. 42 ..
5.253.m: Vairāṭī, and Sāmaverī are considered the six wives of the fifth [rāga]. / Bhairavī, Gurjarī, Bhāṣā, Velāgulī,

5.253.s:
karṇāṭakī raktahaṃsā ṣaḍbhāryā bhairavānugāḥ ..
baṃgālī madhurā caiva kāmodā cākṣinārikā .. 43 ..
5.253.d:
कर्णाटकी रक्तहंसा षड्भार्या भैरवानुगाः ..
बंगाली मधुरा चैव कामोदा चाक्षिनारिका .. 43 ..
5.253.m: Karṇāṭakī, and Raktahaṃsā are the six wives following Bhairava. / Baṅgālī, Madhurā, Kāmodā, Akṣinārikā,

5.253.s:
devagirī ca devālī megha rāgānugā imā ..
troṭakī mīḍakī caiva narādumbī tathaiva ca .. 44 ..
5.253.d:
देवगिरी च देवाली मेघ रागानुगा इमा ..
त्रोटकी मीडकी चैव नरादुम्बी तथैव च .. 44 ..
5.253.m: Devagirī, and Devālī: these follow Megharāga. / Troṭakī, Mīḍakī, and Narādumbī,

5.253.s:
malhārī sindhumalhārī naṭanārāyaṇānugāḥ ..
etā hi giriśaṃ natvā maheśaṃ ca maheśvarīm .. 45 ..
5.253.d:
मल्हारी सिन्धुमल्हारी नटनारायणानुगाः ..
एता हि गिरिशं नत्वा महेशं च महेश्वरीम् .. 45 ..
5.253.m: Malhārī, and Sindhumalhārī follow Naṭanārāyaṇa. / These, having bowed to the Lord of the Mountain, to the Great Lord and the Great Goddess,

5.253.s:
svamūrttivāhanopetāḥ svabhartṛsahitāḥ sthitāḥ ..
brahmā mṛdaṃgavādyena toṣayāmāsa śaṃkaram .. 46 ..
5.253.d:
स्वमूर्त्तिवाहनोपेताः स्वभर्तृसहिताः स्थिताः ..
ब्रह्मा मृदंगवाद्येन तोषयामास शंकरम् .. 46 ..
5.253.m: accompanied by their own forms and vehicles, stood with their husbands. / Brahmā delighted Śaṃkara with the music of the mṛdaṅga drum;

5.253.s:
caturakṣaravādyena suvādyaṃ cākarotpunaḥ ..
tālakriyāṃ maheśāya darśayāmāsa keśavaḥ .. 47 ..
5.253.d:
चतुरक्षरवाद्येन सुवाद्यं चाकरोत्पुनः ..
तालक्रियां महेशाय दर्शयामास केशवः .. 47 ..
5.253.m: he made fine music with the four-syllable drumming again. / Keśava displayed the keeping of the rhythm to the Great Lord.

5.253.s:
vāyavastatra vādyaṃ ca cakruḥ susvaramojasā ..
mahendro vaṃśavādyaṃ ca sugiraṃ susvaraṃ bahuḥ .. 48 ..
5.253.d:
वायवस्तत्र वाद्यं च चक्रुः सुस्वरमोजसा ..
महेन्द्रो वंशवाद्यं च सुगिरं सुस्वरं बहुः .. 48 ..
5.253.m: The winds there played music melodiously and with power; / Mahendra played the flute, many fine notes and sweet tones.

5.253.s:
vahniḥ śūrparavaṃ cakre paṇavaṃ ca tathāśvinau ..
upāṃgavādanaṃ cakre somaḥ sūryaḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 49 ..
5.253.d:
वह्निः शूर्परवं चक्रे पणवं च तथाश्विनौ ..
उपांगवादनं चक्रे सोमः सूर्यः समंततः .. 49 ..
5.253.m: Agni made the sound of a winnowing fan, and the two Aśvins played the paṇava drum; / Soma and Sūrya played subsidiary instruments on all sides.

5.253.s:
ghaṃṭānāṃ vādanaṃ cakrurgaṇāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ ..
munīśvarāstathā devyaḥ pārvatīsahitāstathā .. 6.254.50 ..
5.253.d:
घंटानां वादनं चक्रुर्गणाः शतसहस्रशः ..
मुनीश्वरास्तथा देव्यः पार्वतीसहितास्तथा .. 6.254.50 ..
5.253.m: The gaṇas played bells by hundreds and thousands. / The lords of sages, the goddesses, together with Pārvatī,

5.253.s:
svarṇabhadrāsaneṣvete hyupaviṣṭā vyalokayan ..
śṛṃgāṇāṃ vādanaṃ cakrurvasavaḥ samahoragāḥ .. .. 51 ..
5.253.d:
स्वर्णभद्रासनेष्वेते ह्युपविष्टा व्यलोकयन् ..
शृंगाणां वादनं चक्रुर्वसवः समहोरगाः .. .. 51 ..
5.253.m: seated on golden thrones, looked on. / The vasus, along with great serpents, blew horns;

5.253.s:
bherīdhvaniṃ tathā sādhyā vādyānyanye surottamāḥ ..
jharjharīgomukhādīni sādhyāścakrurmahotsave .. 52 ..
5.253.d:
भेरीध्वनिं तथा साध्या वाद्यान्यन्ये सुरोत्तमाः ..
झर्झरीगोमुखादीनि साध्याश्चक्रुर्महोत्सवे .. 52 ..
5.253.m: the sādhyas made drum sounds, and other foremost gods played instruments; / the sādhyas played the jharjharī, the gomukha, and other instruments in the great festival.

5.253.s:
tantrīlayasamāyuktā gaṃdharvā madhura svarāḥ ..
suvarṇaśṛṃganādaṃ ca cakruḥ siddhāḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 53 ..
5.253.d:
तन्त्रीलयसमायुक्ता गंधर्वा मधुर स्वराः ..
सुवर्णशृंगनादं च चक्रुः सिद्धाः समंततः .. 53 ..
5.253.m: The sweet-voiced gandharvas were joined in rhythm on stringed instruments; / the siddhas on all sides made the sound of golden horns.

5.253.s:
tatastu bhagavānāsīnmahānaṭavapurdharaḥ ..
mukuṭāḥ paṃcaśīrṣe tu pannagairupaśobhitāḥ .. .. 54 ..
5.253.d:
ततस्तु भगवानासीन्महानटवपुर्धरः ..
मुकुटाः पंचशीर्षे तु पन्नगैरुपशोभिताः .. .. 54 ..
5.253.m: Then the Lord assumed the form of the Great Dancer, / with five crowns upon his heads adorned with serpents,

5.253.s:
jaṭā vimucya sakalā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahaḥ ..
bāhubhirdaśabhiryukto hārakeyūrasaṃyutaḥ .. 55 ..
5.253.d:
जटा विमुच्य सकला भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहः ..
बाहुभिर्दशभिर्युक्तो हारकेयूरसंयुतः .. 55 ..
5.253.m: all his matted locks untied, his body smeared with ashes, / endowed with ten arms, adorned with necklaces and armlets.

5.253.s:
trailokyavyāpakaṃ rūpaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham ..
kṛtvā nanartta bhagavānbhāsuraṃ sa mahānage .. 56 ..
5.253.d:
त्रैलोक्यव्यापकं रूपं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम् ..
कृत्वा ननर्त्त भगवान्भासुरं स महानगे .. 56 ..
5.253.m: Assuming a radiant form that pervaded the three worlds, equal in brilliance to ten million suns, / the Lord danced upon the great mountain.

5.253.s:
tataṃ vīṇādikaṃ vādyaṃ kāṃsyatālādikaṃ ghanam ..
vaṃśādikaṃ tu vāditraṃ tomarādikanāmakam .. 57..
5.253.d:
ततं वीणादिकं वाद्यं कांस्यतालादिकं घनम् ..
वंशादिकं तु वादित्रं तोमरादिकनामकम् .. 57..
5.253.m: Stringed instruments such as the vīṇā, solid instruments such as bronze cymbals, / wind instruments such as flutes, and percussion instruments such as drums—

5.253.s:
caturvidhaṃ tato vādyaṃ tumulaṃ samajāyata ..
tālānāṃ paṭahādīnāṃ hastakānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 58 ..
5.253.d:
चतुर्विधं ततो वाद्यं तुमुलं समजायत ..
तालानां पटहादीनां हस्तकानां तथैव च .. 58 ..
5.253.m: a tumultuous fourfold music then arose, / of rhythmic beats, paṭaha drums, and hand gestures,

5.253.s:
mānānāṃ caiva tānānāṃ pratyakṣaṃ rūpamābabhau ..
sukaṃṭhaṃ susvaraṃ muktaṃ sugambhīraṃ mahāsvanam.. 59 ..
5.253.d:
मानानां चैव तानानां प्रत्यक्षं रूपमाबभौ ..
सुकंठं सुस्वरं मुक्तं सुगम्भीरं महास्वनम्.. 59 ..
5.253.m: and the forms of the measures and musical patterns appeared visible to the eyes, / melodious, well-tuned, open, very deep, and loudly resounding.

5.253.s:
viśvāvasurnāradaśca tuṃburuścaiva gāyakāḥ ..
jagurgaṃdharvapatayo'psaraso madhurasvarāḥ .. 6.254.60 ..
5.253.d:
विश्वावसुर्नारदश्च तुंबुरुश्चैव गायकाः ..
जगुर्गंधर्वपतयोऽप्सरसो मधुरस्वराः .. 6.254.60 ..
5.253.m: Viśvāvasu, Nārada, and Tumburu, singers / and lords of gandharvas, sang, along with sweet-voiced apsarases.

5.253.s:
grāmatrayasamopetaṃ svarasaptakasaṃyutam ..
divyaṃ śuddhaṃ ca sāṃkalpaṃ tatra geyamavarttata .. 61 ..
5.253.d:
ग्रामत्रयसमोपेतं स्वरसप्तकसंयुतम् ..
दिव्यं शुद्धं च सांकल्पं तत्र गेयमवर्त्तत .. 61 ..
5.253.m: Equipped with the three parent scales and endowed with the seven notes, / divine, pure, and intentional singing proceeded there.

5.253.s:
parvato'pi mahānādaṃ harapādatalāhataḥ ..
bhramibhirbhramayaṃstatra mahīṃ sapurakānanām.. 62 ..
5.253.d:
पर्वतोऽपि महानादं हरपादतलाहतः ..
भ्रमिभिर्भ्रमयंस्तत्र महीं सपुरकाननाम्.. 62 ..
5.253.m: Struck by the soles of Hara's feet, the mountain too let out a great roar, / spinning the earth, along with its cities and forests, in dizzying circles.

5.253.s:
hastakāṃścaturāśītiṃ sa sasarja sadāśivaḥ ..
lalāṭaphalakasvedātsūtamāgadhabaṃdinaḥ ..63..
5.253.d:
हस्तकांश्चतुराशीतिं स ससर्ज सदाशिवः ..
ललाटफलकस्वेदात्सूतमागधबंदिनः ..63..
5.253.m: Sadāśiva created eighty-four hand-gestures, / and from the sweat of his forehead-plate [he brought forth] sūtas, māgadhas, and bards.

5.253.s:
maheśahṛdayājjātā gaṃdharvā viśvagāyakāḥ ..
te mūrttā devadevasya suraṃgālayasaṃyutāḥ .. 64 ..
5.253.d:
महेशहृदयाज्जाता गंधर्वा विश्वगायकाः ..
ते मूर्त्ता देवदेवस्य सुरंगालयसंयुताः .. 64 ..
5.253.m: From the heart of the Great Lord arose the Gandharvas, singers of the universe; / they embodied the God of gods, accompanied by sweet melodies and stages.

5.253.s:
prekṣakāṇāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca cakrurāścaryamojasā ..
kinnarāḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi sasṛjuḥ svairguṇairiha .. 65 ..
5.253.d:
प्रेक्षकाणामृषीणां च चक्रुराश्चर्यमोजसा ..
किन्नराः पुष्पवर्षाणि ससृजुः स्वैर्गुणैरिह .. 65 ..
5.253.m: By their vigor they produced wonder among the watching seers; / here the Kinnaras showered flowers by their own natural talents.

5.253.s:
evaṃ caturṣumāseṣu yadā nṛtyamajāyata ..
atikrāṃtā śarajjātā nirmalākāśaśobhitā .. 66 .. padmakhaṃḍasamācchannasarovaramukhāṃbujā ..
5.253.d:
एवं चतुर्षुमासेषु यदा नृत्यमजायत ..
अतिक्रांता शरज्जाता निर्मलाकाशशोभिता .. 66 .. पद्मखंडसमाच्छन्नसरोवरमुखांबुजा ..
5.253.m: When the dance had thus continued for four months, / [the rainy season] passed away, and autumn arrived, adorned with a clear sky, / lotus-faced with lakes completely covered by clusters of lotuses,

5.253.s: phalavṛkṣauṣadhībhiśca kiṃcitpāṃḍumukhacchaviḥ .. 67 ..
5.253.d: फलवृक्षौषधीभिश्च किंचित्पांडुमुखच्छविः .. 67 ..
5.253.m: and with the hue of her countenance slightly pale on account of fruit-bearing trees and herbs.

5.253.s:
ūrjaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ prasannā girijā tadā ..
samāptavratacaryaḥ sa īśvaro'pi tadā babhau .. 68 ..
5.253.d:
ऊर्जशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां प्रसन्ना गिरिजा तदा ..
समाप्तव्रतचर्यः स ईश्वरोऽपि तदा बभौ .. 68 ..
5.253.m: Then, on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Ūrja, Girijā became propitious; / having completed the observance of his vow, Īśvara too shone forth at that time.

5.253.s:
sā covāca tadā śaṃbhuṃ vikacasvaralocanā ..
vipraśāpapātitaṃ ca yadā liṃgaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 69 ..
5.253.d:
सा चोवाच तदा शंभुं विकचस्वरलोचना ..
विप्रशापपातितं च यदा लिंगं भविष्यति .. 69 ..
5.253.m: Then, with blooming eyes and voice, she said to Śambhu: / "When the liṅga falls down, brought low by the curse of the brahmins,

5.253.s:
narmadājalasaṃbhūtaṃ viśvapūjyaṃ bhaviṣyati ..
evamuktvā tatastuṣṭā harastotraṃ cakāra ha .. 6.254.70 ..
5.253.d:
नर्मदाजलसंभूतं विश्वपूज्यं भविष्यति ..
एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तुष्टा हरस्तोत्रं चकार ह .. 6.254.70 ..
5.253.m: it will arise in the waters of the Narmadā and will be worshipped by all the world." / Having spoken thus, she, being pleased, then made a hymn of praise to Hara:

5.253.s:
namaste devadevāya mahādevāya mauline ..
jagaddhātre savitre ca śaṃkarāya śivāya ca .. .. 71 ..
kapardine'jayādāya brahmagarbhāya te namaḥ ..
hiraṇyaretase tubhyaṃ nīlagrīvāya te namaḥ .. 71 ..
5.253.d:
नमस्ते देवदेवाय महादेवाय मौलिने ..
जगद्धात्रे सवित्रे च शंकराय शिवाय च .. .. 71 ..
कपर्दिनेऽजयादाय ब्रह्मगर्भाय ते नमः ..
हिरण्यरेतसे तुभ्यं नीलग्रीवाय ते नमः .. 71 ..
5.253.m:
"Obeisance to you, the God of gods, Mahādeva, the crested one, / the supporter of the world, the progenitor, Śaṃkara, and Śiva!
Obeisance to you, the matted-haired one, born of the undefeated, whose womb is the absolute, / the golden-seeded one! Obeisance to you, the blue-throated one!

5.253.s:
namo brahmaṇya devāya sitabhūtidharāya ca ..
paṃcavaktrāya rūpāya nīrūpāya namonamaḥ .. 73 ..
5.253.d:
नमो ब्रह्मण्य देवाय सितभूतिधराय च ..
पंचवक्त्राय रूपाय नीरूपाय नमोनमः .. 73 ..
5.253.m: Obeisance to the deity favorable to brahmins, the bearer of white sacred ash, / the five-faced one, the embodied, and repeatedly obeisance to the formless!

5.253.s:
sahasrākṣāya śubhrāya namaste kṛttivāsase ..
andhakāsuramokṣāya paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ .. 74 ..
5.253.d:
सहस्राक्षाय शुभ्राय नमस्ते कृत्तिवाससे ..
अन्धकासुरमोक्षाय पशूनां पतये नमः .. 74 ..
5.253.m: Obeisance to the thousand-eyed, the radiant! Obeisance to you who are clad in animal skins, / the liberator of the demon Andhaka, the Lord of Beasts!

5.253.s:
vipravahnimukhāgrāya harāya ca bhavāya ca ..
śaṃkarāya maheśāya īśvarāya namo namaḥ .. 76 ..
amūrtabrahmarūpāya mūrttānāṃ bhāvanāya ca ..
namaḥ śivāya cogrāya harāya ca bhavāya ca .. 76 ..
5.253.d:
विप्रवह्निमुखाग्राय हराय च भवाय च ..
शंकराय महेशाय ईश्वराय नमो नमः .. 76 ..
अमूर्तब्रह्मरूपाय मूर्त्तानां भावनाय च ..
नमः शिवाय चोग्राय हराय च भवाय च .. 76 ..
5.253.m:
Obeisance repeatedly to the source of the mouths of brahmins and fire, to Hara, Bhava, / Śaṃkara, the Great Lord, and Īśvara!
To the form of the unmanifest absolute, the animator of embodied beings, / obeisance to Śiva, to the fierce, to Hara, and to Bhava!

5.253.s:
namaḥ kṛṣṇāya śarvāya tripurāṃtaka hāriṇe ..
aghorāya namaste'stu namaste puruṣāya te .. 77 ..
5.253.d:
नमः कृष्णाय शर्वाय त्रिपुरांतक हारिणे ..
अघोराय नमस्तेऽस्तु नमस्ते पुरुषाय ते .. 77 ..
5.253.m: Obeisance to Kṛṣṇa, to Śarva, the destroyer of Tripura, the ravager! / Obeisance to Aghora! Obeisance to you, the Puruṣa!

5.253.s:
sadyojātāya tubhyaṃ bho vāmadevāya te namaḥ ..
īśānāya namastubhyaṃ paṃcāsyāya kapāline .. 78 ..
5.253.d:
सद्योजाताय तुभ्यं भो वामदेवाय ते नमः ..
ईशानाय नमस्तुभ्यं पंचास्याय कपालिने .. 78 ..
5.253.m: Obeisance to you, Sadyojāta! O Vāmadeva, obeisance to you! / Obeisance to you, Īśāna, the five-faced bearer of the skull!

5.253.s:
virūpākṣāya bhāvāya bhaganetranipātine ..
pūṣadaṃtanipātāya mahāyajñanipātine .. 79 ..
5.253.d:
विरूपाक्षाय भावाय भगनेत्रनिपातिने ..
पूषदंतनिपाताय महायज्ञनिपातिने .. 79 ..
5.253.m: To the odd-eyed, to existence itself, the smiter of Bhaga's eyes, / the smiter of Pūṣan's teeth, the destroyer of the great sacrifice!

5.253.s:
mṛgavyādhāya dharmāya kālacakrāya cakriṇe ..
mahāpuruṣapūjyāya gaṇānāṃ pataye namaḥ .. 6.254.80 ..
5.253.d:
मृगव्याधाय धर्माय कालचक्राय चक्रिणे ..
महापुरुषपूज्याय गणानां पतये नमः .. 6.254.80 ..
5.253.m: To the hunter of the deer, to righteousness, the wheel of Time, the wielder of the discus, / worthy of worship by the Great Person, obeisance to the lord of the gaṇas!

5.253.s:
gaṃgādharāya mṛḍine bhavānīpriyakāriṇe ..
jagadānaṃdadātre ca brahmarūpāya te namaḥ ..91..
guṇātītāya guṇine sūkṣmāya gurave'pi ca ..
namo mahāsvarūpāya bhasmano janmakāriṇe .. 82 ..
vairāgyarūpiṇe nityaṃ yogācāryāya vai namaḥ ..
mayoktamapriyaṃ deva smarasaṃhārakāraka .. 83 ..
kṣaṃtumarhasi viśveśa śirasā tvāṃ prasādaye ..
śāpānugraha evaiṣa kṛtaste vai na saṃśayaḥ .. 84 ..
mamāparādhajo manyurna kāryo bhavatā'nagha ..
evaṃ prasāditaḥ śaṃbhurhṛṣṭātmā tridaśaiḥ saha .. 85 ..
tīrṇavrataparānaṃdanirbharaḥ prāha tāmumām ..
ya imāṃ matstutiṃ bhaktyā paṭhiṣyati tavodgatām ..
tasya ceṣṭaviyogaśca na bhaviṣyati pārvati .. 86 ..
janmatrayadhanairyuktaḥ sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ ..
bhuktveha vividhānbhogānaṃte yāsyati matpuram .. 87 ..
5.253.d:
गंगाधराय मृडिने भवानीप्रियकारिणे ..
जगदानंददात्रे च ब्रह्मरूपाय ते नमः ..91..
गुणातीताय गुणिने सूक्ष्माय गुरवेऽपि च ..
नमो महास्वरूपाय भस्मनो जन्मकारिणे .. 82 ..
वैराग्यरूपिणे नित्यं योगाचार्याय वै नमः ..
मयोक्तमप्रियं देव स्मरसंहारकारक .. 83 ..
क्षंतुमर्हसि विश्वेश शिरसा त्वां प्रसादये ..
शापानुग्रह एवैष कृतस्ते वै न संशयः .. 84 ..
ममापराधजो मन्युर्न कार्यो भवताऽनघ ..
एवं प्रसादितः शंभुर्हृष्टात्मा त्रिदशैः सह .. 85 ..
तीर्णव्रतपरानंदनिर्भरः प्राह तामुमाम् ..
य इमां मत्स्तुतिं भक्त्या पठिष्यति तवोद्गताम् ..
तस्य चेष्टवियोगश्च न भविष्यति पार्वति .. 86 ..
जन्मत्रयधनैर्युक्तः सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितः ..
भुक्त्वेह विविधान्भोगानंते यास्यति मत्पुरम् .. 87 ..
5.253.m:
To the bearer of the Gaṅgā, the merciful, who brings delight to Bhavānī, / the giver of joy to the world, whose nature is the absolute: obeisance to you!
To the one beyond attributes, yet possessing attributes, subtle and also the preceptor, / obeisance to the great form, the source of ashes!
Obeisance to the eternal embodiment of dispassion, the master of yoga! / O God, O destroyer of the god of love, whatever unpleasant thing was uttered by me,
you ought to forgive, O Lord of the universe; with my head bowed I propitiate you. / Indeed, this grace in the guise of a curse was granted by you; of this there is no doubt.
No wrath arising from my offense should be held by you, O sinless one!" / Thus propitiated, Śambhu, gladdened in soul along with the gods,
filled with supreme bliss upon crossing the observance of the vow, said to Umā: / "Whoever with devotion will recite this praise of me that has issued from you, / O Pārvatī, there shall be no separation from what is dear for him.
Endowed with wealth for three births, free from all diseases, / having enjoyed various delights in this world, in the end he will go to my abode."

5.253.s:
ityuktvā tāṃ maheśo'pi svamaṃgaṃ pradadau tataḥ ..
vaiṣṇavaṃ vāmabhāgaṃ sā pratijagrāha pārvatī .. 88 ..
śarvaṃ kapālahastaṃ ca grīvārddhe garalānvitam ..
ruṇḍamālārddhahāraṃ ca sitagauraṃ samaṃtataḥ .. 89 ..
brahmāṃḍakoṭijanakaṃ jaṭābhirbhūṣitaṃ śiraḥ ..
sita dyutikalākhaṃḍaratnabhāsāvabhāsitam .. 6.254.90 ..
svarṇābharaṇasaṃyuktamekato bhujagāṃgadam ..
ekataḥ kṛttivasanamanyataḥ paṭṭakūlavat 91 ..
5.253.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तां महेशोऽपि स्वमंगं प्रददौ ततः ..
वैष्णवं वामभागं सा प्रतिजग्राह पार्वती .. 88 ..
शर्वं कपालहस्तं च ग्रीवार्द्धे गरलान्वितम् ..
रुण्डमालार्द्धहारं च सितगौरं समंततः .. 89 ..
ब्रह्मांडकोटिजनकं जटाभिर्भूषितं शिरः ..
सित द्युतिकलाखंडरत्नभासावभासितम् .. 6.254.90 ..
स्वर्णाभरणसंयुक्तमेकतो भुजगांगदम् ..
एकतः कृत्तिवसनमन्यतः पट्टकूलवत् 91 ..
5.253.m:
Having spoken thus, the Great Lord gave her his own half of the body. / Pārvatī received that left half, which belongs to Viṣṇu:
Śarva holding a skull in his hand, with poison on one half of his neck, / wearing half a garland of severed heads, fair and white all around,
the originator of millions of cosmic eggs, his head adorned with matted locks, / shining with the white luster of the crescent moon and the brilliance of gems,
adorned with golden ornaments, having a snake-armlet on one side, / an animal skin as garment on one side, and fine silk like cloth on the other,

5.253.s:
matsya vāhanasaṃyuktamanyato vṛṣabhāṃkitam ..
ekataḥ pārṣadaiḥ sevyamanyataḥ sakhisevitam .. 92 ..
5.253.d:
मत्स्य वाहनसंयुक्तमन्यतो वृषभांकितम् ..
एकतः पार्षदैः सेव्यमन्यतः सखिसेवितम् .. 92 ..
5.253.m: equipped with the fish-vehicle on one side, marked by a bull on the other, / served by attendants on one side, and attended by female companions on the other.

5.253.s:
rūpamevaṃvidhaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmādyā devatāgaṇāḥ ..
tuṣṭuvuḥ parayā bhaktyā tejobhūṣitalocanam .. 93 ..
5.253.d:
रूपमेवंविधं दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्माद्या देवतागणाः ..
तुष्टुवुः परया भक्त्या तेजोभूषितलोचनम् .. 93 ..
5.253.m: Beholding such a form, the hosts of deities headed by Brahmā / praised with supreme devotion the one whose eyes were adorned with splendor:

5.253.s:
tvameko bhagavānsarvavyāpakaḥ sarvadehinām ..
pitṛvadrakṣako'si tvaṃ mātā tvaṃ jīvasaṃjñakaḥ .. 94 ..
5.253.d:
त्वमेको भगवान्सर्वव्यापकः सर्वदेहिनाम् ..
पितृवद्रक्षकोऽसि त्वं माता त्वं जीवसंज्ञकः .. 94 ..
5.253.m: "You alone are the Lord, the all-pervading among all embodied beings; / like a father you are the protector, you are the mother, named as the individual soul.

5.253.s:
sākṣī viśvasya bījaṃ tvaṃ brahmāṃḍavaśakārakaḥ ..
utpadyaṃte vilīyaṃte tvayi brahmāṃḍakoṭayaḥ .. 95 ..
5.253.d:
साक्षी विश्वस्य बीजं त्वं ब्रह्मांडवशकारकः ..
उत्पद्यंते विलीयंते त्वयि ब्रह्मांडकोटयः .. 95 ..
5.253.m: You are the witness, the seed of the universe, the subduer of the cosmic egg; / millions of cosmic eggs arise and dissolve in you,

5.253.s:
ūrmayaḥ sāgare nityaṃ salile budbudā yathā ..
ahaṃ kadā citte netrātkadācittava bhālataḥ .. 96 ..
5.253.d:
ऊर्मयः सागरे नित्यं सलिले बुद्बुदा यथा ..
अहं कदा चित्ते नेत्रात्कदाचित्तव भालतः .. 96 ..
5.253.m: like waves constantly in the ocean, or bubbles in water. / Sometimes [I, Brahmā, arise] from your eye, sometimes from your forehead,

5.253.s:
kvacitsaṃge śivādevyā prāhurbhūtvā sṛje jagat ..
tavājñākariṇaḥ sarve vayaṃ brahmādayaḥ surāḥ .. 97 ..
5.253.d:
क्वचित्संगे शिवादेव्या प्राहुर्भूत्वा सृजे जगत् ..
तवाज्ञाकरिणः सर्वे वयं ब्रह्मादयः सुराः .. 97 ..
5.253.m: and sometimes, in union with the goddess Śivā, having manifested, I create the world. / We, the gods headed by Brahmā, are all doers of your command.

5.253.s:
anaṃtavaibhavo'naṃto'naṃtadhāmā'syanaṃtakaḥ ..
anaṃtaḥ sarvabhaṃgāya kuruṣe rūpamadbhutam .. 98 ..
5.253.d:
अनंतवैभवोऽनंतोऽनंतधामाऽस्यनंतकः ..
अनंतः सर्वभंगाय कुरुषे रूपमद्भुतम् .. 98 ..
5.253.m: You are of infinite majesty, endless, of infinite abode, limitless; / boundless, you assume a wondrous form for the destruction of all.

5.253.s:
bhavāni tvaṃ bhayaṃ nityamaśivānāṃ pavitrakṛt ..
śivā nāmapi dātrī tvaṃ tapasāmapi tvaṃ phalam 99 ..
5.253.d:
भवानि त्वं भयं नित्यमशिवानां पवित्रकृत् ..
शिवा नामपि दात्री त्वं तपसामपि त्वं फलम् 99 ..
5.253.m: O Bhavānī, you are fear constantly, making pure the uninauspicious; / you are the giver of auspicious things, and you are the fruit of austerities.

5.253.s:
yaḥ śivaḥ sa svayaṃ viṣṇuryo viṣṇuḥ sa sadāśivaḥ ..
ityabhedamatirjātā svalpā nastvatprasādataḥ.. .. 6.254.100 ..
yatkiṃcicca jagatyasmindṛśyate śrūyate'pi vā ..
madhye bahiśca tatsarvaṃ trayaṃ vyāpya sthitā yadā .. 1 ..
jagatpūjye sureśāni jagadvaṃdye tathāṃbike ..
prasādaṃ kuru deveśi deveśa praṇatā vayam .. 2 ..
ityuktvā tridaśāḥ sarve hṛṣṭā jagmuryathāgatam .. 3 ..
5.253.d:
यः शिवः स स्वयं विष्णुर्यो विष्णुः स सदाशिवः ..
इत्यभेदमतिर्जाता स्वल्पा नस्त्वत्प्रसादतः.. .. 6.254.100 ..
यत्किंचिच्च जगत्यस्मिन्दृश्यते श्रूयतेऽपि वा ..
मध्ये बहिश्च तत्सर्वं त्रयं व्याप्य स्थिता यदा .. 1 ..
जगत्पूज्ये सुरेशानि जगद्वंद्ये तथांबिके ..
प्रसादं कुरु देवेशि देवेश प्रणता वयम् .. 2 ..
इत्युक्त्वा त्रिदशाः सर्वे हृष्टा जग्मुर्यथागतम् .. 3 ..
5.253.m:
He who is Śiva is himself Viṣṇu; he who is Viṣṇu is Sadāśiva. / Thus the awareness of non-difference has arisen, in some small measure, in us through your grace.
Whatever is seen or heard in this world, / having pervaded all of that within and without, when you abide,
O one worshipped by the world, ruler of the gods, praised by the world, and Ambikā! / Grant your favor, O queen of the gods, O Lord of gods! We are bowed down [before you]."
Having spoken thus, all the thirty gods, delighted, departed as they had come.

5.253.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
taddivyarūpamatulaṃ bhuvi ye manuṣyāḥ saṃsārasāgarasamuttaraṇaikapotam ..
saṃcintayaṃti manasā hṛtakilbiṣāste brahmasvarūpamanuyāṃti vimuktasaṃgāḥ .. ..104..
5.253.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
तद्दिव्यरूपमतुलं भुवि ये मनुष्याः संसारसागरसमुत्तरणैकपोतम् ..
संचिन्तयंति मनसा हृतकिल्बिषास्ते ब्रह्मस्वरूपमनुयांति विमुक्तसंगाः .. ..104..
5.253.m: Gālava said: / "Those mortals on earth who reflect in their minds upon that divine, matchless form, / the sole boat for crossing the ocean of worldly existence, / with sins removed and attachments relinquished, attain the nature of the absolute."

5.253.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsya māhātmye haratāṃḍavanarttanavarṇanaṃnāma catuḥpañcāśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 254 ..
5.253.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्य माहात्म्ये हरतांडवनर्त्तनवर्णनंनाम चतुःपञ्चाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 254 ..
5.253.m: Thus ends the two hundred fifty-fourth chapter, named 'Description of Hara's Tāṇḍava Dance', in the Cāturmāsya-māhātmya within the narrative of Śeṣaśāyin, in the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.254.s:
gālava uvāca .. ..
evaṃ te labdhaśāpāśca pārvatīśāpa pīḍitāḥ ..
anapatyā babhūvuśca tathā ca pratimānavāḥ .. 1 ..
5.254.d:
गालव उवाच .. ..
एवं ते लब्धशापाश्च पार्वतीशाप पीडिताः ..
अनपत्या बभूवुश्च तथा च प्रतिमानवाः .. 1 ..
5.254.m: Gālava said: / In this way, having incurred the curse and afflicted by Pārvatī's curse, / they became childless, and likewise every man [among them].

5.254.s:
śālagrāmastu gaṃḍakyāṃ narmadāyāṃ maheśvaraḥ ..
utpadyate svayaṃbhūśca tāvetau naiva kṛtrimau .. 2 ..
5.254.d:
शालग्रामस्तु गंडक्यां नर्मदायां महेश्वरः ..
उत्पद्यते स्वयंभूश्च तावेतौ नैव कृत्रिमौ .. 2 ..
5.254.m: The śālagrāma stone arises in the Gaṇḍakī river, and Maheśvara arises in the Narmadā, / self-manifest; both of these are entirely unartificial.

5.254.s:
caturviṃśatibhedena śālagrāmagato hariḥ ..
parīkṣyaḥ puruṣairnityamekarūpaḥ sadāśivaḥ .. 3 ..
5.254.d:
चतुर्विंशतिभेदेन शालग्रामगतो हरिः ..
परीक्ष्यः पुरुषैर्नित्यमेकरूपः सदाशिवः .. 3 ..
5.254.m: Hari, present in the śālagrāma stone in twenty-four varieties, / should be examined by men daily, whereas Sadāśiva has a single form.

5.254.s:
śālagrāmaśilā yatra gaṃḍakīvimale jale ..
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca brahmaṇaḥ padamāpnuyāt .. 4 ..
5.254.d:
शालग्रामशिला यत्र गंडकीविमले जले ..
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च ब्रह्मणः पदमाप्नुयात् .. 4 ..
5.254.m: Where there is a śālagrāma stone in the pure waters of the Gaṇḍakī river, / bathing and drinking there, one attains the state of Brahman.

5.254.s:
tāṃ pūjayitvā vidhivadgaṃḍakīsaṃbhavāṃ śilām ..
yogīśvaro viśuddhātmā jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 5 ..
5.254.d:
तां पूजयित्वा विधिवद्गंडकीसंभवां शिलाम् ..
योगीश्वरो विशुद्धात्मा जायते नात्र संशयः .. 5 ..
5.254.m: Worshipping that stone born from the Gaṇḍakī river according to rule, / one becomes a master of yoga of purified self; of this there is no doubt.

5.254.s:
etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'hamiha tvayā ..
yathā haro vipraśāpaṃ prāptavāṃstanniśāmaya .. 6 ..
5.254.d:
एतत्ते कथितं सर्वं यत्पृष्टोऽहमिह त्वया ..
यथा हरो विप्रशापं प्राप्तवांस्तन्निशामय .. 6 ..
5.254.m: All this has been told to you, regarding what I was asked here by you. / Now hear how Hara incurred a curse from the brahmins.

5.254.s:
yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyā vācyamānāmimāṃ kathām ..
girīśanṛtyasaṃbandhāmumādehārddhavarṇitām .. 7 ..
5.254.d:
यः शृणोति नरो भक्त्या वाच्यमानामिमां कथाम् ..
गिरीशनृत्यसंबन्धामुमादेहार्द्धवर्णिताम् .. 7 ..
5.254.m: A man who hears with devotion this narrative being recited, / concerning the dance of the Lord of the Mountains and describing half of Umā's body,

5.254.s:
brahmaṇaḥ stutisaṃyuktāṃ sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim ..
ślokārddhaṃ ślokapādaṃ vā samastaṃ ślokameva vā .. 8 ..
5.254.d:
ब्रह्मणः स्तुतिसंयुक्तां स गच्छेत्परमां गतिम् ..
श्लोकार्द्धं श्लोकपादं वा समस्तं श्लोकमेव वा .. 8 ..
5.254.m: accompanied by praise from Brahmā, shall attain the highest goal. / Reading half a verse, a quarter of a verse, or an entire verse,

5.254.s:
yaḥ paṭhedavirodhena māyāmānavivarjitaḥ ..
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati .. 9 ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa paṭhañchṛṇvannarottamaḥ ..
labhate ciṃtitāṃ siddhiṃ dhanaputrādisaṃvṛtaḥ..6.255.1...
5.254.d:
यः पठेदविरोधेन मायामानविवर्जितः ..
स याति परमं स्थानं यत्र गत्वा न शोचति .. 9 ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण पठञ्छृण्वन्नरोत्तमः ..
लभते चिंतितां सिद्धिं धनपुत्रादिसंवृतः..6.255.1...
5.254.m:
whoever recites it without conflict, free from deceit and pride, / goes to the supreme abode, having reached which he grieves no more.
Especially during the Cāturmāsya, reciting or hearing it, the best among men / obtains desired accomplishment, surrounded by wealth, sons, and the like.

5.254.s:
yathā brahmādayo devā gītavādyābhiyogataḥ ..
parāṃ siddhi mavāpuste durgāśivasamīpataḥ .. 11 ..
5.254.d:
यथा ब्रह्मादयो देवा गीतवाद्याभियोगतः ..
परां सिद्धि मवापुस्ते दुर्गाशिवसमीपतः .. 11 ..
5.254.m: Just as the gods beginning with Brahmā, through the application of singing and instrumental music, / attained supreme accomplishment in the presence of Durgā and Śiva.

5.254.s:
varṣākāle ca saṃprāpte bhaktiyoge janārdane ..
maheśvare'tha durgāyāṃ na bhūyaḥ stanapo bhavet .. 12 ..
5.254.d:
वर्षाकाले च संप्राप्ते भक्तियोगे जनार्दने ..
महेश्वरेऽथ दुर्गायां न भूयः स्तनपो भवेत् .. 12 ..
5.254.m: And when the rainy season arrives, through the discipline of devotion to Janārdana, / to Maheśvara, and to Durgā, one shall not suckle a breast again.

5.254.s:
gaṇeśasya sadā kuryāccāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
pūjāṃ manuṣyo lābhārthaṃ yatno lābhaprado hi saḥ ..13..
5.254.d:
गणेशस्य सदा कुर्याच्चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
पूजां मनुष्यो लाभार्थं यत्नो लाभप्रदो हि सः ..13..
5.254.m: One should always perform worship of Gaṇeśa, especially in the Cāturmāsya, / for the sake of benefit, for that effort indeed bestows benefit.

5.254.s:
sūryo nīrogatāṃ dadyādbhaktyā yaiḥ pūjyate hi saḥ..
cāturmāsye samāyāte viśeṣaphalado nṛṇām .. 14 ..
5.254.d:
सूर्यो नीरोगतां दद्याद्भक्त्या यैः पूज्यते हि सः..
चातुर्मास्ये समायाते विशेषफलदो नृणाम् .. 14 ..
5.254.m: Sūrya bestows freedom from disease on those by whom he is worshipped with devotion; / when the Cāturmāsya has arrived, he bestows special fruit upon men.

5.254.s:
idaṃ hi paṃcāyatanaṃ sevyate gṛhamedhibhiḥ ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa sevitaṃ ciṃtitapradam .. 15 ..
5.254.d:
इदं हि पंचायतनं सेव्यते गृहमेधिभिः ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण सेवितं चिंतितप्रदम् .. 15 ..
5.254.m: This pañcāyatana is indeed served by householders; / served especially during the Cāturmāsya, it grants what is desired.

5.254.s:
śālagrāmagataṃ viṣṇuṃ yaḥ pūjayati nityadā ..
dvāravatīcakraśilāsahitaṃ mokṣadāyakam .. 16 ..
5.254.d:
शालग्रामगतं विष्णुं यः पूजयति नित्यदा ..
द्वारवतीचक्रशिलासहितं मोक्षदायकम् .. 16 ..
5.254.m: He who always worships Viṣṇu situated in the śālagrāma stone, / accompanied by the discus stone of Dvāravatī, receives liberation.

5.254.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa darśanādapi muktidam ..
yasminstute stutaṃ sarvaṃ pūjite pūjitaṃ jagat .. 17 ..
5.254.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण दर्शनादपि मुक्तिदम् ..
यस्मिन्स्तुते स्तुतं सर्वं पूजिते पूजितं जगत् .. 17 ..
5.254.m: Especially in the Cāturmāsya, it grants liberation even by its sight; / when he is praised, all is praised; when he is worshipped, the whole world is worshipped.

5.254.s:
pūjitaḥ paṭhito dhyātaḥ smṛto vai kaluṣāpahaḥ ..
śālagrāme kiṃ punaryacchālagrāmagato hariḥ .. 18 ..
5.254.d:
पूजितः पठितो ध्यातः स्मृतो वै कलुषापहः ..
शालग्रामे किं पुनर्यच्छालग्रामगतो हरिः .. 18 ..
5.254.m: Worshipped, recited, meditated upon, remembered, he indeed removes defilement; / what more [can be said] of the śālagrāma stone, since Hari is present in the śālagrāma?

5.254.s:
punarhi harinaivedyaṃ phalaṃ cāpi dhṛtaṃ jalam ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa śālagrāmagataṃ śubham .. 19 ..
5.254.d:
पुनर्हि हरिनैवेद्यं फलं चापि धृतं जलम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण शालग्रामगतं शुभम् .. 19 ..
5.254.m: Moreover, offering to Hari food, fruit, and held water, / especially during the Cāturmāsya to that which is situated in the śālagrāma, is auspicious.

5.254.s:
tilāḥ punaṃtyarpitāśca śālagrāmasya śūdraja ..
cātumāsye viśeṣeṇa naraṃ bhaktyā samanvitam .. 6.255.20 ..
5.254.d:
तिलाः पुनंत्यर्पिताश्च शालग्रामस्य शूद्रज ..
चातुमास्ये विशेषेण नरं भक्त्या समन्वितम् .. 6.255.20 ..
5.254.m: Sesame seeds offered to the śālagrāma stone, O Śūdraja, / purify a man endowed with devotion, especially during the Cāturmāsya.

5.254.s:
sa lakṣmīsahito nityaṃ dhanadhānyasamanvitaḥ ..
mahābhāgyavatāṃ gehe jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..21..
5.254.d:
स लक्ष्मीसहितो नित्यं धनधान्यसमन्वितः ..
महाभाग्यवतां गेहे जायते नात्र संशयः ..21..
5.254.m: He, always accompanied by Lakṣmī and endowed with wealth and grain, / is born in the home of the very fortunate; of this there is no doubt.

5.254.s:
sa lakṣmīsahito viṣṇurvijñeyo nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
taṃ pūjayenmahābhaktyā sthirā lakṣmīrgṛhe bhavet .. 22 ..
5.254.d:
स लक्ष्मीसहितो विष्णुर्विज्ञेयो नात्र संशयः ..
तं पूजयेन्महाभक्त्या स्थिरा लक्ष्मीर्गृहे भवेत् .. 22 ..
5.254.m: That Viṣṇu should be known as accompanied by Lakṣmī; of this there is no doubt; / one should worship him with great devotion, and stable fortune will remain in his house.

5.254.s:
tāvaddaridratā loke tāvadgarjati pātakam ..
tāvatkleśāḥ śarīre'sminna yāvatpūjayeddharim .. 23 ..
5.254.d:
तावद्दरिद्रता लोके तावद्गर्जति पातकम् ..
तावत्क्लेशाः शरीरेऽस्मिन्न यावत्पूजयेद्धरिम् .. 23 ..
5.254.m: Poverty persists in the world so long, wickedness roars so long, / and afflictions remain in this body so long, as one does not worship Hari.

5.254.s:
sa eva pūjyate yatra paṃcakrośaṃ pavitrakam ..
karoti sakalaṃ kṣetraṃ na tavā'śubhasaṃbhavaḥ .. 24 ..
5.254.d:
स एव पूज्यते यत्र पंचक्रोशं पवित्रकम् ..
करोति सकलं क्षेत्रं न तवाऽशुभसंभवः .. 24 ..
5.254.m: Where he alone is worshipped, he makes pure the entire sacred field / for five krośas; there no occurrence of inauspiciousness can exist for you.

5.254.s:
etadeva mahābhāgyametadevamahātapaḥ ..
eṣa eva paro mokṣo yatra lakṣmīśapūjanam .. 25 ..
5.254.d:
एतदेव महाभाग्यमेतदेवमहातपः ..
एष एव परो मोक्षो यत्र लक्ष्मीशपूजनम् .. 25 ..
5.254.m: This alone is great fortune, this alone is great austerity, / this alone is supreme liberation: where the worship of the Lord of Lakṣmī takes place.

5.254.s:
śaṃkhaśca dakṣiṇāvartto lakṣmīnārāyaṇātmakaḥ ..
tulasī kṛṣṇasāro'tra yatra dvāravatī śilā ..
tatra śrīrvijayo viṣṇurmuktirevaṃ catuṣṭayam.. 26 ..
5.254.d:
शंखश्च दक्षिणावर्त्तो लक्ष्मीनारायणात्मकः ..
तुलसी कृष्णसारोऽत्र यत्र द्वारवती शिला ..
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो विष्णुर्मुक्तिरेवं चतुष्टयम्.. 26 ..
5.254.m: The conch coiling clockwise, identical with Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, / tulasī, and the black antelope [skin] are where the Dvāravatī stone is; / there reside Śrī, victory, Viṣṇu, and liberation—these four.

5.254.s:
lakṣmīnārāyaṇe pūjāṃ vidhāturmanujasya tu ..
dadāti puṇyamatulaṃ mukto bhavati tatkṣaṇāt .. 27 ..
5.254.d:
लक्ष्मीनारायणे पूजां विधातुर्मनुजस्य तु ..
ददाति पुण्यमतुलं मुक्तो भवति तत्क्षणात् .. 27 ..
5.254.m: For a mortal who performs worship unto Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, / it bestows incomparable merit, and he is liberated at that very moment.

5.254.s: cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa pūjyo lakṣmīyuto hariḥ .. 28 ..
5.254.d: चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण पूज्यो लक्ष्मीयुतो हरिः .. 28 ..
5.254.m: Especially during the Cāturmāsya, Hari accompanied by Lakṣmī is to be worshipped.

5.254.s:
kurvatastasya devasya dhyānaṃ kalmaṣanāśanam ..
tulasīmañjarībhiśca pūjito janmanāśanaḥ .. 29 ..
5.254.d:
कुर्वतस्तस्य देवस्य ध्यानं कल्मषनाशनम् ..
तुलसीमञ्जरीभिश्च पूजितो जन्मनाशनः .. 29 ..
5.254.m: When one meditates upon that god, [the meditation] destroys impurities; / worshipped with tulasī blossoms, he destroys [future] births.

5.254.s: pūjito bilvapatreṇa cāturmāsye'ghahṛttamaḥ .. 6.255.30 ..
5.254.d: पूजितो बिल्वपत्रेण चातुर्मास्येऽघहृत्तमः .. 6.255.30 ..
5.254.m: Worshipped with a bilva leaf during the Cāturmāsya, he is the foremost remover of sin.

5.254.s:
sarvaprayatnena sa eva sevyo yo vyāpya viśvaṃ jagatāmadhīśaḥ ..
kāle sṛjatyatti ca helayā vā taṃ prāpya bhakto na hi sīdatīti .. 31 ..
5.254.d:
सर्वप्रयत्नेन स एव सेव्यो यो व्याप्य विश्वं जगतामधीशः ..
काले सृजत्यत्ति च हेलया वा तं प्राप्य भक्तो न हि सीदतीति .. 31 ..
5.254.m: With every effort, he alone should be served who, having pervaded the universe, is the sovereign of the worlds; / in due time he creates and consumes with effortless play; having reached him, a devotee never sinks down.

5.254.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye lakṣmīnārāyaṇamahimavarṇanaṃnāma pañcapañcāśaduttaradviśatatamoadhyāyaḥ .. 255 ..
5.254.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये लक्ष्मीनारायणमहिमवर्णनंनाम पञ्चपञ्चाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोअध्यायः .. 255 ..
5.254.m: Thus ends the two hundred fifty-fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa', in the Cāturmāsya-māhātmya within the narrative of Śeṣaśāyin, in the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.255.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
ekadā bhagavānrudraḥ kailāsaśikhare sthitaḥ ..
dadhāra paramāṃ lakṣmīmumayā sahitaḥ kila .. 1 ..
5.255.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
एकदा भगवान्रुद्रः कैलासशिखरे स्थितः ..
दधार परमां लक्ष्मीमुमया सहितः किल .. 1 ..
5.255.m: Gālava said: / Once, the blessed Rudra, residing on the peak of Kailāsa, / possessed supreme glory together with Umā.

5.255.s:
gaṇānāṃ koṭayastisrastaṃ yadā paryavārayan ..
vīrabāhurvīrabhadro vīrasenaśca bhṛṅgirāṭ .. 2 ..
5.255.d:
गणानां कोटयस्तिस्रस्तं यदा पर्यवारयन् ..
वीरबाहुर्वीरभद्रो वीरसेनश्च भृङ्गिराट् .. 2 ..
5.255.m: When thirty million gaṇas surrounded him: / Vīrabāhu, Vīrabhadra, Vīrasena, and King Bhṛṅgin,

5.255.s:
rucistuṭistathā nandī puṣpadantastathotkaṭaḥ ..
vikaṭaḥ kaṇṭakaścaiva haraḥ keśo vighaṃṭakaḥ .. 3 ..
5.255.d:
रुचिस्तुटिस्तथा नन्दी पुष्पदन्तस्तथोत्कटः ..
विकटः कण्टकश्चैव हरः केशो विघंटकः .. 3 ..
5.255.m: Ruci, Tuṭi, as well as Nandī, Puṣpadanta, and Utkaṭa, / Vikaṭa, and Kaṇṭaka, Hara, Keśa, Vighaṇṭaka,

5.255.s:
mālādharaḥ pāśadharaḥ śṛṅgī ca naranastathā ..
puṇyotkaṭaḥ śālibhadro mahābhadro vibhadrakaḥ .. 4 ..
5.255.d:
मालाधरः पाशधरः शृङ्गी च नरनस्तथा ..
पुण्योत्कटः शालिभद्रो महाभद्रो विभद्रकः .. 4 ..
5.255.m: Mālādhara, Pāśadhara, Śṛṅgin, and also Narana, / Puṇyotkaṭa, Śālibhadra, Mahābhadra, Vibhadraka,

5.255.s:
kaṇapaḥ kālapaḥ kālo dhanapo raktalocanaḥ ..
vikaṭāsyo bhadrakaśca dīrghajihvo virocanaḥ .. 5 ..
5.255.d:
कणपः कालपः कालो धनपो रक्तलोचनः ..
विकटास्यो भद्रकश्च दीर्घजिह्वो विरोचनः .. 5 ..
5.255.m: Kaṇapa, Kālapa, Kāla, Dhanapa, Raktalocana, / Vikaṭāsya, Bhadraka, Dīrghajihva, Virocana,

5.255.s:
pārado ghanado dhvāṃkṣī haṃsakrī narakastathā ..
paṃcaśīrṣastriśīrṣaśca kroḍadaṃṣṭro mahādbhuta .. 6 ..
5.255.d:
पारदो घनदो ध्वांक्षी हंसक्री नरकस्तथा ..
पंचशीर्षस्त्रिशीर्षश्च क्रोडदंष्ट्रो महाद्भुत .. 6 ..
5.255.m: Pārada, Ghanada, Dhvāṅkṣin, Haṃsakrin, and Naraka, / Pañcaśīrṣa, Triśīrṣa, Kroḍadaṃṣṭra, Mahādbhuta,

5.255.s:
siṃhavaktro vṛṣahanuḥ pracaṇḍastuṃḍireva ca ..
ete cānye ca bahavastadā bhavasamīpagāḥ .. 7 ..
5.255.d:
सिंहवक्त्रो वृषहनुः प्रचण्डस्तुंडिरेव च ..
एते चान्ये च बहवस्तदा भवसमीपगाः .. 7 ..
5.255.m: Siṃhavaktra, Vṛṣahanu, Pracaṇḍa, and Tuṇḍi— / these and many others were then gathered near Bhava.

5.255.s:
mahādeva jayetyuccairbhadrakālīsamanvitāḥ ..
bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ samūhā yasya vallabhāḥ ..8..
5.255.d:
महादेव जयेत्युच्चैर्भद्रकालीसमन्विताः ..
भूतप्रेतपिशाचानां समूहा यस्य वल्लभाः ..8..
5.255.m: Accompanied by Bhadrakālī, loudly crying 'Victory to Mahādeva!', / they to whom the hosts of bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas are dear,

5.255.s:
astuvaṃstaṃ samīpasthā vasante samupāgate ..
vanarājirvibhāti sma navakorakaśobhitā .. 9 ..
5.255.d:
अस्तुवंस्तं समीपस्था वसन्ते समुपागते ..
वनराजिर्विभाति स्म नवकोरकशोभिता .. 9 ..
5.255.m: standing nearby, praised him. When spring had arrived, / the rows of forest trees shone, adorned with fresh buds.
