5.255.s:
dakṣiṇānilasaṃsparśaḥ kavīnāṃ sukhakṛdbabhau ..
viyogihṛdayākarṣī kiṃśukaḥ puṣpaśobhitaḥ .. .. 6.256.10 ..
5.255.d:
दक्षिणानिलसंस्पर्शः कवीनां सुखकृद्बभौ ..
वियोगिहृदयाकर्षी किंशुकः पुष्पशोभितः .. .. 6.256.10 ..
5.255.m: The touch of the southern breeze shone forth, causing delight to poets; / the kiṃśuka tree, adorned with blossoms, tugged at the hearts of separated lovers.

5.255.s:
dvandvādivikriyābhāvaṃ cikrīḍuśca samaṃtataḥ ..
tasminvigāḍhe samaye manasyunmādake tathā .. 11 ..
5.255.d:
द्वन्द्वादिविक्रियाभावं चिक्रीडुश्च समंततः ..
तस्मिन्विगाढे समये मनस्युन्मादके तथा .. 11 ..
5.255.m: They engaged in sports on all sides, manifesting affections of couples and the like, / in that deep season that thus intoxicated the mind.

5.255.s:
naṃdī daṃḍadharaḥ saṃjñāṃ dṛṣṭvā cakre haro paraḥ..
alaṃ cāpaladoṣeṇa tapaḥ kurvaṃtu bho gaṇāḥ .. 12 ..
5.255.d:
नंदी दंडधरः संज्ञां दृष्ट्वा चक्रे हरो परः..
अलं चापलदोषेण तपः कुर्वंतु भो गणाः .. 12 ..
5.255.m: Seeing this, Nandī, holding his staff, gave a sign, and another Hara [said]: / “Enough with the fault of fickleness! O attendants, perform austerity!”

5.255.s:
tadā sarve vanamapi bhūkāṃḍajamabhūtpunaḥ ..
gaṇāste tapa ātasthurdṛṣṭvā kāntiṃvasantajām .. 13 ..
5.255.d:
तदा सर्वे वनमपि भूकांडजमभूत्पुनः ..
गणास्ते तप आतस्थुर्दृष्ट्वा कान्तिंवसन्तजाम् .. 13 ..
5.255.m: Then the whole forest again became rooted in the earth; / seeing the beauty born of spring, those attendants undertook austerity.

5.255.s:
tataḥ sā viśvajananī pārvatī prāha śaṃkaram ..
iyaṃ te karagā nityamakṣamālā maheśvara .. 14 ..
5.255.d:
ततः सा विश्वजननी पार्वती प्राह शंकरम् ..
इयं ते करगा नित्यमक्षमाला महेश्वर .. 14 ..
5.255.m: Then Pārvatī, mother of the universe, said to Śaṃkara: / “This rosary is constantly in your hand, O Maheśvara.

5.255.s:
tvayā kiṃ japyate deva saṃdehayati me manaḥ ..
tvamekaḥ sarva bhūtānāmādikṛtsakaleśvaraḥ .. 15 ..
5.255.d:
त्वया किं जप्यते देव संदेहयति मे मनः ..
त्वमेकः सर्व भूतानामादिकृत्सकलेश्वरः .. 15 ..
5.255.m: What is being chanted by you, O lord? My mind is perplexed. / You alone are the first maker of all beings, the lord of all.

5.255.s:
na mātā na pitā baṃdhustava jātirna kaścana ..
ahaṃ tava paraṃ kiṃcidvedmi nāstīti kiṃcana .. 16 ..
5.255.d:
न माता न पिता बंधुस्तव जातिर्न कश्चन ..
अहं तव परं किंचिद्वेद्मि नास्तीति किंचन .. 16 ..
5.255.m: You have no mother, no father, no kinsman, and no caste. / I know of nothing beyond you; nothing exists [higher].

5.255.s:
śrameṇa tvaṃ samāyukto śvāsocchvāsaparāyaṇaḥ..
japannapi mahābhaktyā dṛśyase tvaṃ mayā sadā ..17..
5.255.d:
श्रमेण त्वं समायुक्तो श्वासोच्छ्वासपरायणः..
जपन्नपि महाभक्त्या दृश्यसे त्वं मया सदा ..17..
5.255.m: Engaged with exertion, devoted to in-breathing and out-breathing, / you are always seen by me chanting with great devotion.

5.255.s:
tvattaḥparataraṃ kicidyattvaṃ dhyāyasi cetasā ..
tanme kathaya deveśa yadyahaṃ dayitā tava.. 18 ..
5.255.d:
त्वत्तःपरतरं किचिद्यत्त्वं ध्यायसि चेतसा ..
तन्मे कथय देवेश यद्यहं दयिता तव.. 18 ..
5.255.m: Tell me, O Lord of Gods, if I am dear to you, / what it is higher than you that you meditate upon with your mind.”

5.255.s:
iti spṛṣṭastadā śaṃbhuruvāca harisevakaḥ ..
harernāmasahasrāṇāṃ sāraṃ dhyāyāmi nityaśaḥ .. 19 ..
5.255.d:
इति स्पृष्टस्तदा शंभुरुवाच हरिसेवकः ..
हरेर्नामसहस्राणां सारं ध्यायामि नित्यशः .. 19 ..
5.255.m: Being thus questioned then, Śambhu, the servant of Hari, said: / “I constantly meditate upon the essence of Hari’s thousand names.

5.255.s:
japāmi rāmanāmāṃkamavātaraṃ(?) sasaptamam..
caturviśatisaṃkhyākānprādurbhāvānharerguṇān .. 6.256.20 ..
5.255.d:
जपामि रामनामांकमवातरं(?) ससप्तमम्..
चतुर्विशतिसंख्याकान्प्रादुर्भावान्हरेर्गुणान् .. 6.256.20 ..
5.255.m: I chant the sevenfold descent marked by the name of Rāma, / and the twenty-four manifestations and virtues of Hari.

5.255.s:
eteṣāmapi yatsāraṃ praṇavākhyaṃ mahatphalam ..
dvādaśākṣarasaṃyuktaṃ brahmarūpaṃ sanā tanam.. 21 ..
5.255.d:
एतेषामपि यत्सारं प्रणवाख्यं महत्फलम् ..
द्वादशाक्षरसंयुक्तं ब्रह्मरूपं सना तनम्.. 21 ..
5.255.m: And that which is the essence of these, called Praṇava, bearing great fruit, / united with twelve syllables, eternal, in the form of Brahman,

5.255.s:
akṣaratrayasaṃbaddhaṃ grāmatrayasamanvitam ..
sabiṃduṃ praṇavaṃ śaśvajjapāmi japamālayā .. 22 ..
5.255.d:
अक्षरत्रयसंबद्धं ग्रामत्रयसमन्वितम् ..
सबिंदुं प्रणवं शश्वज्जपामि जपमालया .. 22 ..
5.255.m: bound up with three syllables, endowed with three musical scales, / with the anusvāra—that Praṇava I constantly chant with a rosary.

5.255.s:
vedasāramidaṃ nityaṃ dvyakṣaraṃ satatodyatam ..
nirmalaṃ hyamṛtaṃ śāṃtaṃ sadūpamamṛtopamam .. 23 ..
5.255.d:
वेदसारमिदं नित्यं द्व्यक्षरं सततोद्यतम् ..
निर्मलं ह्यमृतं शांतं सदूपममृतोपमम् .. 23 ..
5.255.m: This eternal essence of the Vedas, of two syllables, ever active, / pure, indeed immortal, peaceful, having the form of existence, resembling nectar,

5.255.s:
kalātītaṃ nirvaśagaṃ nirvyāpāraṃ mahatparam ..
viśvādhāraṃ jaganmadhyaṃ koṭibrahmāṃḍabījakam.. 24 ..
5.255.d:
कलातीतं निर्वशगं निर्व्यापारं महत्परम् ..
विश्वाधारं जगन्मध्यं कोटिब्रह्मांडबीजकम्.. 24 ..
5.255.m: transcending parts, not subject to external control, without activity, the supreme great, / the support of the universe, the center of the world, the seed of crores of cosmic eggs,

5.255.s:
jaḍaṃ śuddhakriyaṃ vāpi niraṃjanaṃ niyāmakam ..
yajjñātvā mucyate kṣipraṃ ghorasaṃsārabaṃdhanāt .. 25 ..
5.255.d:
जडं शुद्धक्रियं वापि निरंजनं नियामकम् ..
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते क्षिप्रं घोरसंसारबंधनात् .. 25 ..
5.255.m: unconscious yet having pure activity, unstained, the regulator— / knowing which, one is swiftly liberated from the dreadful bond of saṃsāra.

5.255.s:
oṃkārasahitaṃ yacca dvādaśākṣarabījakam ..
japataḥ pāpakoṭīnāṃ dāvāgnitvaṃ prajāyate .. 26 ..
5.255.d:
ओंकारसहितं यच्च द्वादशाक्षरबीजकम् ..
जपतः पापकोटीनां दावाग्नित्वं प्रजायते .. 26 ..
5.255.m: And the twelve-syllabled seed-mantra accompanied by the sound ‘oṃ’— / for one who chants it, becomes a forest fire to crores of sins.

5.255.s:
etadeva paraṃ guhyametadeva paraṃ mahaḥ ..
etaddhi durlabhaṃ loke lokatrayavibhūṣaṇam.. 27 ..
5.255.d:
एतदेव परं गुह्यमेतदेव परं महः ..
एतद्धि दुर्लभं लोके लोकत्रयविभूषणम्.. 27 ..
5.255.m: This alone is the supreme secret; this alone is the supreme splendor; / this indeed is rare in the world, an ornament of the three worlds.

5.255.s:
prāpyate janmakoṭībhiḥ śubhāśubhavināśakam ..
etadeva paraṃ jñānaṃ dvādaśākṣaracintanam .. 28 ..
5.255.d:
प्राप्यते जन्मकोटीभिः शुभाशुभविनाशकम् ..
एतदेव परं ज्ञानं द्वादशाक्षरचिन्तनम् .. 28 ..
5.255.m: It is attained through crores of births; it destroys the auspicious and inauspicious. / This meditation on the twelve syllables is the supreme knowledge itself.

5.255.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa brahmadaṃ ciṃtitapradam ..
etadakṣarajaṃ stotraṃ yaḥ samāśrayate sadā .. 29 ..
5.255.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण ब्रह्मदं चिंतितप्रदम् ..
एतदक्षरजं स्तोत्रं यः समाश्रयते सदा .. 29 ..
5.255.m: Especially during Cāturmāsya, it grants Brahman and bestows what is thought upon. / Whoever constantly resorts to this hymn born of these syllables,

5.255.s:
manasā karmaṇā vācā tasya nāsti punarbhavaḥ ..
dvādaśākṣarasaṃyuktaṃ cakradvādaśabhūṣitam .. 6.256.30 ..
5.255.d:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा तस्य नास्ति पुनर्भवः ..
द्वादशाक्षरसंयुक्तं चक्रद्वादशभूषितम् .. 6.256.30 ..
5.255.m: in thought, word, and deed, has no rebirth. / Endowed with twelve syllables, adorned with twelve wheels,

5.255.s:
māsadvādaśanāmāni viṣṇoryo bhaktitatparaḥ ..
śālagrāmeṣu tānyuktvā nyasedaghaharāṇi ca .. 31 ..
5.255.d:
मासद्वादशनामानि विष्णोर्यो भक्तितत्परः ..
शालग्रामेषु तान्युक्त्वा न्यसेदघहराणि च .. 31 ..
5.255.m: one who is devoted to Viṣṇu, having recited those sin-destroying / twelve names of the months, should deposit them upon Śālagrāma stones.

5.255.s:
divasedivase tasya dvādaśāhaphalaṃ labhet ..
dvādaśākṣara māhātmyaṃ varṇituṃ naiva śakyate .. 32 ..
5.255.d:
दिवसेदिवसे तस्य द्वादशाहफलं लभेत् ..
द्वादशाक्षर माहात्म्यं वर्णितुं नैव शक्यते .. 32 ..
5.255.m: Day after day, he obtains the fruit of a twelve-day rite. / The majesty of the twelve syllables cannot indeed be described.

5.255.s:
jihvāsahasrairapi ca brahmaṇāpi na vāryate ..
mahāmantro hyayaṃ loke japyo dhyātaḥ stutastathā .. 33 ..
5.255.d:
जिह्वासहस्रैरपि च ब्रह्मणापि न वार्यते ..
महामन्त्रो ह्ययं लोके जप्यो ध्यातः स्तुतस्तथा .. 33 ..
5.255.m: Even with thousands of tongues, even by Brahmā, it cannot be exhausted. / For this great mantra in the world, when chanted, meditated upon, and praised,

5.255.s:
pāpahā sarvamāseṣu cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
idaṃ rahasyaṃ vedānāṃ purāṇānāmanekaśaḥ .. 34 ..
5.255.d:
पापहा सर्वमासेषु चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
इदं रहस्यं वेदानां पुराणानामनेकशः .. 34 ..
5.255.m: destroys sin in all months, especially during Cāturmāsya. / This is the secret of the Vedas and repeatedly of the Purāṇas

5.255.s:
smṛtīnāmapi sarvāsāṃ dvādaśākṣaracintanam..
ciṃtanādeva martyānāṃ siddhirbhavati hīpsitā .. 35 ..
5.255.d:
स्मृतीनामपि सर्वासां द्वादशाक्षरचिन्तनम्..
चिंतनादेव मर्त्यानां सिद्धिर्भवति हीप्सिता .. 35 ..
5.255.m: and of all the Smṛtis: meditation on the twelve syllables. / Indeed, through mere meditation, the desired perfection of mortals comes about.

5.255.s:
puṇyadānena yāmyena muktirbhavati śāśvatī ..
varṇaistathāśramaireva praṇavena samanvitaiḥ .. 36 ..
5.255.d:
पुण्यदानेन याम्येन मुक्तिर्भवति शाश्वती ..
वर्णैस्तथाश्रमैरेव प्रणवेन समन्वितैः .. 36 ..
5.255.m: Through the gift of merit, eternal liberation from [the realm of] Yama occurs. / By the castes and stages of life, endowed with Praṇava,

5.255.s:
japairdhyānaiḥ śamaparairmokṣaṃ yāsyeta niścitama ..
śūdrāṇāṃ cāpi nārīṇāṃ praṇavena vivarjitaḥ .. 37 ..
5.255.d:
जपैर्ध्यानैः शमपरैर्मोक्षं यास्येत निश्चितम ..
शूद्राणां चापि नारीणां प्रणवेन विवर्जितः .. 37 ..
5.255.m: through chants and meditations devoted to tranquility, liberation will certainly be attained. / But for Śūdras and women, it is devoid of Praṇava.

5.255.s:
prakṛtīnāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ na mantro dvādaśākṣaraḥ ..
na japo na tapaḥ kāryaṃ kāyakleśādviśuddhitā .. 38 ..
5.255.d:
प्रकृतीनां च सर्वासां न मन्त्रो द्वादशाक्षरः ..
न जपो न तपः कार्यं कायक्लेशाद्विशुद्धिता .. 38 ..
5.255.m: And for all ordinary people, the twelve-syllabled mantra is not prescribed; / no chanting and no austerity is to be performed—purification comes from bodily mortification,

5.255.s:
viprabhaktyā ca dānena viṣṇudhyānena siddhyati ..
tāsāṃ mantro rāmanāma dhyeyaḥ koṭyadhiko bhavet .. 39 ..
5.255.d:
विप्रभक्त्या च दानेन विष्णुध्यानेन सिद्ध्यति ..
तासां मन्त्रो रामनाम ध्येयः कोट्यधिको भवेत् .. 39 ..
5.255.m: and through devotion to brahmins, through giving, and through meditation on Viṣṇu, success is attained. / For them, the mantra to be meditated upon is the name of Rāma, which is worth more than a crore.

5.255.s:
rāmeti dvyakṣarajapaḥ sarvapāpāpanodakaḥ ..
gacchaṃstiṣṭhañchayāno vā manujo rāmakīrtanāt .. 6.256.40 ..
5.255.d:
रामेति द्व्यक्षरजपः सर्वपापापनोदकः ..
गच्छंस्तिष्ठञ्छयानो वा मनुजो रामकीर्तनात् .. 6.256.40 ..
5.255.m: Chanting the two syllables ‘Rāma’ removes all sins. / Walking, standing, or lying down, a mortal, through reciting Rāma,

5.255.s:
iha nirvartato yāti prānte harigaṇo bhavet ..
rāmeti dvyakṣaro mantro maṃtrakoṭiśatādhikaḥ .. 41 ..
5.255.d:
इह निर्वर्ततो याति प्रान्ते हरिगणो भवेत् ..
रामेति द्व्यक्षरो मन्त्रो मंत्रकोटिशताधिकः .. 41 ..
5.255.m: attains cessation in this world and becomes an attendant of Hari at the end. / The two-syllabled mantra ‘Rāma’ surpasses a hundred crores of mantras.

5.255.s:
sarvāsāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ ca kathitaḥ pāpanāśakaḥ ..
cāturmāsye'tha saṃprāpte so'pyanaṃtaphalapradaḥ .. 42 ..
5.255.d:
सर्वासां प्रकृतीनां च कथितः पापनाशकः ..
चातुर्मास्येऽथ संप्राप्ते सोऽप्यनंतफलप्रदः .. 42 ..
5.255.m: It is declared to destroy the sins of all ordinary people. / And when Cāturmāsya has arrived, it bestows infinite fruit.

5.255.s:
cāturmāsye mahāpuṇye labhyate bhaktitatparaiḥ ..
devavanniṣphalaṃ teṣāṃ yamalokasyasevanam .. 43 ..
5.255.d:
चातुर्मास्ये महापुण्ये लभ्यते भक्तितत्परैः ..
देववन्निष्फलं तेषां यमलोकस्यसेवनम् .. 43 ..
5.255.m: In the highly meritorious Cāturmāsya, it is obtained by those devoted to bhakti; / for them, attending the world of Yama becomes fruitless, like that of the gods.

5.255.s:
na rāmādadhikaṃ kiṃcitpaṭhanaṃ jagatītale ..
rāmanāmāśrayā ye vai na teṣāṃ yamayātanā .. 44 ..
5.255.d:
न रामादधिकं किंचित्पठनं जगतीतले ..
रामनामाश्रया ये वै न तेषां यमयातना .. 44 ..
5.255.m: There is no recitation on the surface of the earth greater than Rāma; / for those who take refuge in the name of Rāma, there is no torment by Yama.

5.255.s:
ye ca doṣā vighnakarā mṛtakā vigrahāśca ye ..
rāma nāmaiva vilayaṃ yāṃti nātra vicāraṇā .. 45 ..
5.255.d:
ये च दोषा विघ्नकरा मृतका विग्रहाश्च ये ..
राम नामैव विलयं यांति नात्र विचारणा .. 45 ..
5.255.m: Whatever faults cause obstacles, whatever impurities of death and conflicts there be, / they dissolve by the very name of Rāma; there is no doubt in this.

5.255.s:
ramate sarvabhūteṣu sthāvareṣu careṣu ca ..
antarātmasvarūpeṇa yacca rāmeti kathyate .. 46 .
5.255.d:
रमते सर्वभूतेषु स्थावरेषु चरेषु च ..
अन्तरात्मस्वरूपेण यच्च रामेति कथ्यते .. 46 .
5.255.m: He takes delight in all beings, both stationary and moving, / as the inner self, and that is why he is called Rāma.

5.255.s:
rāmeti matrarājo'yaṃ bhayavyādhiniṣūdakaḥ ..
raṇe vijayadaścāpi sarvakāryārthasādhakaḥ .. 47 ..
5.255.d:
रामेति मत्रराजोऽयं भयव्याधिनिषूदकः ..
रणे विजयदश्चापि सर्वकार्यार्थसाधकः .. 47 ..
5.255.m: This king of mantras, ‘Rāma’, destroys fear and disease; / it gives victory in battle and accomplishes all aims and objectives.

5.255.s:
sarvatīrthaphalaḥ prokto viprāṇāmapi kāmadaḥ ..
rāmacandreti rāmeti rāmeti samudāhṛtaḥ .. 48 ..
5.255.d:
सर्वतीर्थफलः प्रोक्तो विप्राणामपि कामदः ..
रामचन्द्रेति रामेति रामेति समुदाहृतः .. 48 ..
5.255.m: It is declared to grant the fruit of all sacred fords and fulfills desires even for brahmins. / It is proclaimed as ‘Rāmacandra’, as ‘Rāma’, as ‘Rāma’.

5.255.s:
dvyakṣaro mantrarājo'yaṃ sarvakāryakaro bhuvi ..
devā api pragāyaṃti rāmanāmaguṇākaram .. 49 ..
5.255.d:
द्व्यक्षरो मन्त्रराजोऽयं सर्वकार्यकरो भुवि ..
देवा अपि प्रगायंति रामनामगुणाकरम् .. 49 ..
5.255.m: This two-syllabled king of mantras accomplishes everything on earth. / Even the gods sing aloud the mine of virtues that is the name of Rāma.

5.255.s:
tasmāttvamapi deveśi rāmanāma sadā vada ..
rāmanāma japedyo vai mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 6.256.50 ..
5.255.d:
तस्मात्त्वमपि देवेशि रामनाम सदा वद ..
रामनाम जपेद्यो वै मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .. 6.256.50 ..
5.255.m: Therefore, O ruler of gods, you too should always utter the name of Rāma. / Whoever chants the name of Rāma is freed from all sins.

5.255.s:
sahasranāmajaṃ puṇyaṃ rāmanāmnaiva jāyate ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa tatpuṇyaṃ daśadhottaram .. 51 ..
5.255.d:
सहस्रनामजं पुण्यं रामनाम्नैव जायते ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण तत्पुण्यं दशधोत्तरम् .. 51 ..
5.255.m: The merit born of the thousand names arises from the name of Rāma alone. / Especially during Cāturmāsya, that merit is tenfold greater.

5.255.s: hīnajātiprajātānāṃ mahadahyati pātakam .. 52 ..
5.255.d: हीनजातिप्रजातानां महदह्यति पातकम् .. 52 ..
5.255.m: It burns away even the great sin of those born in low castes.

5.255.s:
rāmo hyayaṃ viśvamidaṃ samayaṃ svatejasā vyāpya janāṃtarātmanā ..
punāti janmāṃtarapātakāni sthūlāni sūkṣmāṇi kṣaṇācca dagdhvā .. 53 ..
5.255.d:
रामो ह्ययं विश्वमिदं समयं स्वतेजसा व्याप्य जनांतरात्मना ..
पुनाति जन्मांतरपातकानि स्थूलानि सूक्ष्माणि क्षणाच्च दग्ध्वा .. 53 ..
5.255.m: For this Rāma, pervading this universe entirely with his own splendor as the inner self of people, / having burned gross and subtle sins from other lives in an instant, purifies.

5.255.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye rāmanāmamahimavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭpaṃcāśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 256 ..
5.255.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये रामनाममहिमवर्णनं नाम षट्पंचाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 256 ..
5.255.m: Thus ends the two hundred fifty-sixth chapter, named "Description of the Greatness of the Name of Rāma," in the Greatness of the Cāturmāsya within the dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, in the account of the One Sleeping on Śeṣa, in the Greatness of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.256.s:
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
dvādaśākṣaramāhātmyaṃ mama vistarato vada ..
yathāvarṇaṃ yatphalaṃ ca yathā ca kriyate mayā .. 1 ..
5.256.d:
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
द्वादशाक्षरमाहात्म्यं मम विस्तरतो वद ..
यथावर्णं यत्फलं च यथा च क्रियते मया .. 1 ..
5.256.m:
Pārvatī said:
Tell me in detail the greatness of the twelve-syllable [mantra], / according to caste, its fruit, and how it is to be performed by me. (1)

5.256.s:
.. śrīmahādeva uvāca .. ..
dvijātīnāṃ sahoṃkārasahito dvādaśākṣaraḥ ..
strīśūdrāṇāṃ namaskārapūrvakaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ .. 2 ..
5.256.d:
.. श्रीमहादेव उवाच .. ..
द्विजातीनां सहोंकारसहितो द्वादशाक्षरः ..
स्त्रीशूद्राणां नमस्कारपूर्वकः समुदाहृतः .. 2 ..
5.256.m:
The glorious Mahādeva said:
The twelve-syllable [mantra] with the Praṇava is declared for the twice-born; / for women and Śūdras it is preceded by "namaḥ." (2)

5.256.s:
prakṛtīnāṃ rāmanāma saṃmato vā ṣaḍakṣaraḥ ..
so'pi praṇavahīnaḥ syātpurāṇasmṛtinirṇayaḥ .. 3 ..
5.256.d:
प्रकृतीनां रामनाम संमतो वा षडक्षरः ..
सोऽपि प्रणवहीनः स्यात्पुराणस्मृतिनिर्णयः .. 3 ..
5.256.m: For common people the name of Rāma is approved, or the six-syllable [mantra]; / that too must be devoid of the Praṇava: such is the determination of the Purāṇas and Smṛtis. (3)

5.256.s:
kramo'yaṃ sarvavarṇānāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ sadaiva hi ..
krameṇa rahito yastu karoti manujo japam ..
tasya prakupyati vibhurnarakādipradāyakaḥ .. 4 ..
5.256.d:
क्रमोऽयं सर्ववर्णानां प्रकृतीनां सदैव हि ..
क्रमेण रहितो यस्तु करोति मनुजो जपम् ..
तस्य प्रकुप्यति विभुर्नरकादिप्रदायकः .. 4 ..
5.256.m: This order is indeed prescribed for all castes and common people at all times. / But the mortal who recites the mantra disregarding the proper order— / against him the all-pervading Lord grows wrathful, consigning him to hell and the like. (4)

5.256.s:
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
mayā trimātrayā svāminsevyate jagadīśvaraḥ ..
rūpamasya kathaṃ jāne vacasāmapyagocaram .. 5 ..
5.256.d:
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
मया त्रिमात्रया स्वामिन्सेव्यते जगदीश्वरः ..
रूपमस्य कथं जाने वचसामप्यगोचरम् .. 5 ..
5.256.m:
Pārvatī said:
O Lord, by me with the three morae the Lord of the universe is served; / how may I know his form, which lies beyond the reach of words? (5)

5.256.s:
.. īśvara uvāca . ..
praṇavasyādhikāro na tavāsti varavarṇini ..
namo bhagavate vāsudevāyeti japaḥ sadā .. 6 ..
5.256.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच . ..
प्रणवस्याधिकारो न तवास्ति वरवर्णिनि ..
नमो भगवते वासुदेवायेति जपः सदा .. 6 ..
5.256.m:
Īśvara said:
You have no eligibility for the Praṇava, O fair-complexioned one. / Your perpetual recitation is "namo bhagavate vāsudevāya." (6)

5.256.s:
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
yadi sapraṇavaṃ dadyāddvādaśākṣaraciṃtanama ..
praṇave nādhikāro me kathaṃ bhavati dhūrjaṭe . 7 .. ..
5.256.d:
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
यदि सप्रणवं दद्याद्द्वादशाक्षरचिंतनम ..
प्रणवे नाधिकारो मे कथं भवति धूर्जटे . 7 .. ..
5.256.m:
Pārvatī said:
If meditation on the twelve-syllable [mantra] confers [merit] when accompanied by the Praṇava, / why do I have no eligibility for the Praṇava, O Dhūrjaṭi? (7)

5.256.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
praṇavaḥ sarvadevānāmādireṣa prakīrtitaḥ ..
brahmā viṣṇuḥ śivaścaiva vasaṃti dayitāyutāḥ .. 8 ..
5.256.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
प्रणवः सर्वदेवानामादिरेष प्रकीर्तितः ..
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः शिवश्चैव वसंति दयितायुताः .. 8 ..
5.256.m:
Īśvara said:
The Praṇava is declared to be the beginning of all the gods; / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva dwell [therein] together with their beloveds. (8)

5.256.s:
tatra sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarva tīrthāni bhāgaśaḥ ..
tiṣṭhaṃti sarvatīrthāni kaivalyaṃ brahma eva yaḥ ..9..
5.256.d:
तत्र सर्वाणि भूतानि सर्व तीर्थानि भागशः ..
तिष्ठंति सर्वतीर्थानि कैवल्यं ब्रह्म एव यः ..9..
5.256.m: There all beings and all sacred fords reside in their respective portions; / all sacred fords abide [there], which is Brahman itself, absolute liberation. (9)

5.256.s:
tasya yogyā tadā devi bhaviṣyasi yadā tapaḥ ..
cāturmāsye hariprītyai kariṣyasi śubhānane .. 6.257.10 ..
5.256.d:
तस्य योग्या तदा देवि भविष्यसि यदा तपः ..
चातुर्मास्ये हरिप्रीत्यै करिष्यसि शुभानने .. 6.257.10 ..
5.256.m: You will become eligible for it, O goddess, when you perform / austerity during the Cāturmāsya to please Hari, O fair-faced one. (10)

5.256.s:
tapasā prāpyate kāmastapasā ca mahatphalam ..
tapasā jāyate sarvaṃ tattapaḥ sulabhaṃ naraiḥ .. 11 ..
5.256.d:
तपसा प्राप्यते कामस्तपसा च महत्फलम् ..
तपसा जायते सर्वं तत्तपः सुलभं नरैः .. 11 ..
5.256.m: By austerity desire is attained, and by austerity great fruit [is won]; / through austerity everything comes to be, and such austerity is easily obtained by mortals. (11)

5.256.s:
yaśaḥ saubhāgyamatulaṃ kṣamāsatyādayo guṇāḥ ..
sulabhaṃ tapasā nityaṃ tapaścarttuṃ na śakyate .. 12 ..
5.256.d:
यशः सौभाग्यमतुलं क्षमासत्यादयो गुणाः ..
सुलभं तपसा नित्यं तपश्चर्त्तुं न शक्यते .. 12 ..
5.256.m: Fame, matchless fortune, forbearance, truth, and other virtues / are always easily won through austerity; yet austerity is difficult to practice. (12)

5.256.s:
yadā hi tapaso vṛddhistadā bhaktirharau bhavet ..
tadā hi tapaso hāniryadā bhaktiṃ vinā kṛtam .. 13 ..
5.256.d:
यदा हि तपसो वृद्धिस्तदा भक्तिर्हरौ भवेत् ..
तदा हि तपसो हानिर्यदा भक्तिं विना कृतम् .. 13 ..
5.256.m: Indeed, when austerity increases, then devotion to Hari arises; / and indeed there is loss of austerity when it is performed without devotion. (13)

5.256.s:
tāvattapāṃsi garjaṃti dehe'sminsatataṃ nṛṇām ..
yadā viṣṇuṃ smarennityaṃ jihvāgraṃ pāvanaṃ bhavet .. 14 ..
5.256.d:
तावत्तपांसि गर्जंति देहेऽस्मिन्सततं नृणाम् ..
यदा विष्णुं स्मरेन्नित्यं जिह्वाग्रं पावनं भवेत् .. 14 ..
5.256.m: Austerities roar continually in this body of mortals / only so long as one constantly remembers Viṣṇu, and the tip of the tongue becomes purified. (14)

5.256.s:
yathā pradīpe jvalite praṇaśyati mahattamaḥ ..
tathā hareḥ kathāyāṃ ca yāti pāpamanekadhā .. 15..
tasmātpārvati yatnena harau supte tapaḥ kuru ..
cāturmāsye'tha saṃprāpte praṇavena samanvitam .. 16 ..
5.256.d:
यथा प्रदीपे ज्वलिते प्रणश्यति महत्तमः ..
तथा हरेः कथायां च याति पापमनेकधा .. 15..
तस्मात्पार्वति यत्नेन हरौ सुप्ते तपः कुरु ..
चातुर्मास्येऽथ संप्राप्ते प्रणवेन समन्वितम् .. 16 ..
5.256.m: Just as dense darkness is destroyed when a lamp is lit, / even so manifold sin vanishes during the narration of Hari. (15) / Therefore, O Pārvatī, diligently practice austerity while Hari is asleep, / when the Cāturmāsya has arrived, together with the Praṇava. (16)

5.256.s:
viśuddhahṛdayā bhūtvā mantrarājamimaṃ japa. ..
sa eva bhagavāṃstuṣṭo dvādaśākṣarasaṃyutam .. 17 ..
5.256.d:
विशुद्धहृदया भूत्वा मन्त्रराजमिमं जप. ..
स एव भगवांस्तुष्टो द्वादशाक्षरसंयुतम् .. 17 ..
5.256.m: Having become pure of heart, recite this king of mantras; / and that Lord himself, being pleased, together with the twelve syllables, (17)

5.256.s:
pradāsyati paraṃ jñānaṃ brahmarūpamakhaṇḍitam .
brahmakalpāṃtakoṭīṣu japa tvaṃ dvādaśākṣaram .. 18 ..
5.256.d:
प्रदास्यति परं ज्ञानं ब्रह्मरूपमखण्डितम् .
ब्रह्मकल्पांतकोटीषु जप त्वं द्वादशाक्षरम् .. 18 ..
5.256.m: will bestow supreme knowledge, indivisible, in the form of Brahman. / Through crores of Brahma-kalpas, recite the twelve syllables. (18)

5.256.s:
mantrarājaṃ sapraṇavaṃ dhyāyetso'pi na paśyati ..
ityuktā sā taponiṣṭhā tapaścaritumāgatā .. 19 ..
5.256.d:
मन्त्रराजं सप्रणवं ध्यायेत्सोऽपि न पश्यति ..
इत्युक्ता सा तपोनिष्ठा तपश्चरितुमागता .. 19 ..
5.256.m: Even he who meditates on the king of mantras with the Praṇava does not see [him]. / Having been thus addressed, she, devoted to austerity, departed to practice austerity. (19)

5.256.s:
himācalasya śikhare cāturmāsye samāgate ..
brahmacaryavrataparā vasanatrayasaṃyutā .. 6.257.20 ..
5.256.d:
हिमाचलस्य शिखरे चातुर्मास्ये समागते ..
ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतपरा वसनत्रयसंयुता .. 6.257.20 ..
5.256.m: On the peak of the Himācala, when the Cāturmāsya had arrived, / dedicated to the vow of celibacy, wearing three garments, (20)

5.256.s:
prātarmadhye'parāhne ca dhyāyantī hariśaṃkaram ..
vapuryathā purā kṛṣṭaṃ pūjane śaṃkarasya ca .. 21 ..
5.256.d:
प्रातर्मध्येऽपराह्ने च ध्यायन्ती हरिशंकरम् ..
वपुर्यथा पुरा कृष्टं पूजने शंकरस्य च .. 21 ..
5.256.m: meditating on Hari and Śaṃkara at dawn, noon, and afternoon, / emaciating her body just as she had formerly done in the worship of Śaṃkara, (21)

5.256.s:
sakhījana samāyuktā pituḥ śṛṃge manohare ..
atapatsā viśālākṣī kṣamādiguṇasaṃyutā .. 22 ..
5.256.d:
सखीजन समायुक्ता पितुः शृंगे मनोहरे ..
अतपत्सा विशालाक्षी क्षमादिगुणसंयुता .. 22 ..
5.256.m: accompanied by her female companions on the delightful peak of her father, / that large-eyed lady, endowed with forbearance and other virtues, practiced austerity. (22)

5.256.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
yā hi yogīśvaradhyeyā yā vandyā viśvavanditā ..
jananī yā ca viśvasya sā'pi kāmāttapogatā .. 23 ..
5.256.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
या हि योगीश्वरध्येया या वन्द्या विश्ववन्दिता ..
जननी या च विश्वस्य साऽपि कामात्तपोगता .. 23 ..
5.256.m:
Gālava said:
She who is to be meditated upon by the lords of yoga, who is worthy of homage, revered by the universe, / and who is the mother of the universe—even she resorted to austerity out of desire! (23)

5.256.s:
yā hi prakṛtisadrūpā taḍitkoṭisamaprabhā ..
virajā yā svayaṃ vandyā guṇātītācarattapaḥ .. 24 ..
5.256.d:
या हि प्रकृतिसद्रूपा तडित्कोटिसमप्रभा ..
विरजा या स्वयं वन्द्या गुणातीताचरत्तपः .. 24 ..
5.256.m: She whose true form is Prakṛti, possessing the radiance of ten million lightning bolts, / free from passion, herself worthy of worship, beyond the guṇas, performed austerity! (24)

5.256.s:
pṛthvyaṃbu tejo vāyuśca gaganaṃ yanmayaṃ viduḥ ..
mūlaprakṛtirūpā yā sā cakārottama tapaḥ .. 25 ..
5.256.d:
पृथ्व्यंबु तेजो वायुश्च गगनं यन्मयं विदुः ..
मूलप्रकृतिरूपा या सा चकारोत्तम तपः .. 25 ..
5.256.m: She of whom earth, water, fire, wind, and ether are known to be composed, / she whose form is primordial nature, performed supreme austerity! (25)

5.256.s:
yā sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamamāśu viśvaṃ vyāpya sthitā yā prakṛteḥ purāpi ..
spṛhādirūpeṇa ca tṛptidātrī deve prasupte tapasā''pa śuddhim .. 26 ..
5.256.d:
या स्थावरं जंगममाशु विश्वं व्याप्य स्थिता या प्रकृतेः पुरापि ..
स्पृहादिरूपेण च तृप्तिदात्री देवे प्रसुप्ते तपसा'ऽप शुद्धिम् .. 26 ..
5.256.m: She who swiftly pervaded the universe of mobile and immobile beings and remained so, who existed even before Prakṛti, / and who, in the form of desire and the like, grants contentment—while the God was asleep, she attained purification through austerity. (26)

5.256.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye dvādaśākṣaranāmamahimapūrvakapārvatītapovarṇanaṃ nāma saptapaṃcāśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 257 ..
5.256.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये द्वादशाक्षरनाममहिमपूर्वकपार्वतीतपोवर्णनं नाम सप्तपंचाशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 257 ..
5.256.m: Thus ends the two hundred fifty-seventh chapter, named "Description of Pārvatī's Austerity Preceded by the Greatness of the Twelve-Syllable Name," in the Greatness of the Cāturmāsya within the dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, in the account of the One Sleeping on Śeṣa, in the Greatness of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.257.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
pravṛttāyāṃ śailaputryāṃ mahattapasi dāruṇe ..
kandarpeṇa parābhūto vicacāra mahīṃ haraḥ .. 1 ..
5.257.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
प्रवृत्तायां शैलपुत्र्यां महत्तपसि दारुणे ..
कन्दर्पेण पराभूतो विचचार महीं हरः .. 1 ..
5.257.m:
Gālava said:
While the Daughter of the Mountain engaged in severe and terrible austerity, / Hara, overcome by the god of love, roamed over the earth. (1)

5.257.s:
vṛkṣacchāyāsu tīrtheṣu nadīṣu ca nadeṣu ca ..
jalena siṃcatsvavapuḥ sarvatrāpi maheśvaraḥ .. 2 ..
5.257.d:
वृक्षच्छायासु तीर्थेषु नदीषु च नदेषु च ..
जलेन सिंचत्स्ववपुः सर्वत्रापि महेश्वरः .. 2 ..
5.257.m: In the shade of trees, at sacred fords, and by rivers and streams, / sprinkling his own body everywhere with water, Maheśvara [wandered]. (2)

5.257.s:
tathāpi kāmākulito na lebhe śarma karhicit ..
ekadā yamunāṃ dṛṣṭvā jalakallolamālinīm .. .. 3 ..
5.257.d:
तथापि कामाकुलितो न लेभे शर्म कर्हिचित् ..
एकदा यमुनां दृष्ट्वा जलकल्लोलमालिनीम् .. .. 3 ..
5.257.m: Nevertheless, agitated by desire, he found no comfort anywhere. / Once, upon seeing the Yamunā garlanded with billowing waves, (3)

5.257.s:
vigāhituṃ manaścakre tāpārtiṃ śamayanniva ..
kṛṣṇaṃ babhūva tannīraṃ harakāyāgnivahninā .. 4 ..
5.257.d:
विगाहितुं मनश्चक्रे तापार्तिं शमयन्निव ..
कृष्णं बभूव तन्नीरं हरकायाग्निवह्निना .. 4 ..
5.257.m: he made up his mind to plunge in, as if to quell the torment of his burning heat; / [and] its water turned black from the fire of Hara's bodily flame. (4)

5.257.s:
dagdhaṃ vigāhanenāśu maṣīprāyaṃ tadā babhau 1.
sā'pi divyavapuḥ pūrvaṃ śyāmā bhūtvā harādyataḥ .. 5 ..
5.257.d:
दग्धं विगाहनेनाशु मषीप्रायं तदा बभौ 1.
साऽपि दिव्यवपुः पूर्वं श्यामा भूत्वा हराद्यतः .. 5 ..
5.257.m: Scorched instantly by his plunging in, it appeared almost like ink. / She too, who previously possessed a divine body, having become dark-complexioned because of Hara, (5)

5.257.s:
stutvā natvā maheśānamuvāca punareva sā ..
prasādaṃ kuru deveśa vaśagāsmi sadā tava .. 6 ..
5.257.d:
स्तुत्वा नत्वा महेशानमुवाच पुनरेव सा ..
प्रसादं कुरु देवेश वशगास्मि सदा तव .. 6 ..
5.257.m: praised and bowed down to the great Lord, and spoke once again: / "Grant your grace, O Lord of gods; I am forever subject to your will." (6)

5.257.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
asmiṃstīrthavarepuṇye yaḥ snāsyati naro bhuvi ..
tasya pāpasahasrāṇi yāsyaṃti vilayaṃ dhruvam 1. 7 ..
5.257.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
अस्मिंस्तीर्थवरेपुण्ये यः स्नास्यति नरो भुवि ..
तस्य पापसहस्राणि यास्यंति विलयं ध्रुवम् 1. 7 ..
5.257.m:
Īśvara said:
Whatever mortal on earth shall bathe in this excellent, holy sacred ford, / his thousands of sins will surely dissolve away. (7)

5.257.s:
haratīrthamiti khyātaṃ puṇyaṃ loke bhaviṣyati ..
ityuktvā tāṃ praṇamyātha tatraivāṃtaradhīyata .. 8 ..
5.257.d:
हरतीर्थमिति ख्यातं पुण्यं लोके भविष्यति ..
इत्युक्त्वा तां प्रणम्याथ तत्रैवांतरधीयत .. 8 ..
5.257.m: It shall become famous in the world as the holy Haratīrtha. / Having spoken thus to her and bowed, he vanished right there. (8)

5.257.s:
tasyāstīre maheśo'pi kṛtvā rūpaṃ manoharam ..
kāmālayaṃ vādyahastaṃ kṛtapuṃḍraṃ jaṭādharam .. 9 ..
5.257.d:
तस्यास्तीरे महेशोऽपि कृत्वा रूपं मनोहरम् ..
कामालयं वाद्यहस्तं कृतपुंड्रं जटाधरम् .. 9 ..
5.257.m: Upon its bank, Maheśa assumed a charming form— / an abode of desire, holding a musical instrument in hand, marked with sectarian lines, wearing matted locks. (9)

5.257.s:
svecchayā munigeheṣu darśayatyaṃgacāpalam ..
kvacidgāyati gītāni kvacinnṛtyati chandataḥ .. 6.258.10 ..
5.257.d:
स्वेच्छया मुनिगेहेषु दर्शयत्यंगचापलम् ..
क्वचिद्गायति गीतानि क्वचिन्नृत्यति छन्दतः .. 6.258.10 ..
5.257.m: At will, he displayed bodily coquetry in the houses of the sages; / in one place he sang songs, in another he danced as he pleased. (10)

5.257.s:
sa ca kruddhyati hasati strīṇāṃ madhyagataḥ kvacit ..
evaṃ vicaratastasya ṛṣipatnyaḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 11 ..
5.257.d:
स च क्रुद्ध्यति हसति स्त्रीणां मध्यगतः क्वचित् ..
एवं विचरतस्तस्य ऋषिपत्न्यः समंततः .. 11 ..
5.257.m: He grew angry, and he laughed, standing at times in the midst of women. / As he thus wandered about, the wives of the seers on all sides [gazed upon him]. (11)

5.257.s:
patyuḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ gehe tyaktvā kāryāṇyapi kṣaṇāt ..
tameva manasā cakruḥ patirūpeṇa mohitāḥ .. 12 ..
5.257.d:
पत्युः शुश्रूषणं गेहे त्यक्त्वा कार्याण्यपि क्षणात् ..
तमेव मनसा चक्रुः पतिरूपेण मोहिताः .. 12 ..
5.257.m:
Abandoning in an instant their service to their husbands at home and their duties,
they, captivated by delusion, fixed upon him alone in their minds as their husband.

5.257.s:
bhramaṃtyaścaiva hāsyāni cakrustā api yoṣitaḥ ..
tatastu munayo dṛṣṭvā tāsāṃ duḥśīlabhāvanām .. 13 ..
5.257.d:
भ्रमंत्यश्चैव हास्यानि चक्रुस्ता अपि योषितः ..
ततस्तु मुनयो दृष्ट्वा तासां दुःशीलभावनाम् .. 13 ..
5.257.m:
Those women wandered about, laughing aloud.
Then the sages, seeing their unruly state of mind,

5.257.s:
cukrudhurmunayaḥ sarve rūpaṃ tasya manoharam ..
gṛhyatāṃ hanyatāmeṣa ko'yaṃ duṣṭa upāgataḥ .. 14 ..
5.257.d:
चुक्रुधुर्मुनयः सर्वे रूपं तस्य मनोहरम् ..
गृह्यतां हन्यतामेष कोऽयं दुष्ट उपागतः .. 14 ..
5.257.m:
all the sages became enraged at his enchanting form:
“Seize him! Strike him! Who is this wicked one that has arrived?”

5.257.s:
iti te gṛhya kāṣṭhāni yadopasthe yayustadā ..
palāyitaḥ sa bahudhā bhayātteṣāṃ mahātmanām .. 15 ..
5.257.d:
इति ते गृह्य काष्ठानि यदोपस्थे ययुस्तदा ..
पलायितः स बहुधा भयात्तेषां महात्मनाम् .. 15 ..
5.257.m:
Thus, picking up pieces of wood, when they went against him,
he fled in various directions out of fear of those great-souled [sages].

5.257.s:
yo jīvakalayā viśvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhati dehinām ..
na jñāyate na ca grāhyo na bhedyaścāpi jāyate .. 16 ..
5.257.d:
यो जीवकलया विश्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठति देहिनाम् ..
न ज्ञायते न च ग्राह्यो न भेद्यश्चापि जायते .. 16 ..
5.257.m:
He who abides pervading the universe of embodied beings by a portion of life,
is not known, cannot be grasped, and cannot be divided.

5.257.s:
na śekuste yadā sarve grahītuṃ taṃ maheśvaram ..
tadā śivaṃ prakupitā śepuritthaṃ dvijātayaḥ .. 17 ..
5.257.d:
न शेकुस्ते यदा सर्वे ग्रहीतुं तं महेश्वरम् ..
तदा शिवं प्रकुपिता शेपुरित्थं द्विजातयः .. 17 ..
5.257.m:
When they were all unable to seize that Maheśvara,
then the twice-born, filled with rage, cursed Śiva thus:

5.257.s:
yasmālliṃgārthamāgatya hyāśramāṃścoravatkṛtam ..
paradārāpaharaṇaṃ talliṅgaṃ patatāṃ bhuvi .. 18 ..
5.257.d:
यस्माल्लिंगार्थमागत्य ह्याश्रमांश्चोरवत्कृतम् ..
परदारापहरणं तल्लिङ्गं पततां भुवि .. 18 ..
5.257.m:
“Since you have entered the hermitages like a thief for the sake of the phallus,
carrying off others' wives, may that liṅga fall to the ground!

5.257.s:
sadya eva hi śāpaṃ tvaṃ duṣṭaṃ prāpnuhi tāpasa ..
evamukte sa śāpāgnirvajrarūpadharo mahān .. 19 ..
5.257.d:
सद्य एव हि शापं त्वं दुष्टं प्राप्नुहि तापस ..
एवमुक्ते स शापाग्निर्वज्ररूपधरो महान् .. 19 ..
5.257.m:
Immediately indeed may you receive a terrible curse, ascetic!”
When this was said, that great fire of the curse, assuming the form of a thunderbolt,

5.257.s:
talligaṃ dhūrjaṭeśchittvā pātayāmāsa bhūtale ..
rudhiraughaparivyāpto mumoha bhagavānvibhuḥ .. 6.258.20 ..
5.257.d:
तल्लिगं धूर्जटेश्छित्त्वा पातयामास भूतले ..
रुधिरौघपरिव्याप्तो मुमोह भगवान्विभुः .. 6.258.20 ..
5.257.m:
severed that liṅga of Dhūrjaṭi and cast it down upon the ground.
Pervaded by a torrent of blood, the sovereign Lord fainted.

5.257.s:
vedanārttojjvalavapurmahāśāpābhibhūtadhīḥ ..
taṃ tathā patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ta ājagmurmaharṣayaḥ .. 21 ..
5.257.d:
वेदनार्त्तोज्ज्वलवपुर्महाशापाभिभूतधीः ..
तं तथा पतितं दृष्ट्वा त आजग्मुर्महर्षयः .. 21 ..
5.257.m:
His blazing body afflicted with pain, his intellect overwhelmed by the great curse—
seeing him fallen thus, those great seers came there.

5.257.s:
ākāśe sarvabhūtāni tresurviśvaṃ cacāla ha ..
devāśca vyākulā jātā mahābhayamupāgatāḥ .. 22 ..
5.257.d:
आकाशे सर्वभूतानि त्रेसुर्विश्वं चचाल ह ..
देवाश्च व्याकुला जाता महाभयमुपागताः .. 22 ..
5.257.m:
All creatures in the sky trembled, and the universe shook;
the gods became agitated and fell into great terror.

5.257.s:
jñātvā viprā maheśānaṃ pīḍitā hṛdaye'bhavan ..
śuśucurbhṛśaduḥkhārtā daivaṃ hi balavattaram .. 23 ..
5.257.d:
ज्ञात्वा विप्रा महेशानं पीडिता हृदयेऽभवन् ..
शुशुचुर्भृशदुःखार्ता दैवं हि बलवत्तरम् .. 23 ..
5.257.m:
Recognizing Maheśāna, the brahmins became afflicted at heart;
smitten with intense sorrow, they lamented, for fate is indeed all-powerful:

5.257.s:
kiṃ kṛtaṃ bhagavāneṣa devairapi sa sevyate ..
sākṣī sarvasya jagato'smābhirnaivopalakṣitaḥ .. 24 ..
5.257.d:
किं कृतं भगवानेष देवैरपि स सेव्यते ..
साक्षी सर्वस्य जगतोऽस्माभिर्नैवोपलक्षितः .. 24 ..
5.257.m:
“What have we done? This is the Lord who is served even by the gods,
the witness of the entire world, yet he was not recognized by us!

5.257.s:
vayaṃ mūḍhadhiyaḥ pāpāḥ paramajñānadurbalāḥ..
kathamasmābhiryasyātmā śrutaśca na niveditaḥ .. 25 ..
5.257.d:
वयं मूढधियः पापाः परमज्ञानदुर्बलाः..
कथमस्माभिर्यस्यात्मा श्रुतश्च न निवेदितः .. 25 ..
5.257.m:
We are foolish in mind, wicked, weak in the supreme knowledge!
How was his true self, though heard of, not acknowledged by us?

5.257.s:
mayedṛśo gṛhasthāya hyātmā'yaṃ na niveditaḥ ..
nirvikāro nirviṣayo nirīho nirupadravaḥ .. 26 ..
5.257.d:
मयेदृशो गृहस्थाय ह्यात्माऽयं न निवेदितः ..
निर्विकारो निर्विषयो निरीहो निरुपद्रवः .. 26 ..
5.257.m:
Such a self was not offered by me to this householder—
changeless, free from sense-objects, desireless, free from afflictions,

5.257.s:
nirmamo nirahaṃkāro yaḥ śaṃbhurnopalakṣitaḥ ..
yasya lokā ime sarve dehe tiṣṭhaṃti madhyagāḥ .. 27 ..
5.257.d:
निर्ममो निरहंकारो यः शंभुर्नोपलक्षितः ..
यस्य लोका इमे सर्वे देहे तिष्ठंति मध्यगाः .. 27 ..
5.257.m:
without possessiveness, without egotism—which Śambhu was not perceived,
in the midst of whose body all these worlds abide!

5.257.s:
sa eṣa jagatāṃ svāmī haro'smābhirna vīkṣitaḥ ..
ityuktvā te hyupaviṣṭā yāvattatra samāgatāḥ .. 28 ..
5.257.d:
स एष जगतां स्वामी हरोऽस्माभिर्न वीक्षितः ..
इत्युक्त्वा ते ह्युपविष्टा यावत्तत्र समागताः .. 28 ..
5.257.m:
This master of the worlds, Hara, was not seen by us!”
Having spoken thus, they sat down, and as they gathered there,

5.257.s:
tāndṛṣṭvā sahasā trastaḥ punareva maheśvaraḥ ..
vipraśāpabhayānnaṣṭastripurārirdivaṃ yayau .. 29 ..
5.257.d:
तान्दृष्ट्वा सहसा त्रस्तः पुनरेव महेश्वरः ..
विप्रशापभयान्नष्टस्त्रिपुरारिर्दिवं ययौ .. 29 ..
5.257.m:
Maheśvara, seeing them, was suddenly alarmed again;
fleeing in fear of the brahmins' curse, the enemy of Tripura went to heaven.

5.257.s:
surabhiṃ gāṃ ca goloke tāṃ tuṣṭāva susaṃyataḥ 1.
sṛṣṭisthiti vināśānāṃ kartryai mātre namonamaḥ .. 6.258.30 ..
5.257.d:
सुरभिं गां च गोलोके तां तुष्टाव सुसंयतः 1.
सृष्टिस्थिति विनाशानां कर्त्र्यै मात्रे नमोनमः .. 6.258.30 ..
5.257.m:
In Goloka, fully self-controlled, he praised the cow Surabhi:
“Homage, homage to the Mother, the creator of origination, preservation, and destruction!

5.257.s:
yā tvaṃ rasamayairbhāvairāpyāyasi bhūtalam ..
devānāṃ ca tathāsaṃghānpitṝṇāmapi vai gaṇān .. 31 1.
sarvai rjñātā rasābhijñairmadhurāsvādadāyinī ..
tvayā viśvamidaṃ sarvaṃ balasnehasamanvitam .. 32 ..
5.257.d:
या त्वं रसमयैर्भावैराप्यायसि भूतलम् ..
देवानां च तथासंघान्पितॄणामपि वै गणान् .. 31 1.
सर्वै र्ज्ञाता रसाभिज्ञैर्मधुरास्वाददायिनी ..
त्वया विश्वमिदं सर्वं बलस्नेहसमन्वितम् .. 32 ..
5.257.m:
You who invigorate the surface of the earth with fluid essences,
and likewise the hosts of gods and the troops of ancestors;
known by all who are connoisseurs of rasa, grantor of sweet taste—
by you this entire universe is endowed with strength and affection.

5.257.s:
tvaṃ mātā sarvarudrāṇāṃ vasūnāṃ duhitā tathā ..
ādityānāṃ svasā caiva tuṣṭā vāṃcchitasiddhidā .. 33 ..
5.257.d:
त्वं माता सर्वरुद्राणां वसूनां दुहिता तथा ..
आदित्यानां स्वसा चैव तुष्टा वांच्छितसिद्धिदा .. 33 ..
5.257.m:
You are the mother of all the Rudras, the daughter of the Vasus,
and the sister of the Ādityas; when pleased, you bestow desired perfections.

5.257.s:
tvaṃ dhṛtistvaṃ tathā puṣṭistvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tathā ..
ṛddhiḥ siddhistathā lakṣmīrdhṛtiḥ kīrti stathā matiḥ .. 34 ..
5.257.d:
त्वं धृतिस्त्वं तथा पुष्टिस्त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा तथा ..
ऋद्धिः सिद्धिस्तथा लक्ष्मीर्धृतिः कीर्ति स्तथा मतिः .. 34 ..
5.257.m:
You are steadfastness, you are nourishment, you are Svāhā, you are Svadhā,
prosperity, perfection, Lakṣmī, patience, renown, and intellect;

5.257.s:
kāṃtirlajjā mahāmāyā śraddhā sarvārthasādhinī ..
tvayā virahitaṃ kiṃcinnāsti tribhuvaneṣvapi .. 35 ..
5.257.d:
कांतिर्लज्जा महामाया श्रद्धा सर्वार्थसाधिनी ..
त्वया विरहितं किंचिन्नास्ति त्रिभुवनेष्वपि .. 35 ..
5.257.m:
radiance, modesty, the great power of illusion, faith that accomplishes all aims.
There is nothing bereft of you, even in the three worlds.

5.257.s:
vahnestṛptipradātrī ca devādīnām ca tṛptidā ..
tvayā sarvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam .. 36 ..
5.257.d:
वह्नेस्तृप्तिप्रदात्री च देवादीनाम् च तृप्तिदा ..
त्वया सर्वमिदं व्याप्तं जगत्स्थावरजंगमम् .. 36 ..
5.257.m:
Giver of satisfaction to the fire, and giver of satisfaction to the gods and others,
by you this entire world, both stationary and moving, is pervaded.

5.257.s:
pādāste vedāścatvāraḥ samudrāḥ stanatāṃ yayuḥ ..
caṃdrārkau locane yasyā romāgreṣu ca devatāḥ .. 37 ..
5.257.d:
पादास्ते वेदाश्चत्वारः समुद्राः स्तनतां ययुः ..
चंद्रार्कौ लोचने यस्या रोमाग्रेषु च देवताः .. 37 ..
5.257.m:
Your feet are the four Vedas; the oceans have become your udders;
you whose eyes are the moon and the sun, and the gods are at the tips of your hairs.

5.257.s:
śṛṅgayoḥ parvatāḥ sarve karṇayorvāyavastathā ..
nābhau caivāmṛtaṃ devi pātālāni khurāstathā ..38..
5.257.d:
शृङ्गयोः पर्वताः सर्वे कर्णयोर्वायवस्तथा ..
नाभौ चैवामृतं देवि पातालानि खुरास्तथा ..38..
5.257.m:
All the mountains are on your horns, and the winds are in your ears;
in your navel is nectar, O goddess, and the realms of Pātāla are your hooves.

5.257.s:
skandhe ca bhagavānbrahmā mastakasthaḥ sadāśivaḥ ..
hṛddeśe ca sthito viṣṇuḥ pucchāgre pannagāstathā .. 39 ..
śakṛtsthā vasavaḥ sarve sādhyā mūtrasthitāstava ..
sarve yajñā hyasthideśe kinnarā guhyasaṃsthitāḥ .. 6.258.40 ..
5.257.d:
स्कन्धे च भगवान्ब्रह्मा मस्तकस्थः सदाशिवः ..
हृद्देशे च स्थितो विष्णुः पुच्छाग्रे पन्नगास्तथा .. 39 ..
शकृत्स्था वसवः सर्वे साध्या मूत्रस्थितास्तव ..
सर्वे यज्ञा ह्यस्थिदेशे किन्नरा गुह्यसंस्थिताः .. 6.258.40 ..

5.257.s:
pitṝṇāṃ ca gaṇāḥ sarve puraḥsthā bhāṃti sarvadā ..
sarve yakṣā bhāladeśe kinnarāśca kapolayoḥ .. 41 ..
5.257.d:
पितॄणां च गणाः सर्वे पुरःस्था भांति सर्वदा ..
सर्वे यक्षा भालदेशे किन्नराश्च कपोलयोः .. 41 ..
5.257.m:
All the hosts of ancestors shine ever before you;
all the Yakṣas are upon your forehead, and the Kinnaras upon your cheeks.

5.257.s:
sarvadevamayī tvaṃ hi sarvabhūtavivṛddhidā ..
sarvalokahitā nityaṃ mama dehahitā bhava .. 42 ..
5.257.d:
सर्वदेवमयी त्वं हि सर्वभूतविवृद्धिदा ..
सर्वलोकहिता नित्यं मम देहहिता भव .. 42 ..
5.257.m:
Composed of all the gods, you cause the growth of all living beings;
every beneficent to all worlds, be beneficent to my body!

5.257.s:
praṇatastava deveśi pūjaye tvāṃ sadā'naghe ..
staumi viśvārtihantrīṃ tvāṃ prasannā varadā bhava .. 43 ..
5.257.d:
प्रणतस्तव देवेशि पूजये त्वां सदाऽनघे ..
स्तौमि विश्वार्तिहन्त्रीं त्वां प्रसन्ना वरदा भव .. 43 ..
5.257.m:
Bowed before you, O ruler of the gods, I ever worship you, sinless one;
I praise you, the destroyer of universal distress: be gracious, granter of boons!

5.257.s:
vipraśāpāgninā dagdhaṃ śarīraṃ mama śobhane ..
svatejasā punaḥ karttumarhasyamṛtasaṃbhave .. 44 ..
5.257.d:
विप्रशापाग्निना दग्धं शरीरं मम शोभने ..
स्वतेजसा पुनः कर्त्तुमर्हस्यमृतसंभवे .. 44 ..
5.257.m:
My body has been burned by the fire of the brahmins' curse, O beautiful one;
you ought to recreate it by your own splendor, O you born from nectar!”

5.257.s:
ityuktvā tā parikramya tasyā dehe layaṃ gataḥ ..
sā'pi garbhe dadhārātha surabhistadanantaram .. 45 ..
5.257.d:
इत्युक्त्वा ता परिक्रम्य तस्या देहे लयं गतः ..
साऽपि गर्भे दधाराथ सुरभिस्तदनन्तरम् .. 45 ..
5.257.m:
Having spoken thus and circumambulated her, he dissolved into her body;
then Surabhi immediately bore him within her womb.

5.257.s:
kālātikramayogena sarvavyākulatāṃ yayau ..
yasminpranaṣṭe deveśe vipraśāpabhayāvṛte .. 46 ..
5.257.d:
कालातिक्रमयोगेन सर्वव्याकुलतां ययौ ..
यस्मिन्प्रनष्टे देवेशे विप्रशापभयावृते .. 46 ..
5.257.m:
With the passage of time, everything fell into perturbation,
for when the Lord of gods had vanished, enveloped in fear of the brahmins' curse,

5.257.s:
devā mahārtiṃ prayayuścacāla pṛthivī tathā ..
caṃdrārkau niṣprabhau caiva vāyuruccaṇḍa eva ca .. 47 ..
5.257.d:
देवा महार्तिं प्रययुश्चचाल पृथिवी तथा ..
चंद्रार्कौ निष्प्रभौ चैव वायुरुच्चण्ड एव च .. 47 ..
5.257.m:
the gods suffered great distress, the earth trembled,
the moon and sun lost their luster, and the wind blew furiously;

5.257.s: samudrāḥ kṣobhamaga maṃstasminkāle dvijottama .. 48 ..
5.257.d: समुद्राः क्षोभमग मंस्तस्मिन्काले द्विजोत्तम .. 48 ..
5.257.m: the oceans were stirred to agitation at that time, O best of the twice-born.

5.257.s:
yasmiñjagatsthāvarajaṃgamādikaṃ kāle layaṃ prāpya punaḥ prarohati ..
tasminpranaṣṭe dvijaśāpapīḍite jayaddhataprāya mavartata kṣaṇāt .. 49 ..
5.257.d:
यस्मिञ्जगत्स्थावरजंगमादिकं काले लयं प्राप्य पुनः प्ररोहति ..
तस्मिन्प्रनष्टे द्विजशापपीडिते जयद्धतप्राय मवर्तत क्षणात् .. 49 ..
5.257.m:
He in whom the world of mobile and immobile things meets dissolution in due time and sprouts again—
when he had vanished, tormented by the twice-borns' curse, the world turned as if virtually destroyed in a moment.

5.257.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye haraśāpo nāmāṣṭapaṃcāśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 258 .. .. .
5.257.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये हरशापो नामाष्टपंचाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 258 .. .. .
5.257.m: Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-eighth chapter, named 'The Curse of Hara', in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the account of Śeṣaśāyin, in the section on the greatness of Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.258.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
tasmiṃstu patite liṃge yojanāyāmavistṛte..
viṣādārttā ṛṣigaṇāstatrājagmuḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 1 ..
vyalokayanta sarvatra dṛṣṭvā tatra maheśvaram..
nāsau dṛṣṭipathe teṣāṃ babhūva bhayavihvalaḥ .. 2 .1
5.258.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
तस्मिंस्तु पतिते लिंगे योजनायामविस्तृते..
विषादार्त्ता ऋषिगणास्तत्राजग्मुः सहस्रशः .. 1 ..
व्यलोकयन्त सर्वत्र दृष्ट्वा तत्र महेश्वरम्..
नासौ दृष्टिपथे तेषां बभूव भयविह्वलः .. 2 .1
5.258.m:
Gālava said: / When that liṅga had fallen, extending across a yojana,
the hosts of seers, smitten with dejection, came there by the thousands.
Looking in all directions to see Maheśvara there,
he was not within their range of sight, distraught with fear.

5.258.s:
vīryaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi bahūnyapi susaṃcitam ..
pṛthivīṃ sakalāṃ vyāpya sthitaṃ dadṛśire dvijāḥ ..3..
5.258.d:
वीर्यं वर्षसहस्राणि बहून्यपि सुसंचितम् ..
पृथिवीं सकलां व्याप्य स्थितं ददृशिरे द्विजाः ..3..
5.258.m:
His semen, well accumulated over many thousands of years,
the twice-born saw remaining, pervading the entire earth.

5.258.s:
taddṛṣṭvā sumahalliṃgaṃ rudhirāktaṃ jalaiḥ plutam ..
brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśayagatā dahyamānā vasundharā .. 4 ..
5.258.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वा सुमहल्लिंगं रुधिराक्तं जलैः प्लुतम् ..
ब्राह्मणाः संशयगता दह्यमाना वसुन्धरा .. 4 ..
5.258.m:
Seeing that very great liṅga smeared with blood and flooded with waters,
the brahmins fell into doubt, while the earth was burning.

5.258.s:
talliṃgaṃ tatra saṃsthāpya cakrustāṃ narmadāṃ nadīm ..
tajjalaṃ narmadārūpaṃ lliṃgaṃ cāmarakaṇṭakam..5..
narakaṃ vārayatyetatsevitaṃ narakāpaham..
bhūtagrahāśca sarve'pi yāsyaṃti vilayaṃ dhruvam..6..
5.258.d:
तल्लिंगं तत्र संस्थाप्य चक्रुस्तां नर्मदां नदीम् ..
तज्जलं नर्मदारूपं ल्लिंगं चामरकण्टकम्..5..
नरकं वारयत्येतत्सेवितं नरकापहम्..
भूतग्रहाश्च सर्वेऽपि यास्यंति विलयं ध्रुवम्..6..
5.258.m: Having established that liṅga there, they formed that Narmadā river. / That water has the form of Narmadā, and the liṅga is Amarakaṇṭaka. / When attended upon, it averts hell, removing hell. / And all malevolent spirits and seizing demons will surely vanish into dissolution.

5.258.s:
tatra snātvā jalaṃ pītvā saṃtarpya ca pitṝṃstathā..
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti manuṣyo bhuvi durlabhān..7..
5.258.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा जलं पीत्वा संतर्प्य च पितॄंस्तथा..
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति मनुष्यो भुवि दुर्लभान्..7..
5.258.m: Having bathed there, drunk the water, and likewise satisfied the ancestors, / a person attains all desires that are hard to obtain on earth.

5.258.s:
liṃgāni nārmadeyāni pūjayiṣyaṃti ye narāḥ..
teṣāṃ rudramayo deho bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa liṃgapūjā mahāphalā..
cāturmāsye rudrajapaṃ harapūjā śive ratiḥ.. 9..
5.258.d:
लिंगानि नार्मदेयानि पूजयिष्यंति ये नराः..
तेषां रुद्रमयो देहो भविष्यति न संशयः..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण लिंगपूजा महाफला..
चातुर्मास्ये रुद्रजपं हरपूजा शिवे रतिः.. 9..
5.258.m: Those men who will worship the liṅgas born of the Narmadā— / their bodies will become composed of Rudra, without doubt. / Especially during Cāturmāsya, the worship of the liṅga bears great fruit: / during Cāturmāsya, recitation of Rudra's [mantra], worship of Hara, and delight in Śiva.

5.258.s:
paṃcāmṛtena snapanaṃ na teṣāṃgarbhavedanā ..
ye kariṣyaṃti madhunā secanaṃ liṃgamastake .. 6.259.10 ..
5.258.d:
पंचामृतेन स्नपनं न तेषांगर्भवेदना ..
ये करिष्यंति मधुना सेचनं लिंगमस्तके .. 6.259.10 ..
5.258.m: [For those who perform] the ceremonial bath with the five nectars, there is no pain of the womb. / Those who will perform sprinkling with honey upon the head of the liṅga—

5.258.s:
teṣāṃ duḥkhasahasrāṇi yāsyaṃti vilayaṃ dhruvam ..
dīpadānaṃ kṛtaṃ yena cātu rmāsye śivāgrataḥ .. 11 ..
5.258.d:
तेषां दुःखसहस्राणि यास्यंति विलयं ध्रुवम् ..
दीपदानं कृतं येन चातु र्मास्ये शिवाग्रतः .. 11 ..
5.258.m: their thousands of miseries will surely vanish into dissolution. / By whomsoever a gift of a lamp is offered before Śiva during Cāturmāsya,

5.258.s:
kulakoṭiṃ samuddhṛtya svecchayā śivalokabhāk ..
candanāgurudhūpaiśca suśvetakusumairapi .. 12 ..
5.258.d:
कुलकोटिं समुद्धृत्य स्वेच्छया शिवलोकभाक् ..
चन्दनागुरुधूपैश्च सुश्वेतकुसुमैरपि .. 12 ..
5.258.m: he, having delivered ten million ancestors of his family, enjoys the world of Śiva at his will. / And with sandal, agallochum incense, and pure white flowers,

5.258.s:
narmadājalaliṃgaṃ ye hyarca yiṣyaṃti te śivāḥ ..
śilā haratvamāpannāḥ prāṇināmapi kā kathā .. 13 ..
5.258.d:
नर्मदाजललिंगं ये ह्यर्च यिष्यंति ते शिवाः ..
शिला हरत्वमापन्नाः प्राणिनामपि का कथा .. 13 ..
5.258.m: those who will worship the liṅga in the waters of the Narmadā become Śivas indeed. / [When] even stones have attained the nature of Hara, what to say of living beings?

5.258.s:
tatsaṃbhūtaṃ mahāliṃgaṃ jaladhāraṇasaṃyutam ..
pūjayitvā vidhānena cāturmāsye śivo bhavet .. 14 ..
5.258.d:
तत्संभूतं महालिंगं जलधारणसंयुतम् ..
पूजयित्वा विधानेन चातुर्मास्ये शिवो भवेत् .. 14 ..
5.258.m: Having properly worshipped during Cāturmāsya that great liṅga arisen there, / which is accompanied by the holding of water, one becomes Śiva.

5.258.s:
cāturmāsye ye manujā narmadā'marakaṇṭake ..
tīrthe snāsyaṃti niyatāsteṣāṃ vāsastriviṣṭape .. 15 .. ..
5.258.d:
चातुर्मास्ये ये मनुजा नर्मदाऽमरकण्टके ..
तीर्थे स्नास्यंति नियतास्तेषां वासस्त्रिविष्टपे .. 15 .. ..
5.258.m: Those men who, restrained, will bathe in the sacred ford of Amarakaṇṭaka on the Narmadā / during Cāturmāsya, their dwelling is in heaven.

5.258.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
ityuktvā te dvijāstatra sthāpya liṃgaṃ yathāvidhi ..
amarakaṇṭakatīrthe narmadāṃ ca mahānadīm .. 16 ..
5.258.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
इत्युक्त्वा ते द्विजास्तत्र स्थाप्य लिंगं यथाविधि ..
अमरकण्टकतीर्थे नर्मदां च महानदीम् .. 16 ..
5.258.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, those twice-born, having established the liṅga according to rule / and the great river Narmadā at the Amarakaṇṭaka sacred ford,

5.258.s:
punaścintāparā jātā viśvasya kṣobhakāraṇe ..
padmāsanagatā bhūtvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ .. 17 ..
5.258.d:
पुनश्चिन्तापरा जाता विश्वस्य क्षोभकारणे ..
पद्मासनगता भूत्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः .. 17 ..
5.258.m: became once again absorbed in thought over the cause of the agitation of the universe. / Seated in the lotus posture and devoted to breath-control,

5.258.s:
cintayāmāsuravyagraṃ hṛdayasthaṃ mahe śvaram ..
tato devā maheṃdrādyāḥ saṃprāpyāmarakaṇṭakam .. 18 ..
5.258.d:
चिन्तयामासुरव्यग्रं हृदयस्थं महे श्वरम् ..
ततो देवा महेंद्राद्याः संप्राप्यामरकण्टकम् .. 18 ..
5.258.m: they meditated with undisturbed mind upon the Great Lord residing within their heart. / Then the gods, headed by Mahendra, having reached Amarakaṇṭaka,

5.258.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ stutiṃ cakrurvinayānatakandharāḥ ..
namo'stu vo dvijātibhyo brahmavidbhyo maheśvarāḥ .. 19 ..
5.258.d:
ब्राह्मणानां स्तुतिं चक्रुर्विनयानतकन्धराः ..
नमोऽस्तु वो द्विजातिभ्यो ब्रह्मविद्भ्यो महेश्वराः .. 19 ..
5.258.m: praised the brahmins with their necks bowed in modesty: / “Homage be to you twice-born, knowers of Brahman, great lords,

5.258.s:
bhūsurebhyo gurubhyaśca vimuktebhyaśca vaṃdhanāt ..
yūyaṃ guṇatrayātītā guṇarūpā guṇākarāḥ .. 6.259.20 ..
5.258.d:
भूसुरेभ्यो गुरुभ्यश्च विमुक्तेभ्यश्च वंधनात् ..
यूयं गुणत्रयातीता गुणरूपा गुणाकराः .. 6.259.20 ..
5.258.m: gods on earth, teachers, and liberated from bondage! / You have transcended the three guṇas, you embody the guṇas, you are mines of virtues.

5.258.s:
guṇatrayamayairbhāvaiḥ satataṃ prāṇabudbudāḥ ..
yeṣāṃ vākyajalenaiva pāpiṣṭhā api śuddhatām ..
prayāṃti pāpapuṃjāśca bhasmasādyāṃti pāpinām .. 21 ..
5.258.d:
गुणत्रयमयैर्भावैः सततं प्राणबुद्बुदाः ..
येषां वाक्यजलेनैव पापिष्ठा अपि शुद्धताम् ..
प्रयांति पापपुंजाश्च भस्मसाद्यांति पापिनाम् .. 21 ..
5.258.m: By states consisting of the three guṇas, [all] are continually bubbles of breath. / By the very water of the words of those [brahmins], even the most sinful attain purity, / and the heaps of sins of sinners are reduced to ashes.

5.258.s:
śastraṃ lohamayaṃ yeṣāṃ vāgeva tatsamanvitāḥ ..
pāpaiḥ parābhibhūtānāṃ teṣāṃ lokottaraṃ balam .. 22 ..
5.258.d:
शस्त्रं लोहमयं येषां वागेव तत्समन्विताः ..
पापैः पराभिभूतानां तेषां लोकोत्तरं बलम् .. 22 ..
5.258.m: Those whose weapon is made of iron are endowed with only that; / [but] the power of those overcome by sins is surpassed by the speech [of brahmins], which has extraordinary might.

5.258.s:
kṣamayā pṛthivītulyāḥ kope vaiśvānaraprabhāḥ ..
pātane'nekaśaktīnāṃ samarthā yūyameva hi .. 23 ..
5.258.d:
क्षमया पृथिवीतुल्याः कोपे वैश्वानरप्रभाः ..
पातनेऽनेकशक्तीनां समर्था यूयमेव हि .. 23 ..
5.258.m: In forbearance you equal the earth; in wrath you have the radiance of fire. / You alone indeed are capable of bringing down manifold powers.

5.258.s: svargādīnāṃ tathā yāne bhavanto gatayo dhruvam .. 24 ..
5.258.d: स्वर्गादीनां तथा याने भवन्तो गतयो ध्रुवम् .. 24 ..
5.258.m: Likewise, for journeying to heaven and the like, you are the sure refuges.

5.258.s:
satkarmakārakāścaiva satkarmaniratāḥ sadā ..
satkarmaphaladātāraḥ satkarmebhyo mumukṣavaḥ .. 25 ..
5.258.d:
सत्कर्मकारकाश्चैव सत्कर्मनिरताः सदा ..
सत्कर्मफलदातारः सत्कर्मेभ्यो मुमुक्षवः .. 25 ..
5.258.m: You are the instigators of good deeds and ever devoted to good deeds; / givers of the fruit of good deeds, desiring liberation from good deeds.

5.258.s:
sāvitrīmaṃtraniratā ye bhavaṃto'ghanāśanāḥ ..
ātmānaṃ yajamānaṃ ca tārayaṃti na saṃśayaḥ .. 26 ..
5.258.d:
सावित्रीमंत्रनिरता ये भवंतोऽघनाशनाः ..
आत्मानं यजमानं च तारयंति न संशयः .. 26 ..
5.258.m: You who are devoted to the Sāvitrī mantra, destroyers of sin, / deliver both yourselves and the sacrificer, without doubt.

5.258.s:
vahnayaśca tathā viprāstarpitāḥ kāryasādhakāḥ ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa teṣāṃ pūjā mahāphalā .. 27 ..
5.258.d:
वह्नयश्च तथा विप्रास्तर्पिताः कार्यसाधकाः ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण तेषां पूजा महाफला .. 27 ..
5.258.m: And likewise the fires, and the satisfied brahmins, accomplish all ends. / Especially during Cāturmāsya, worshipping them bears great fruit.

5.258.s:
kopitāḥ sarvadehasya nāśanāya bhavaṃti hi 1.
tāvanna vajramiṃdrasya śūlaṃ naiva pinākinaḥ .. 28 ..
5.258.d:
कोपिताः सर्वदेहस्य नाशनाय भवंति हि 1.
तावन्न वज्रमिंद्रस्य शूलं नैव पिनाकिनः .. 28 ..
5.258.m: When angered, they indeed bring about the destruction of the entire body. / Indra's thunderbolt is not such, nor indeed is the trident of the Pināka-wielder;

5.258.s:
daṇḍo yamasya tāvanno yāvacchāpo dvijodbhavaḥ ..
agninā jvālyate dṛśyaṃ śāpoddiṣṭānapi svayam .. 29 ..
5.258.d:
दण्डो यमस्य तावन्नो यावच्छापो द्विजोद्भवः ..
अग्निना ज्वाल्यते दृश्यं शापोद्दिष्टानपि स्वयम् .. 29 ..
5.258.m: Yama's staff is not such, as is a curse arising from a twice-born. / What is visible is burned by fire, but [a curse] itself [burns] even those designated by the curse;

5.258.s:
haṃti jātānajātāṃśca tasmādvipraṃ na kopayet..
viprakopāgninā dagdho narakānnaiva mucyate .. 6.259.30 ..
5.258.d:
हंति जातानजातांश्च तस्माद्विप्रं न कोपयेत्..
विप्रकोपाग्निना दग्धो नरकान्नैव मुच्यते .. 6.259.30 ..
5.258.m: it slays the born and the unborn; therefore one should not anger a brahmin. / Burned by the fire of a brahmin's wrath, one is never freed from hell.

5.258.s:
śastrakṣato'pi narakānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
devānāṃ madhudhānyānāṃ sāmarthyaṃ bhedanena hi .. 31 ..
5.258.d:
शस्त्रक्षतोऽपि नरकान्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ..
देवानां मधुधान्यानां सामर्थ्यं भेदनेन हि .. 31 ..
5.258.m: Even one wounded by a weapon is freed from hell, there is no doubt of this. / The power of the gods, mead, and grains lies indeed in splitting [external objects];

5.258.s:
vāṅmātreṇa hi viprasya bhidyate sakalaṃ jagat ..
te yūyaṃ guravo'smākaṃ viśvakāraṇakārakāḥ ..
prasādaparamā nityaṃ bhavaṃtu bhuvaneśvarāḥ .. 32 ..
5.258.d:
वाङ्मात्रेण हि विप्रस्य भिद्यते सकलं जगत् ..
ते यूयं गुरवोऽस्माकं विश्वकारणकारकाः ..
प्रसादपरमा नित्यं भवंतु भुवनेश्वराः .. 32 ..
5.258.m: by a mere word of a brahmin, the entire universe is shattered. / You are our teachers, makers of the cause of the universe; / may you, lords of the world, be ever supremely gracious!

5.258.s:
īśvareṇa vinā sarve vayaṃ lokāśca duḥkhitāḥ ..
tatkathyatāṃ sa bhagavānkutrāste parameśvaraḥ .. 33 .. ..
5.258.d:
ईश्वरेण विना सर्वे वयं लोकाश्च दुःखिताः ..
तत्कथ्यतां स भगवान्कुत्रास्ते परमेश्वरः .. 33 .. ..
5.258.m: Without the Lord, all of us and the worlds are miserable. / Therefore let it be told: where does that venerable Supreme Lord dwell?”

5.258.s:
gālava uvāca .. ..
jñātvā munibhayatrastaṃ deveśaṃ śūlapāṇinam .. 34 ..
5.258.d:
गालव उवाच .. ..
ज्ञात्वा मुनिभयत्रस्तं देवेशं शूलपाणिनम् .. 34 ..
5.258.m: Gālava said: / Having known that the Lord of gods, who holds the trident in his hand, terrified of the sages,

5.258.s:
surabhīgarbhasaṃbhūtaṃ devānūcurmaharṣayaḥ ..
svāgataṃ devadevebhyo jñāto vai sa maheśvaraḥ .. 35 ..
5.258.d:
सुरभीगर्भसंभूतं देवानूचुर्महर्षयः ..
स्वागतं देवदेवेभ्यो ज्ञातो वै स महेश्वरः .. 35 ..
5.258.m: was born from the womb of Surabhi, the great seers said to the gods: / “Welcome to the gods of gods! Indeed, that Great Lord is known [to us].

5.258.s:
tatra gacchaṃtu deveśā yatra devaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
ityuktvā te mahātmānaḥ saha devairyayustadā .. 36 ..
5.258.d:
तत्र गच्छंतु देवेशा यत्र देवः सनातनः ..
इत्युक्त्वा ते महात्मानः सह देवैर्ययुस्तदा .. 36 ..
5.258.m: Let the lords of the gods go to that place where the eternal God is.” / Having spoken thus, those great souls then went together with the gods

5.258.s:
golokaṃ devamārgeṇa yatra pāyasakardamāḥ ..
ghṛtanadyomadhu hradā nadīnāṃ yatra saṃghaśaḥ .. 37 ..
5.258.d:
गोलोकं देवमार्गेण यत्र पायसकर्दमाः ..
घृतनद्योमधु ह्रदा नदीनां यत्र संघशः .. 37 ..
5.258.m: along the divine path to Goloka, where there is mud of milk-rice, / where there are rivers of ghee, pools of honey, and clusters of rivers;

5.258.s:
pūrvajānāṃ gaṇāḥ sarve dadhipīyūṣapāṇayaḥ ..
marīcipāḥ somapāśca siddhasaṃghāstathā pare .. 38 ..
5.258.d:
पूर्वजानां गणाः सर्वे दधिपीयूषपाणयः ..
मरीचिपाः सोमपाश्च सिद्धसंघास्तथा परे .. 38 ..
5.258.m: where all the hosts of ancestors hold curd and nectar in their hands; / where Marīcipas, Somapas, and other hosts of siddhas,

5.258.s:
ghṛtapāścaiva sādhyāśca yatra devāḥ sanātanāḥ ..
te tatra gatvā munayo dadṛśuḥ surabhīsutam .. 39 ..
5.258.d:
घृतपाश्चैव साध्याश्च यत्र देवाः सनातनाः ..
ते तत्र गत्वा मुनयो ददृशुः सुरभीसुतम् .. 39 ..
5.258.m: Ghrtapas, Sādhyas, and eternal gods dwell. / Having gone there, those sages saw the son of Surabhi,

5.258.s:
tejasā bhāskaraṃ caiva nīlanāmeti viśrutam ..
itastato'bhidhāvaṃtaṃ gavāṃ saṃghātamadhyagam .. 6.259.40 ..
5.258.d:
तेजसा भास्करं चैव नीलनामेति विश्रुतम् ..
इतस्ततोऽभिधावंतं गवां संघातमध्यगम् .. 6.259.40 ..
5.258.m: resembling the sun in radiance, renowned by the name Nīla, / running here and there, standing in the midst of a multitude of cows:

5.258.s:
naṃdā sumanasā caiva surūpā ca suśīlakā ..
kāminī naṃdinī caiva medhyā caiva hiraṇyadā .. 41 ..
5.258.d:
नंदा सुमनसा चैव सुरूपा च सुशीलका ..
कामिनी नंदिनी चैव मेध्या चैव हिरण्यदा .. 41 ..
5.258.m: Nandā, Sumanasā, Surūpā, Suśīlakā, / Kāminī, Nandinī, Medhyā, Hiraṇyadā,

5.258.s:
dhanadā dharmadā caiva narmadā sakalapriyā ..
vāmanālaṃbikā kṛṣṇā dīrghaśṛṃgā supicchikā .. 42 ..
5.258.d:
धनदा धर्मदा चैव नर्मदा सकलप्रिया ..
वामनालंबिका कृष्णा दीर्घशृंगा सुपिच्छिका .. 42 ..
5.258.m: Dhanadā, Dharmadā, Narmadā dear to all, / Vāmanālambikā, Kṛṣṇā, Dīrghaśṛṅgā, Supicchikā,

5.258.s:
tārā tareyikā śāṃtā durviṣahyā manoramā ..
sunāsā dīrghanāsā ca gaurā gauramukhīha yā .. 43 ..
5.258.d:
तारा तरेयिका शांता दुर्विषह्या मनोरमा ..
सुनासा दीर्घनासा च गौरा गौरमुखीह या .. 43 ..
5.258.m: Tārā, Tāreyikā, Śāntā, Durviṣahyā, Manoramā, / Sunāsā, Dīrghanāsā, and Gaurā, Gauramukhī here,

5.258.s:
haridravarṇā nīlā ca śaṃkhinī paṃcavarṇakā ..
vinatābhinatācaiva bhinnavarṇā supatrikā .. 44 ..
5.258.d:
हरिद्रवर्णा नीला च शंखिनी पंचवर्णका ..
विनताभिनताचैव भिन्नवर्णा सुपत्रिका .. 44 ..
5.258.m: Haridravarṇā, Nīlā, Śaṅkhinī, Pañcavarṇakā, / Vinatā, Abhinatā, Bhinnavarṇā, Supatrikā,

5.258.s:
jayā'ruṇā ca kuṇḍodhnī sudatī cārucaṃpakā ..
etāsāṃ madhyagaṃ nīlaṃ dṛṣṭvā tā munidevatāḥ ..45..
5.258.d:
जयाऽरुणा च कुण्डोध्नी सुदती चारुचंपका ..
एतासां मध्यगं नीलं दृष्ट्वा ता मुनिदेवताः ..45..
5.258.m: Jayā, Aruṇā, Kuṇḍodhnī, Sudatī, and Cārucampakā. / Seeing Nīla standing in the midst of these [cows], those sages and gods,

5.258.s:
vicaraṃti surūpaṃ taṃ saṃjātavismayonmukhāḥ ..
munīśvarāḥ kṛpāviṣṭā indrādyā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ ..
stutimārebhire karttuṃ tejasā tasya toṣitāḥ .. 46 .. ..
5.258.d:
विचरंति सुरूपं तं संजातविस्मयोन्मुखाः ..
मुनीश्वराः कृपाविष्टा इन्द्राद्या हृष्टमानसाः ..
स्तुतिमारेभिरे कर्त्तुं तेजसा तस्य तोषिताः .. 46 .. ..
5.258.m: their faces uplifted in wonder that had arisen, moved about him of handsome form. / Filled with compassion, their minds delighted, the lords of sages and Indra and the other gods, / pleased by his splendor, began to sing praises.

5.258.s:
.. śūdra uvāca .. ..
kathaṃ nīleti nāmāsau jātoyamadbhutākṛtiḥ ..
kimastuvanprasannāste brāhmaṇā viśvakāraṇam .. 47 ..
5.258.d:
.. शूद्र उवाच .. ..
कथं नीलेति नामासौ जातोयमद्भुताकृतिः ..
किमस्तुवन्प्रसन्नास्ते ब्राह्मणा विश्वकारणम् .. 47 ..
5.258.m: The Śūdra said: / How did he come to have the name Nīla, he of wondrous form? / What did those pleased brahmins praise to the cause of the universe?

5.258.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
lohito yastu varṇena mukhe pucche ca pāṃḍuraḥ .. 48 ..
5.258.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
लोहितो यस्तु वर्णेन मुखे पुच्छे च पांडुरः .. 48 ..
5.258.m: Gālava said: / He who is red in color, but pale white on the face and tail—

5.258.s:
śvetaḥ khuraviṣāṇeṣu sa nīlo vṛṣabhaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
catuṣpādo dharmarūpo nīla lohitacihnakaḥ .. 49 ..
5.258.d:
श्वेतः खुरविषाणेषु स नीलो वृषभः स्मृतः ..
चतुष्पादो धर्मरूपो नील लोहितचिह्नकः .. 49 ..
5.258.m: [and] white on the hooves and horns, is regarded as a blue bull (nīlavṛṣabha), / four-footed, the embodiment of dharma, bearing blue and red marks.

5.258.s:
kapilaḥ khuracihneṣu sa nīlo vṛṣabhaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
yo'sau maheśvaro devo vṛṣaścāpi sa eva hi .. 6.259.50 ..
5.258.d:
कपिलः खुरचिह्नेषु स नीलो वृषभः स्मृतः ..
योऽसौ महेश्वरो देवो वृषश्चापि स एव हि .. 6.259.50 ..
5.258.m: One brown at the marks of the hooves is [also] regarded as a blue bull. / For he who is the god Maheśvara is indeed this very bull.

5.258.s:
catuṣpādo dharmarūpo nīlaḥ paṃcamukho haraḥ ..
yasya saṃdarśanādeva vājapeyaphalaṃ labhet .. 51 ..
5.258.d:
चतुष्पादो धर्मरूपो नीलः पंचमुखो हरः ..
यस्य संदर्शनादेव वाजपेयफलं लभेत् .. 51 ..
5.258.m: Four-footed, the embodiment of dharma, blue, five-faced Hara— / merely by seeing him one obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice.

5.258.s:
nīle ca pūjite yasminpūjitaṃ sakalaṃ jagat ..
snigdhagrāsapradānena jagadāpyāyitaṃ bhavet .. 52 ..
5.258.d:
नीले च पूजिते यस्मिन्पूजितं सकलं जगत् ..
स्निग्धग्रासप्रदानेन जगदाप्यायितं भवेत् .. 52 ..
5.258.m: And when the blue [bull] is worshipped, the entire universe is worshipped; / by giving [him] an unctuous morsel, the universe becomes gratified.

5.258.s:
yasya dehe sadā śrīmānviśvavyāpī janārdanaḥ ..
nityamarcayate yo'sau vedamantraiḥ sanātanaiḥ .. 53 ..
5.258.d:
यस्य देहे सदा श्रीमान्विश्वव्यापी जनार्दनः ..
नित्यमर्चयते योऽसौ वेदमन्त्रैः सनातनैः .. 53 ..
5.258.m: In whose body the glorious, all-pervading Janārdana ever [resides], / whom he constantly worships with the eternal Vedic mantras.

5.258.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
tvaṃ devaḥ sarvagoptṝṇāṃ viśvagoptā sanātanaḥ ..
vighnahartā jñānadaśca dharmarūpaśca mokṣadaḥ ..54..
5.258.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
त्वं देवः सर्वगोप्तॄणां विश्वगोप्ता सनातनः ..
विघ्नहर्ता ज्ञानदश्च धर्मरूपश्च मोक्षदः ..54..
5.258.m: The seers said: / "You are the god of all protectors, the eternal protector of the universe, / the remover of obstacles, the giver of knowledge, the embodiment of dharma, and the grantor of liberation.

5.258.s:
tvameva dhanadaḥ śrīdaḥ sarvavyādhiniṣūdanaḥ ..
jagatāṃ śarmakaraṇe pravṛttaḥ kanakapradaḥ .. 55 ..
5.258.d:
त्वमेव धनदः श्रीदः सर्वव्याधिनिषूदनः ..
जगतां शर्मकरणे प्रवृत्तः कनकप्रदः .. 55 ..
5.258.m: You alone are the giver of wealth, the giver of prosperity, the destroyer of all afflictions, / dedicated to the welfare of the worlds, the bestower of gold.

5.258.s:
tejasāṃ dhāma sarveṣāṃ saurabheya mahābala ..
śṛṃgāgre dhṛtakailāsaḥ pārvatīsahitastvayā .. 56 ..
5.258.d:
तेजसां धाम सर्वेषां सौरभेय महाबल ..
शृंगाग्रे धृतकैलासः पार्वतीसहितस्त्वया .. 56 ..
5.258.m: Abode of all splendours, son of Surabhī, of great strength! / Kailāsa, together with Pārvatī, is borne by you on the tip of your horn.

5.258.s:
33 stutyo vedamayo vedātmā vedavittamaḥ ..
vedavedyo vedayāno vedarūpo guṇākaraḥ .. 57 ..
5.258.d:
33 स्तुत्यो वेदमयो वेदात्मा वेदवित्तमः ..
वेदवेद्यो वेदयानो वेदरूपो गुणाकरः .. 57 ..
5.258.m: [You are] worthy of praise, composed of the Veda, the self of the Veda, the best knower of the Veda, / knowable through the Veda, having the Veda as your conveyance, having the form of the Veda, a mine of virtues.

5.258.s:
guṇatrayebhyo'pi paro yāthātmyaṃ veda kastava ..
vṛṣastvaṃ bhagavāndeva yastubhyaṃ kurute tvagham .. 58 ..
5.258.d:
गुणत्रयेभ्योऽपि परो याथात्म्यं वेद कस्तव ..
वृषस्त्वं भगवान्देव यस्तुभ्यं कुरुते त्वघम् .. 58 ..
5.258.m: Beyond even the three guṇas, who knows your true nature? / You are the bull, the Lord God; whoever commits a sin against you,

5.258.s:
vṛṣalaḥ sa tu vijñeyo rauravādiṣu pacyate ..
yadā spṛṣṭaḥ sa tu naro narakādiṣu yātanāḥ .. 59 ..
5.258.d:
वृषलः स तु विज्ञेयो रौरवादिषु पच्यते ..
यदा स्पृष्टः स तु नरो नरकादिषु यातनाः .. 59 ..
5.258.m: is to be known as an outcast (vṛṣala) and is cooked in Raurava and other hells. / If that man is touched [by you], the torments in hell and elsewhere,

5.258.s:
sevate pāpanicayairnigāḍhaprāyabandhanaiḥ ..
kṣutkṣāmaṃ ca tṛṣākrāṃtaṃ mahābhārasamanvitam .. 6.259.60 ..
5.258.d:
सेवते पापनिचयैर्निगाढप्रायबन्धनैः ..
क्षुत्क्षामं च तृषाक्रांतं महाभारसमन्वितम् .. 6.259.60 ..
5.258.m: he experiences with heaps of sins through very tight bonds. / And those who, without pity, emaciate [him] when exhausted by hunger, overcome with thirst,

5.258.s:
nirdayā ye praśoṣyaṃti matisteṣāṃ na śāśvatī ..
caturbhiḥ sahitaṃ martyā vivāhavidhinā tu ye .. 61 ..
5.258.d:
निर्दया ये प्रशोष्यंति मतिस्तेषां न शाश्वती ..
चतुर्भिः सहितं मर्त्या विवाहविधिना तु ये .. 61 ..
5.258.m: and laden with a heavy burden—their intellect is not enduring. / Those mortals who, according to the rite of marriage, [perform]

5.258.s:
vivāhaṃ nīlarūpasya ye kariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ ..
pitṝnuddiśya teṣāṃ vai kule naivāsti nārakī .. .. 62 ..
5.258.d:
विवाहं नीलरूपस्य ये करिष्यंति मानवाः ..
पितॄनुद्दिश्य तेषां वै कुले नैवास्ति नारकी .. .. 62 ..
5.258.m: the marriage of the blue-formed [bull] along with four [heifers], / intended for their ancestors, in their family there is never any dweller in hell.

5.258.s:
tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvalokānāṃ tvapitā parameśvaraḥ ..
tvayā vinā jagatsarvaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati .. 63 ..
5.258.d:
त्वं गतिः सर्वलोकानां त्वपिता परमेश्वरः ..
त्वया विना जगत्सर्वं तत्क्षणादेव नश्यति .. 63 ..
5.258.m: You are the refuge of all the worlds, and the father, the Supreme Lord; / without you, the entire universe would perish at that very moment.

5.258.s:
parā caiva tu paśyaṃtī madhyamā vaikharī tathā ..
caturvidhānāṃ vacasāmīśvaraṃ tvāṃ vidurbudhāḥ .. 64 ..
5.258.d:
परा चैव तु पश्यंती मध्यमा वैखरी तथा ..
चतुर्विधानां वचसामीश्वरं त्वां विदुर्बुधाः .. 64 ..
5.258.m: The wise know you to be the Lord of the four kinds of speech: / Parā, Paśyantī, Madhyamā, and Vaikharī.

5.258.s:
catuḥśṛṃgaṃ catuṣpādaṃ dviśīrṣasaptahastakam ..
tridhā baddhaṃ dharmamayaṃ tvāmeva vṛṣabhaṃ viduḥ .. 65 ..
5.258.d:
चतुःशृंगं चतुष्पादं द्विशीर्षसप्तहस्तकम् ..
त्रिधा बद्धं धर्ममयं त्वामेव वृषभं विदुः .. 65 ..
5.258.m: Four horns, four feet, two heads, and seven hands, / bound threefold, full of dharma—thus indeed they know you, the bull.

5.258.s:
tṛptidaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viśvavyāpakamojasā ..
brahma dharmamayaṃ nityaṃ tvāmātmānaṃ vidurjanāḥ .. 66 ..
5.258.d:
तृप्तिदं सर्वभूतानां विश्वव्यापकमोजसा ..
ब्रह्म धर्ममयं नित्यं त्वामात्मानं विदुर्जनाः .. 66 ..
5.258.m: Giving satisfaction to all beings, pervading the universe with energy, / people know you to be Brahman, eternal, full of dharma, the Self.

5.258.s:
acchedyastvamabhedyastvamaprameyomahā yaśāḥ ..
aśocyastvamadāhyo'si viduḥ paurāṇikā janāḥ .. 67 ..
5.258.d:
अच्छेद्यस्त्वमभेद्यस्त्वमप्रमेयोमहा यशाः ..
अशोच्यस्त्वमदाह्योऽसि विदुः पौराणिका जनाः .. 67 ..
5.258.m: You cannot be cut, you cannot be pierced, you are immeasurable, of great renown, / you are beyond sorrow, you cannot be burned—so know the people versed in the Purāṇas.

5.258.s:
tvadādhāramidaṃ sarvaṃ tvadādhāramidaṃ jagat ..
tvadādhārāśca devāśca tvadādhāraṃ tathā mṛtam .. 68 ..
5.258.d:
त्वदाधारमिदं सर्वं त्वदाधारमिदं जगत् ..
त्वदाधाराश्च देवाश्च त्वदाधारं तथा मृतम् .. 68 ..
5.258.m: Everything has you as its support; this world has you as its support; / the gods have you as their support, and likewise the departed [spirits] have you as their support.

5.258.s:
jīvarūpeṇa lokāṃstrīnvyāpya tiṣṭhasi nityadā ..
evaṃ sa saṃstuto nīlo vipraistaiḥ somapāyibhiḥ .. 69 ..
5.258.d:
जीवरूपेण लोकांस्त्रीन्व्याप्य तिष्ठसि नित्यदा ..
एवं स संस्तुतो नीलो विप्रैस्तैः सोमपायिभिः .. 69 ..
5.258.m: Pervading the three worlds in the form of the individual soul, you remain eternally." / Thus praised, that blue [bull] by those soma-drinking brahmins,

5.258.s:
prasannavadano bhūtvā viprā npraṇatitatparaḥ ..
punareva vacaḥ procurviprāḥ kṛtaśivāgasaḥ .. 6.259.70 ..
5.258.d:
प्रसन्नवदनो भूत्वा विप्रा न्प्रणतितत्परः ..
पुनरेव वचः प्रोचुर्विप्राः कृतशिवागसः .. 6.259.70 ..
5.258.m: becoming pleasant-faced, devoted to bowing down to the brahmins— / the brahmins, who had committed an offense against Śiva, spoke these words again.

5.258.s:
varaṃ dadurmaheśasya nīlarūpasya dharmataḥ ..
ekādaśāhe pretasya yasya notsṛjyate vṛṣaḥ .. 71 ..
5.258.d:
वरं ददुर्महेशस्य नीलरूपस्य धर्मतः ..
एकादशाहे प्रेतस्य यस्य नोत्सृज्यते वृषः .. 71 ..
5.258.m: They gave a boon to the Great Lord in the form of the blue bull, in accordance with dharma: / "For whichever deceased person a bull is not released on the eleventh day,

5.258.s:
pretatvaṃ susthiraṃ tasya dattaiḥ śrāddhaśatairapi ..
punareva susarpaṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā nīlaṃ mahāvṛṣam .. 72 ..
5.258.d:
प्रेतत्वं सुस्थिरं तस्य दत्तैः श्राद्धशतैरपि ..
पुनरेव सुसर्पंतं दृष्ट्वा नीलं महावृषम् .. 72 ..
5.258.m: his state as a ghost remains completely fixed, even with hundreds of śrāddhas offered." / Then, seeing the great blue bull creeping forward again,

5.258.s:
svalpakrodhasamāviṣṭaṃ dvijāścakrustamaṃ kitam ..
cakraṃ ca vāmabhāgeṣu śūlaṃ pārśve ca dakṣiṇe .. 73 ..
5.258.d:
स्वल्पक्रोधसमाविष्टं द्विजाश्चक्रुस्तमं कितम् ..
चक्रं च वामभागेषु शूलं पार्श्वे च दक्षिणे .. 73 ..
5.258.m: filled with a slight anger, the twice-born branded him: / a discus on the left flanks and a trident on the right flank.

5.258.s:
utsasṛjurgavāṃ madhye taṃ devairgopitaṃ tadā ..
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve maharṣīṇāṃ gaṇāḥ punaḥ ..
svāni sthānāni te jagmurmunayo vītamatsarāḥ .. 74 ..
5.258.d:
उत्ससृजुर्गवां मध्ये तं देवैर्गोपितं तदा ..
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे महर्षीणां गणाः पुनः ..
स्वानि स्थानानि ते जग्मुर्मुनयो वीतमत्सराः .. 74 ..
5.258.m: They released him among the cows, who was then hidden by the gods. / Then all the hosts of gods, and likewise the hosts of great seers, / the sages free from jealousy, went to their own abodes.

5.258.s:
evamṛṣīṇāṃ dayitāsu saktaḥ kāmārttacitto munipuṃgavānām ..
śāpaṃ samāsādya śivo'pi bhaktyā revājale'gātsuśilāmayatvam .. 79 ..
5.258.d:
एवमृषीणां दयितासु सक्तः कामार्त्तचित्तो मुनिपुंगवानाम् ..
शापं समासाद्य शिवोऽपि भक्त्या रेवाजलेऽगात्सुशिलामयत्वम् .. 79 ..
5.258.m: Thus attached to the wives of the seers, his mind afflicted by desire, / even Śiva, having incurred a curse, through devotion became pure stone in the water of the Revā.

5.258.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇaekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetra māhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye paijavanopākhyāne vṛṣastutirnāmaikonaṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamoadhyāyaḥ .. 259 .. [. cha ..
5.258.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराणएकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्र माहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्याने वृषस्तुतिर्नामैकोनषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोअध्यायः .. 259 .. [. छ ..
5.258.m: Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-ninth chapter, entitled "Praise of the Bull", in the story of Paijavana, in the praise of the Cāturmāsya, in the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada, in the story of the one who reclines on Śeṣa, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses, the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

5.259.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
iti te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ śālagrāmakathānakam ..
maheśvarasya cotpattiryathā liṃgatvamāpa saḥ .. 1 ..
5.259.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
इति ते कथितं सर्वं शालग्रामकथानकम् ..
महेश्वरस्य चोत्पत्तिर्यथा लिंगत्वमाप सः .. 1 ..
5.259.m: Gālava said: / "Thus has the whole narrative of the Śālagrāma been told to you, / and the origin of Maheśvara, how he attained the state of a liṅga.

5.259.s:
tasmādvaraṃ liṃgarūpaṃ śālagrāmagataṃ harim ..
ye'rcayaṃti narā bhaktyā na teṣāṃ duḥkhayātanāḥ .. 2 ..
5.259.d:
तस्माद्वरं लिंगरूपं शालग्रामगतं हरिम् ..
येऽर्चयंति नरा भक्त्या न तेषां दुःखयातनाः .. 2 ..
5.259.m: Therefore, the supreme form of the liṅga, and Hari residing in the Śālagrāma— / those men who worship [them] with devotion suffer no torments of pain.

5.259.s:
cāturmāsye samāyāte viśeṣātpūjayecca tau ..
arcitau yāvabhedena svargamokṣapradāyakau .. 3 ..
5.259.d:
चातुर्मास्ये समायाते विशेषात्पूजयेच्च तौ ..
अर्चितौ यावभेदेन स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदायकौ .. 3 ..
5.259.m: When the Cāturmāsya arrives, one should worship the two of them especially; / worshipped without distinction, they bestow heaven and liberation.

5.259.s:
devau hariharau bhaktyā vipravahnigavāṃ gatau ..
ye'rcayaṃti mahāśūdra teṣāṃ mokṣapradohariḥ .. .. 4 ..
5.259.d:
देवौ हरिहरौ भक्त्या विप्रवह्निगवां गतौ ..
येऽर्चयंति महाशूद्र तेषां मोक्षप्रदोहरिः .. .. 4 ..
5.259.m: The two gods, Hari and Hara, present in brahmins, fire, and cows, / those who worship with devotion, O noble Śūdra, to them Hari grants liberation.

5.259.s:
vedoktaṃ kārayetkarma pūrteṣṭaṃ vedatatparaḥ ..
paṃcāyatanapūjā ca satyavādo hyalolatā .. 5 ..
5.259.d:
वेदोक्तं कारयेत्कर्म पूर्तेष्टं वेदतत्परः ..
पंचायतनपूजा च सत्यवादो ह्यलोलता .. 5 ..
5.259.m: Devoted to the Veda, one should perform the rites enjoined by the Veda, both sacrificial and charitable; / and the worship of the five deities (pañcāyatana), truthfulness, and lack of fickleness—

5.259.s:
vivekādiguṇairyuktaḥ sa śūdro yāti sadgatim..
brahmacaryaṃ tapo nānyaddvādaśākṣaraciṃtanāt 1. 6 ..
5.259.d:
विवेकादिगुणैर्युक्तः स शूद्रो याति सद्गतिम्..
ब्रह्मचर्यं तपो नान्यद्द्वादशाक्षरचिंतनात् 1. 6 ..
5.259.m: endowed with virtues such as discernment, that Śūdra attains the good path. / There is no celibacy or austerity other than contemplating the twelve-syllable mantra.

5.259.s:
mantrairvinā ṣoḍaśa sopacāraiḥ kāryā supūjā narakādihaṃtuḥ ..
yathā tathā vai girijāpateśca kāryā mahā śūdra mahāghahaṃtrī .. 7 ..
5.259.d:
मन्त्रैर्विना षोडश सोपचारैः कार्या सुपूजा नरकादिहंतुः ..
यथा तथा वै गिरिजापतेश्च कार्या महा शूद्र महाघहंत्री .. 7 ..
5.259.m: Without mantras, an excellent worship of the slayer of hell and other [evils] should be performed with the sixteen offerings; / and in like manner [worship] of the lord of the mountain's daughter should be performed, O noble Śūdra, which destroys great sins."

5.259.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
evaṃ kathayatoreṣā rajanī kṣayamāyayau ..
sacchūdro gālavaścaiva śiṣyaiśca parivāritaḥ .. 8 ..
5.259.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
एवं कथयतोरेषा रजनी क्षयमाययौ ..
सच्छूद्रो गालवश्चैव शिष्यैश्च परिवारितः .. 8 ..
5.259.m: Brahmā said: / "As the good Śūdra and Gālava, surrounded by his disciples, / were conversing in this manner, that night came to an end.

5.259.s: sa tena pūjito vipro yayau śīghraṃ nijāśramam .. 9 ..
5.259.d: स तेन पूजितो विप्रो ययौ शीघ्रं निजाश्रमम् .. 9 ..
5.259.m: Worshipped by him, that brahmin went swiftly to his own hermitage.

5.259.s:
ya imaṃ śruṇuyānmartyo vācayetpāṭhayecca vā ..
ślokaṃ vā sarvamapi ca tasya puṇyakṣayo na hi .. 6.260.10 ..
5.259.d:
य इमं श्रुणुयान्मर्त्यो वाचयेत्पाठयेच्च वा ..
श्लोकं वा सर्वमपि च तस्य पुण्यक्षयो न हि .. 6.260.10 ..
5.259.m: The mortal who hears this, reads it, or causes it to be read, / even a verse or the whole of it, has no loss of religious merit."

5.259.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsya māhātmye paijavanopākhyāne ṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 260 ..
5.259.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्य माहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्याने षष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 260 ..
5.259.m: Thus ends the two hundred and sixtieth chapter in the story of Paijavana, in the praise of the Cāturmāsya, in the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada, in the story of the one who reclines on Śeṣa, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses, the glorious Skandapurāṇa.
